* README.md: Document them.

Add pre-command hook to clear overlay for specific commands

* copilot.el (copilot-clear-overlay-on-commands): New user option.
(copilot--pre-command): New function that clears the overlay before
commands occurring in the above user option.
(copilot--mode-setup): Add 'copilot--pre-command' to
'pre-command-hook'.
(copilot--mode-teardown): Remove 'copilot--pre-command' from
'pre-command-hook'.

Fix checkdoc and indentation lint warnings

- Quote `copilot-mode' and `track-changes' symbols in docstrings
- Add missing punctuation in easy-menu-define docstring
- Fix f-join argument indentation in copilot-server-executable

Add linting CI job

Add a lint job that runs checkdoc, declare, and indent linters via
Eask on ubuntu-latest with Emacs 30.1. Also rename the "test" job
to "compile" and fix the trigger branch (master -> main).

Replace f dependency with compat

Use file-name-concat (provided by compat for Emacs < 28.1)
instead of f-join, eliminating the f package dependency.
Sync Eask version and summary with package header

Set up buttercup test infrastructure

Add buttercup as a dev dependency, create initial test file, and add
a test job to the CI workflow.

Add test for events-buffer-scrollback-size fallback

The code already handles the deprecation of :events-buffer-scrollback-size
by using condition-case to try :events-buffer-config first and falling
back on invalid-slot-name error (copilot.el:471-475).

Closes #329

Add test confirming copilot loads without company-mode

The company dependency was removed previously. This test verifies that
copilot.el loads successfully without requiring company-mode.

Closes #243

Don't warn about copilot-max-char in non-file buffers

Temporary and non-file-visiting buffers (e.g. *scratch*, magit buffers)
should not trigger the max-char warning since they are not user-edited
source files.

Closes #313

Add comprehensive tests for core functionality

Cover utility functions (copilot--mode-symbol, copilot--string-common-prefix,
copilot--get-uri, copilot--get-relative-path, copilot--get-language-id,
copilot--infer-indentation-offset), source retrieval and truncation,
overlay management, minor mode setup/teardown, trigger predicates,
doc generation, LSP position calculation, and copilot-balancer functions
(extract-pairs, trim-closing-pairs, collapse-matching-pairs, fix-completion).
Add CHANGELOG.md with all changes since v0.3.0

Use tab-width as fallback indentation offset

Replace standard-indent with tab-width in copilot--infer-indentation-offset.
This provides a more sensible default for modes not in copilot-indentation-alist,
especially tab-oriented modes like go-mode where tab-width is typically 4 or 8.

Closes #312

Set priority on copilot completion overlay

Add priority 100 to the main display overlay to avoid conflicts with
Emacs 30's completion-preview-mode, which also uses overlays with
after-string in the same region. The keymap overlay already had
priority 101.

Closes #377

Filter out minibuffers and internal buffers in global-copilot-mode

Skip enabling copilot-mode in minibuffers and hidden internal buffers
(those with names starting with a space) when using global-copilot-mode.
This prevents excessive overhead from track-changes registration and
window-change hooks in buffers where completions are not useful.

Closes #337

Don't start the server in copilot--on-doc-close when connection is dead

Guard the didClose notification with copilot--connection-alivep and use
jsonrpc-notify directly instead of the copilot--notify macro, which
unconditionally starts the server. This prevents errors when killing
buffers (especially TRAMP buffers) after the server has exited.

Fixes #265

Add completion model selection (#382)

Add `copilot-completion-model` defcustom and `copilot-select-completion-model`
interactive command for choosing the AI model used for code completions.

Migrate from legacy getCompletions to textDocument/inlineCompletion

Replace the proprietary getCompletions/getCompletionsCycling API with
the standard LSP textDocument/inlineCompletion API (LSP 3.18) for
compatibility with newer Copilot language server versions.

Key changes:
- Use textDocument/inlineCompletion instead of getCompletions
- Send textDocument/didShowCompletion notification instead of notifyShown
- Accept via workspace/executeCommand instead of notifyAccepted
- Add partial acceptance telemetry via didPartiallyAcceptCompletion
- Remove notifyRejected (no equivalent in new API)
- Simplify cycling to use cached items from initial response
- Add client-side staleness tracking in copilot-complete
- Add manual integration test in dev/test-integration.el

Fix keyword symbols in didFocus and didOpen notifications

Leading colons on ':textDocument/didFocus and ':textDocument/didOpen
made jsonrpc-notify serialize them as ":textDocument/didFocus" etc.,
which the server does not recognize.  All other notifications already
use plain symbols.

Remove :dummy placeholder parameters from JSON-RPC requests

jsonrpc-request handles nil params correctly (omits the field),
which is valid JSON-RPC 2.0.  The dummy plists were unnecessary.

Fix PanelSolution handler to not activate the mark

call-interactively on mark-whole-buffer activates the mark and
interferes with user state.  org-sort-entries does not need an active
region when called non-interactively; goto-char to point-min suffices.

Send didChangeConfiguration instead of restarting on settings change

copilot--lsp-settings-changed now sends a workspace/didChangeConfiguration
notification (as copilot-select-completion-model already does) instead of
restarting the entire server, guarded by copilot--connection-alivep.

Send workspace folders during LSP initialization

- Add copilot--workspace-root to detect project root via project.el,
  projectile, or vc-root-dir (also fixes boundp -> fboundp for vc-root-dir)
- Add copilot--path-to-uri helper and refactor copilot--get-uri to use it
- Refactor copilot--get-relative-path to use copilot--workspace-root
- Send rootUri and workspaceFolders in the initialize request
- Dynamically notify the server via workspace/didChangeWorkspaceFolders
  when a new project root is encountered in copilot--on-doc-focus
- Reset copilot--workspace-folders in copilot-diagnose

Fix copilot--lsp-pos to use UTF-16 code unit offsets

LSP requires character positions in UTF-16 code units, but Emacs was
sending codepoint counts.  Characters above U+FFFF (e.g. emoji) are 2
UTF-16 code units but 1 Emacs character, causing off-by-one errors.

Add copilot--utf16-offset, copilot--utf16-strlen, and
copilot--goto-utf16-offset helpers and update copilot--lsp-pos,
copilot--show-completion, and copilot--lsp-range-end-from-oldtext.
Update CHANGELOG for workspace folders, UTF-16, and quick fixes

Rename test-integration.el to avoid buttercup auto-discovery

Buttercup recursively picks up any file starting with "test-".
Rename to integration-test.el so it is no longer loaded during
eask test buttercup runs.

Rename integration-test.el to integration-smoke.el

Buttercup also matches files ending with -test.el, so the previous
rename was not sufficient.

Rewrite README for clarity and accuracy

Restructure sections (quick start, installation-first, collapsed
Doom/Spacemacs), fix stale dependency list, add missing commands,
use keymap-set, fix typos and grammar, update copyright year.

Add cycling/dismiss keybindings and Fish-style alternative to README

Expand Quick Start and Keybindings examples with M-n/M-p for cycling
completions. Add a Fish-style keybinding section that avoids TAB
conflicts with company/corfu. Separate zap remaps under their own
heading.

Ref #103

Add clean LSP shutdown for Copilot server

Send shutdown request + exit notification before killing the server
process, matching the standard LSP shutdown sequence. This lets the
server flush telemetry, release resources, and exit gracefully.

Also register copilot--shutdown-server on kill-emacs-hook so Emacs
exits don't leave the server orphaned.

Handle didChangeStatus server notification in mode-line

The Copilot LSP server sends didChangeStatus notifications to report
its operational state. Reflect this in a dynamic mode-line lighter so
users can see errors, warnings, and busy status at a glance.

Handle window/showMessageRequest and window/showDocument server requests

These are standard LSP methods where the server asks the client to show
a message with action buttons or open a document/URL. The request handler
infrastructure was already in place but had no built-in handlers registered.
Handle $/progress notifications for progress reporting in mode-line

Send $/cancelRequest for stale in-flight completion requests

When the user types, each keystroke fires a new textDocument/inlineCompletion
request but the previous one was never cancelled -- the server kept working on
it even though the result would be discarded. Now copilot--async-request returns
the request ID, and copilot--get-completion cancels any in-flight request before
sending a new one. copilot-clear-overlay also cancels to avoid wasted work when
the user explicitly dismisses the completion.
Document protocol improvements in CHANGELOG and add protocol coverage table to README

[Fix #440] Rewrite copilot-balancer using parse-partial-sexp

The hand-rolled pair tracker counted delimiters inside comments and
strings, producing wrong results.  Replace ~300 lines of custom logic
with Emacs's built-in parse-partial-sexp + matching-paren, which
handles comments, strings, and escapes correctly via syntax tables.
Add CONTRIBUTING.md
Add test for balancer with redundant closers in suffix

Add copilot-enable-parentheses-balancer option

Allow users to disable the Lisp parentheses balancer by setting
copilot-enable-parentheses-balancer to nil. This is useful as an
escape hatch if the balancer causes issues, or to test raw Copilot
completions as the server's Lisp support improves.

Move copilot-enable-parentheses-balancer defcustom to copilot.el

All user-facing defcustoms live in copilot.el; the balancer module
just forward-declares the variable.

[Fix #448] Update tail-length after partial accept with replacement range

When the server returns a completion with a replacement range (start != end),
accept-by-word would delete the range but only insert the first word. The
stale tail-length caused copilot--overlay-end to compute wrong values on
subsequent accepts. Recalculate tail-length from the current buffer state
before setting the overlay text for the remaining completion.

[Fix #448] Preserve replacement range during partial accept-by-word

The previous fix (a62c1a5) only addressed stale tail-length, but the
real problem was that delete-region removed the entire replacement range
while only inserting the first word. Skip delete-region for partial
accepts so the range text stays in the buffer, covered by the overlay.
On subsequent accepts the overlay tracks the correct start/end to
eventually replace the range text.

[Fix #445] Send empty object instead of omitting params in JSON-RPC requests

When copilot--request receives nil params, jsonrpc-request omits the
params field entirely. The Copilot language server rejects this with
"Expected object" schema validation error, breaking login and other
no-argument RPCs.

Fix by having copilot--request substitute nil params with an empty
hash table, which serializes to {} in JSON.

[Fix #449] Preserve comment/string closers when server uses a replacement range

The balancer's parse-partial-sexp approach correctly ignores parens
inside comments and strings for balancing, but when the server's
replacement range covers a closer inside such a context, that closer
was silently dropped. Detect this case via syntax-ppss and re-append
the replaced closers.

Update CHANGELOG with recent bug fixes and new option

Add entries for the balancer rewrite (#440), comment/string closer
fix (#449), partial accept-by-word fix (#448), JSON-RPC empty params
fix (#445), and the new copilot-enable-parentheses-balancer option.
Add CI status badge to README

Trim CI matrix to remove redundant OS/version combinations

Byte-compilation runs on Linux only (platform-independent). Tests
run all Emacs versions on Linux for version coverage, with macOS and
Windows on latest stable only for OS-specific smoke testing. Cuts the
matrix from 21 jobs to 12.

[Fix #450] Send didOpen before completing when copilot-mode is off

copilot-complete was requesting completions without first notifying
the server about the current buffer.  This worked with copilot-mode
because the mode sends textDocument/didOpen on focus, but calling
copilot-complete standalone left the server unaware of the file.

Extract copilot--ensure-doc-open from copilot--on-doc-focus and
call it from copilot-complete so the document is always registered
before requesting completions.
Add FAQ section to README
Bump copyright years to 2026
Remove "unofficial" mentions from docs and code
Release 0.4.0

casos.name: v0.5.0
casos.body:
### New Features

- Add Copilot Chat support (`copilot-chat`, `copilot-chat-send`, `copilot-chat-send-region`, `copilot-chat-reset`) using the `conversation/*` LSP methods. ([#446](https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/pull/446))
- Add Next Edit Suggestions (`copilot-nes-mode`) via `textDocument/copilotInlineEdit`. NES predicts edits anywhere in the file based on recent editing patterns. ([#447](https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/pull/447))
- Add `copilot-chat-stop` command to cancel in-flight streaming.
- Show mode-line streaming status indicator for chat.
- Display follow-up suggestions after chat responses.
- Show errors inline in the chat buffer.
- Use `markdown-mode` GFM font-lock in the chat buffer when available.
- Add Chat, NES, Panel Complete, Clear Overlay, Select Completion Model, and Reinstall Server entries to the Copilot mode menu.
- Add GitHub issue templates for bug reports and feature requests.

### Changes

- Add a default error handler to `copilot--async-request` so async failures (e.g. cancelled completions) are logged to `*Messages*` instead of being silently swallowed.
- Remove unused `copilot-server-log-level` defcustom (dead code — nothing read it).
- Improve `copilot-log-max` docstring to explain the `*copilot events*` buffer.
- Convert `copilot--satisfy-predicates` from macro to function for simplicity.

### Bug Fixes

- Fix chat `conversation/create` sending `allSkills` as a string array instead of a boolean, which caused a schema validation error on `copilot-language-server` v1.436.0+. ([#452](https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/issues/452))
- Fix `copilot-complete` being immediately cancelled when called from wrapper commands (lambdas, user-defined functions) whose name doesn't start with `copilot-`. ([#453](https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/issues/453))
- Fix chat not displaying replies from newer server versions. ([#459](https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/issues/459))
- Fix `:json-false` treated as truthy for `external` in `window/showDocument` handler.
- Normalize `:json-false` busy flag in `didChangeStatus` handler. ([#457](https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/issues/457))
- Guard against `:json-null` in server responses.
- Clear `copilot--completion-initiated-p` flag in idle timer path to prevent stale state. ([#454](https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/issues/454))
- Suppress `copilot-max-char` warning when `copilot-max-char-warning-disable` is non-nil.
mensagens_commits:
Use copilot--handle-notification in progress handler tests

Calling (car handlers) directly is fragile when other packages
register additional handlers for the same notification method.

Add Copilot Next Edit Suggestions (NES) (#447)

* Add Copilot Next Edit Suggestions (NES) support

NES predicts edits the developer will want to make next, based on
recent edit history. Unlike inline completions, NES suggestions can
appear anywhere in the file and can replace or delete existing text.

The implementation uses the textDocument/copilotInlineEdit LSP method
and lives entirely in a new copilot-nes.el file with no changes to
copilot.el.

Closes #374

* Fix TAB binding and font-lock after accepting NES edits

- Bind both TAB (C-i) and <tab> (function key) so the accept
  binding works in GUI Emacs and modes like Python that intercept
  <tab> before function-key-map translates it.
- Remove inhibit-modification-hooks from the accept path — it was
  suppressing after-change-functions, which prevented font-lock from
  re-fontifying the inserted text.
- Only count actual point movements for auto-dismiss, not every
  post-command event.

* Fix NES rendering, add server version check and docs

- Change deletion face from `shadow` to `diff-removed` for visible
  red/pink highlighting with strikethrough instead of faint gray
- Add overlay priority 100 to match inline completion overlays
- Warn on activation when copilot-language-server < 1.434.0
- Extract copilot-nes--handle-response for testability
- Add NES section to README with usage, keybindings, customization
- Add NES entries to Commands and Protocol Support tables
- Add tests for response handling, version check, telemetry, and
  mode coexistence

Add Copilot Chat support (#446)

* Add Copilot Chat support via conversation/* LSP methods

Implement chat functionality using the conversation/* LSP protocol,
reusing the existing copilot.el connection and dispatcher infrastructure.

Closes #199

* Add Chat documentation to README

- Chat subsection under Configuration with usage, keybindings,
  and customization
- Chat commands in the Commands table
- conversation/* and conversation/context in Protocol Support tables
- Update "Do you want to chat" section to reflect built-in support
Add FUNDING.yml
Add sponsorship badge and support section to README
Update the maintainers list
Replace first-person prose with neutral language in README

Add design document and update README

Create doc/design.md covering the architecture, the rationale for using
jsonrpc directly instead of eglot/lsp-mode, document synchronization,
the completion pipeline, extensibility, and modularity of Chat and NES.

Update the README with a richer introduction, a History section
explaining how copilot.el was originally reverse-engineered from
copilot.vim before migrating to the official language server, and
various smaller improvements (rename "Server-side hooks" section,
move copilot-chat.el mention into the Chat section, remove the
now-redundant standalone chat section).

Fix chat schema validation error with allSkills (#452)

The server now expects allSkills to be a boolean, not a vector of skill
names. Send t instead of ["current-editor"] to fix the validation error
on copilot-language-server v1.436.0+.

Add tests for conversation/create params (allSkills type, model
inclusion/omission).

Add missing commands to the Copilot mode menu

Add Chat, NES, Panel Complete, Clear Overlay, Select Completion Model,
and Reinstall Server to the menu. Reorganize entries into logical
groups.

Update CHANGELOG with changes since v0.4.0

Add entries for Copilot Chat, Next Edit Suggestions, the allSkills
schema fix, and the mode menu additions.

Fix copilot-complete being cancelled when called from wrapper commands (#453)

copilot--post-command clears the overlay (and cancels in-flight requests)
for any command whose name doesn't start with "copilot-". This breaks
wrapper commands (anonymous lambdas, user-defined functions) that call
copilot-complete programmatically — the request is sent and then
immediately cancelled by the post-command hook.

Fix this by having copilot-complete set a buffer-local flag
(copilot--completion-initiated-p) that copilot--post-command checks and
resets. When the flag is set, the post-command hook skips clearing.
Add #453 fix to CHANGELOG

Log async request errors by default instead of swallowing them

copilot--async-request now injects a default :error-fn that logs
via copilot--log when callers don't provide one. This makes failures
like cancelled completions visible in *Messages* rather than silent.

Also removes the redundant :error-fn from getPanelCompletions (the
default does the same thing) and deletes the unused
copilot-server-log-level defcustom. Improves copilot-log-max
docstring to explain the *copilot events* buffer.
Update README and CHANGELOG for async error logging changes

Use copilot--log in PanelSolutionsDone handler

Raw `message` was inconsistent with the rest of the codebase.

Don't message when copilot-max-char-warning-disable is t

Previously the "disabled" path still called (message ...), which
defeated the purpose of the setting. Now it's truly silent.

Improve copilot-diagnose docstring

Explain what the command actually does and what to look for
in *Messages* afterward.

Add timeout handler to NES request

User-initiated NES requests silently timed out with no feedback.

Remove redundant error-fn from copilot-diagnose

The default handler already logs errors with the method name,
which is more informative than the old "%S" format.

Fix copilot-chat--create tests failing without a server

copilot--connection-alivep is a defsubst that gets inlined when
byte-compiled, so spying on it has no effect. Mock the underlying
pieces (copilot--connection, jsonrpc--process, process-exit-status)
instead, matching the pattern used in copilot--on-doc-close tests.

Replace defsubst with defun for testability

copilot--connection-alivep, copilot--log, and copilot--overlay-visible
were all defsubst, which gets inlined when byte-compiled. This made
copilot--connection-alivep impossible to spy on in tests for
byte-compiled code, forcing workarounds that mocked jsonrpc internals.

Now that they're regular defun, tests can simply spy on
copilot--connection-alivep directly. This also eliminates the
"defsubst used before defined" compiler warning.

[Fix #454] Clear completion-initiated flag in idle timer path

copilot-complete sets copilot--completion-initiated-p so that
post-command-hook won't immediately cancel a request initiated by a
wrapper command. However, when copilot-complete is called from the idle
timer (copilot--post-command-debounce), no post-command-hook runs
afterward, so the flag persists. The next keystroke then sees the stale
flag, skips overlay clearing, and the typed character gets hidden inside
the overlay — causing the cursor to visually jump.

Clear the flag right after copilot-complete in the debounce function.

Warn about copilot-chat.el package conflict in README

Closes #456

Extract copilot-chat--remove-active-tokens and remove dead boundp check

The boundp guard on copilot-chat--source-buffer is unnecessary since
the variable is always defined via defvar-local. Extract the
active-buffers cleanup into a reusable helper for DRY.

Display follow-up suggestions after chat responses

Show the server's follow-up suggestion (when present) at the end of
each streamed response, styled with copilot-chat-follow-up-face.

Show errors inline in chat buffer

Add copilot-chat--insert-error to display errors with a distinct face
instead of silently logging. Extract copilot-chat--end-streaming and
copilot-chat--handle-request-error to share error handling between
conversation/create and conversation/turn, fixing a missing
buffer-live-p check in the create error path.

Add mode-line streaming status indicator

Show "[Streaming]" in the mode-line while a response is being
received, using a dynamic :eval lighter on copilot-chat-mode.

Add copilot-chat-stop to cancel in-flight streaming

C-c C-k now cancels the current streaming response via $/cancelRequest
when streaming is active, or falls back to copilot-chat-reset when idle.
The request ID is tracked per-buffer for targeted cancellation.

Always pass workspaceFolders in conversation/create

The server uses workspace folders for context resolution. Send the
current project root so the server can locate relevant files.

Use markdown-mode GFM font-lock when available

Borrow gfm-mode's font-lock-defaults for full markdown rendering
(headings, code blocks, emphasis) when markdown-mode is installed.
Fall back to basic highlighting otherwise. Add q binding for
quit-window.
Note markdown-mode recommendation for chat in README

Update chat keybindings and commands in README

C-c C-k now runs copilot-chat-stop (cancel or reset), document the
new q binding, and add copilot-chat-stop to the commands table.

[Fix #457] Normalize :json-false busy flag in didChangeStatus

The LSP server sends busy: false which json.el decodes as :json-false,
a non-nil symbol. This caused the mode-line to always show "Copilot*".

Fix :json-false treated as truthy for external in showDocument

Same class of bug as #457: JSON false decodes to :json-false which
is non-nil in Elisp. Use (eq external t) to match only true.

Fix chat not displaying replies from newer server versions (#459)

The server changed the progress report format — reply text moved from a
flat :reply field to :editAgentRounds vector. Extract the reply from
whichever format is present so both old and new servers work.
Add GitHub issue templates for bug reports and feature requests

Guard against :json-null in server responses

JSON null decodes to :json-null which is truthy in Elisp. Add type
guards where server data is used in conditionals:

- copilot-chat--extract-reply: ensure reply is a string
- progress handler "end": ensure result is a list before plist-get
- window/showMessageRequest: ensure actions is a non-empty vector
- copilot-nes--handle-response: ensure edits is a sequence
- copilot--progress-lighter: use stringp/numberp for message/percentage

Cache indentation offset in copilot--generate-doc

Avoid calling copilot--infer-indentation-offset twice for :tabSize
and :indentSize when a single let binding suffices.

Convert copilot--satisfy-predicates from macro to function

A defun is simpler and easier to debug here; the macro provided no
compile-time benefit since the predicate lists are evaluated at runtime.
Release 0.5.0

casos.name: copilot.el v0.7.0
casos.body:
### New Features

Agent mode tooling:

- Add MCP (Model Context Protocol) server support for agent mode via the new `copilot-mcp-servers` option. Configured servers are forwarded to the language server and their tools become available in `copilot-chat`, each prompting for confirmation like the built-in tools.
- Add `copilot-chat-list-mcp-tools` to see the connected MCP servers, their status, and their tools, and warn when an MCP server fails to start (previously silent).
- Preview file changes in a temporary buffer before confirming an agent-mode edit tool (`create_file`, `insert_edit_into_file`, `replace_string_in_file`), so you can see what will be written before approving. Controlled by `copilot-chat-preview-tool-edits` (default on).
- Offer an `always` choice at agent-mode tool confirmation prompts, alongside yes and no, to approve a tool for the rest of the conversation instead of confirming each call. The choice is remembered until a new conversation starts.
- Run the agent-mode `run_in_terminal` tool asynchronously instead of blocking Emacs for the whole command. The editor stays responsive, the language-server connection keeps flowing, `C-g` aborts a running command, and `copilot-chat-terminal-timeout` (default 30s) kills runaways. The command's exit status is now reported back to the model.
- Show a status line in the chat buffer when Copilot runs one of its own built-in or MCP tools that asks for confirmation (`read_file`, the edit tools, etc.), so those tool calls leave a trace, not just the ones copilot.el executes locally.

Workspace access for agent mode:

- Answer the server's `workspace/findFiles` and `workspace/findTextInFiles` requests so agent mode can search the project by file glob and by text/regex (via ripgrep), a step toward whole-workspace questions.
- Answer the server's `workspace/readFile` and `workspace/readDirectory` requests so agent mode can read files and list directories across the project.
- Add opt-in semantic search (`copilot-chat-enable-semantic-search`): declare the `watchedFiles` capability and answer the server's `copilot/watchedFiles` request with the project's file list, so the server can build a workspace index for whole-codebase questions.

Chat usability:

- Add `copilot-chat-slash-command` (`C-c /`) to pick and send a chat slash command (`/explain`, `/fix`, `/tests`, `/doc`, etc.) fetched from the server, with optional arguments.
- Act on chat code blocks: `copilot-chat-insert-code-block` (`C-c C-i`) inserts the block at point into the source buffer, and `copilot-chat-copy-code-block` (`C-c M-w`) copies it to the kill ring, instead of leaving chat output as read-only text.
- Attach extra context to a chat message: `copilot-chat-add-file-reference` (`C-c C-f`) and `copilot-chat-add-region-reference` send specific files or selections along with the next message, and `copilot-chat-clear-references` drops anything pending.

Account and usage:

- Track Copilot usage quota: surface the server's quota warnings and add `copilot-quota` to show how much of your chat, completion, and premium-request allowance is left.
- Announce when a suggestion matches public code, and collect the matches (with licenses and reference URLs) in a buffer shown by `copilot-list-code-citations`. Controlled by `copilot-show-code-citations` (default on). ([#471](https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/issues/471))

### Changes

- Show readable agent-mode confirmation prompts for the server's own tools (`read_file`, `insert_edit_into_file`, `replace_string_in_file`, etc.) instead of a raw plist dump, falling back to the server-provided message, then the raw input, for any tool we don't recognize. `copilot-chat-auto-approve-tools` is matched exactly so it never auto-approves a same-named tool from a different namespace.

### Bug Fixes

- Fix agent-mode tool confirmations always failing (so Copilot Chat couldn't read files, edit, etc.) by returning the `(:result "accept")`/`(:result "dismiss")` shape the server expects instead of a bare string. ([#483](https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/issues/483))
- Resolve a concrete default chat model from the server when `copilot-chat-model` is nil (preferring the server's designated chat default, then an `auto` model) instead of leaving the model unset, which some servers answer with an empty reply. The lookup runs once per session, only against an already-running server. ([#473](https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/issues/473))
- Surface a turn-level error reported by the server at the end of a chat turn, instead of leaving only an empty reply. ([#473](https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/issues/473))
- Stop the `copilot--infer-indentation-offset` warning from firing while generating chat context, so chatting from a buffer whose mode has no configured indentation offset no longer nags. ([#473](https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/issues/473))
- Report Flycheck diagnostics for the agent-mode `get_errors` tool, not just Flymake, so Flycheck users get real diagnostics instead of "no diagnostics available".
mensagens_commits:
Fix agent-mode tool confirmations rejected by the server [Fix #483]

The confirmation handler returned a bare string ("Accept"/"Dismiss"),
but the language server validates the response against an object schema
{result: "accept"|"dismiss"}. The bare string failed validation, so the
server reported a ResponseError and treated every confirmation as a
non-acceptance -- Copilot Chat could never read files, edit, or run any
server-side tool that needs confirmation.

Return the (:result "accept")/(:result "dismiss") plist the server
expects instead.

Improve agent-mode tool confirmation prompts

Now that confirmations work, the most common agentic tools (read_file,
insert_edit_into_file, replace_string_in_file) are server built-ins that
fell through to a raw plist dump in the confirmation prompt. Add tailored
summaries for them. For any tool we don't recognize, fall back to the
human-readable message the server already sends, and only then to the
tool name plus its raw input, so the user can always see what they are
approving.

Server built-in tools can arrive namespaced (e.g. copilot.read_file), so
match the display summaries on the base name. Auto-approval, by contrast,
stays an exact match: it bypasses confirmation entirely (including the
server's sensitive-file prompts), so it must never approve a same-named
tool from a different namespace.

Resolve a default chat model when none is configured [#473]

When copilot-chat-model is nil we sent no model at all and relied on the
server to pick one, but some servers answer with an empty reply instead.
Resolve a concrete default from copilot/models (the server's designated
chat default, then an auto model, then the first chat model).

The lookup runs at most once per session and caches its result, nil
included, so a server with no usable default isn't re-queried on every
message. It only fires when the connection is already up, with a short
timeout, so chat never blocks on starting the server. Clearing the model
via copilot-chat-select-model forgets the cache so it re-resolves.

This addresses the default-model part of #473; the indentation warning
and follow-up-answer reports there are separate.

Preview file changes before confirming agent edit tools

When agent mode wants to write a file (create_file, insert_edit_into_file,
replace_string_in_file), show the proposed change in a temporary buffer
while prompting for confirmation, so the user can see what will be written
before approving. String replacements render as a colorized diff. Other
tools (terminal commands, reads, web fetches) keep the plain prompt.

Controlled by copilot-chat-preview-tool-edits, on by default.

Add MCP server support for agent mode

Let users expose Model Context Protocol servers to Copilot agent mode via
a new copilot-mcp-servers option. The map is serialized to JSON and sent
to the language server through the existing settings channel, so the
server's MCP tools become available in copilot-chat. Their invocations
flow through the same confirmation path as the built-in tools.

Changing the option through the customization framework pushes the new
configuration to a running server, matching copilot-lsp-settings.

Run agent-mode terminal commands asynchronously

run_in_terminal used shell-command-to-string, freezing Emacs for the
entire command with no way to cancel and no timeout, so a long build or
test would lock the editor. Drive the command with make-process and pump
events instead: redisplay and the language-server connection keep
working, C-g aborts, and copilot-chat-terminal-timeout kills runaways.

The command's exit status is now surfaced too. A non-zero exit is handed
back to the model as output with its code (the tool call still succeeded),
while timeouts and cancellations report error/cancelled.

Show server-side tool activity in the chat buffer

The server runs its own built-in and MCP tools internally, so until now
they left no trace in *copilot-chat* - only the four tools copilot.el
executes locally logged a status line. Log a status line when such a
tool is approved (the single choke point for every tool call, prompted
or auto-approved), skipping the client tools that already log their own
progress.

Add an 'always' choice to agent-mode tool confirmations

The confirmation prompt was a binary yes/no, so a safe tool had to be
re-approved on every call. Offer a third choice, always, that approves
the tool for the rest of the conversation: it is remembered in a
session-scoped set (matched by base name) that copilot-chat--create
clears when a new conversation begins. The persistent
copilot-chat-auto-approve-tools list keeps its exact-match semantics.

Surface MCP server and tool status

MCP servers were configured but invisible: there was no way to see which
ones connected or what tools they exposed, and a server that failed to
start did so silently. Handle the copilot/mcpTools notification to cache
the server snapshots, warn once when a server newly fails, and add
copilot-chat-list-mcp-tools to list servers, their status, and tools.

Surface turn errors and quiet the indent warning in chat [#473]

Two of the remaining complaints in #473. First, the server can report a
turn-level error in the end progress result; the handler only read the
follow-up from there, so an errored turn showed nothing but an empty
reply. Surface that error in the chat buffer. Second, generating chat
context ran copilot--infer-indentation-offset, which warns when the
source buffer's mode has no configured offset; that debugging aid is
irrelevant to chat, so suppress it there.

Support Flycheck in the get_errors agent tool

get_errors only read Flymake diagnostics, so Flycheck users got
"no diagnostics available" for every file. Collect from whichever
backends are active - Flymake, Flycheck, or both - and only report no
backend when neither is on.

Track and surface Copilot usage quota

The server reports usage via copilot/quotaChange and copilot/quotaWarning
notifications, which we previously ignored. Cache the quota snapshot,
surface the server's warning messages, and add a copilot-quota command
that shows how much of the chat, completion, and premium-request
allowance remains. Useful now that premium models draw on a quota.

Surface public code citations [Fix #471]

GitHub Copilot can detect when a suggestion closely matches public code;
the server only emitted these as log lines. Declare the ipCodeCitation
capability and handle the copilot/ipCodeCitation notification: announce
the match in the echo area and collect each match, with its licenses and
reference URLs, in a *copilot-code-references* buffer reachable via
copilot-list-code-citations. Controlled by copilot-show-code-citations.

Insert and copy chat code blocks

Chat output was read-only text, so applying a suggested snippet meant
retyping it. Parse the fenced code blocks in the chat buffer and add two
commands: copilot-chat-insert-code-block (C-c C-i) inserts the block at
point into the originating source buffer, and copilot-chat-copy-code-block
(C-c M-w) copies it to the kill ring. When point is not inside a block,
both prompt for which block to use.

Add chat slash commands

Slash commands (/explain, /fix, /tests, /doc, ...) are a staple of the
VS Code chat but were unavailable here. Fetch the server's templates via
conversation/templates, filtered to the scope for the current mode, and
add copilot-chat-slash-command (C-c /) to pick one and send it (with
optional arguments) as a /<id> message.

Attach files and selections as chat context

Chat could only ever send the originating buffer as context. Add a
pending-references list and commands to attach specific files
(copilot-chat-add-file-reference, C-c C-f) or the current selection
(copilot-chat-add-region-reference), sent as the turn's references and
cleared only once a message is actually delivered, so a failed request
does not lose the attachment. Attaching context creates the chat buffer
when none exists, and copilot-chat-clear-references drops what is pending.

Add workspace file and text search for agent mode

The server drives codebase search by sending the editor workspace/findFiles
and workspace/findTextInFiles requests; we ignored them, so agent mode
could not search the project. Answer both via ripgrep (which honors
.gitignore): findFiles globs file paths, findTextInFiles does literal or
regex text search and returns {uri, lineNumber, lineText} matches. Both
run through an event-pumped subprocess so Emacs stays responsive, and
pass an explicit search path so ripgrep never blocks reading stdin.

Refactors the terminal tool's process runner into a reusable
copilot-chat--run-argv that takes an argv directly.

Add workspace file and directory read for agent mode

Round out the agent content provider: answer the server's
workspace/readFile and workspace/readDirectory requests so it can read
file contents (bounded by a max-bytes cap) and list directory entries
(with VS Code file-type integers) across the project, not just search.

Add opt-in workspace semantic search

Enable embeddings-based whole-codebase search. When
copilot-chat-enable-semantic-search is on, declare the watchedFiles
capability so the server turns on semantic search, and answer its
copilot/watchedFiles request with the project's file list (enumerated
with ripgrep, honoring .gitignore) - the source the server indexes.

Off by default since indexing computes embeddings server-side; takes
effect on the next server start. Incremental re-indexing on file change
(didChangeWatchedFiles) is left for a follow-up; the initial index is
built from the file list.

Tidy changelog and fill README gaps for the week's work

Consolidate the duplicated Bug Fixes section in the unreleased changelog
into a single New Features / Changes / Bug Fixes layout, and document the
two options that were missing from the README (copilot-chat-terminal-timeout
and copilot-show-code-citations, with a short public-code-references note).

Group the unreleased changelog by theme for release

Reorder the unreleased entries into thematic clusters (agent-mode
tooling, workspace access, chat usability, account and usage) with short
group labels, and order the bug fixes from most foundational outward, so
the release notes read as a narrative rather than merge order.
Release 0.7.0

casos.name: copilot.el v0.8.0
casos.body:
## What's Changed
* Use "references" consistently for public-code matches by @bbatsov in https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/pull/505
* Clarify the issue-reference commit convention by @bbatsov in https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/pull/506
* Make user-facing messages and chat context wording consistent by @bbatsov in https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/pull/507
* Send the chat model on every conversation turn by @bbatsov in https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/pull/510
* Warn when agent mode uses a model that can't call tools by @bbatsov in https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/pull/512
* Show a status header line in the chat buffer by @bbatsov in https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/pull/515
* Add one-shot chat task commands by @bbatsov in https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/pull/514
* Add commit message generation from the staged diff by @bbatsov in https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/pull/513
* Add a transient menu for the most common commands by @bbatsov in https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/pull/516
* Add opt-in chat session persistence by @bbatsov in https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/pull/517
* Document the server's custom instruction files by @bbatsov in https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/pull/518
* Surface cloud coding agent messages by @bbatsov in https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/pull/519
* Add a region rewrite command with diff preview by @bbatsov in https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/pull/520
* Add native Copilot Code Review commands by @bbatsov in https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/pull/521
* Add chat presets by @bbatsov in https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/pull/522
* Let users edit a tool's input before it runs by @bbatsov in https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/pull/523
* Notify when a long chat turn finishes by @bbatsov in https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/pull/524
* Let users pick the chat mode, including InlineAgent by @bbatsov in https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/pull/525
* Add an Org frontend for the chat buffer by @bbatsov in https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/pull/526


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/copilot-emacs/copilot.el/compare/v0.7.0...v0.8.0
mensagens_commits:
Use "references" consistently for public-code matches

The feature mixed "citations" and "references": copilot-show-code-citations
and copilot-list-code-citations versus the *copilot-code-references* buffer.
GitHub calls these matches "code references" (its "find matching code"
feature), so standardize on that: the option and command become
copilot-show-code-references and copilot-list-code-references, with obsolete
aliases for the names that shipped in 0.7.0.

Also clarify in the README that these are GitHub's public-code references and
have nothing to do with Emacs xref.

Clarify the issue-reference commit convention

Spell out that ticket references go as a prefix in the commit subject,
and distinguish [#N] (related issue) from [Fix #N] (fully closes it).

Make user-facing messages and chat context wording consistent

Two terminology cleanups:

- Prefix user-facing messages and interactive errors with a component tag
  (Copilot: for the core, Copilot Chat: for chat), matching the install and
  quota messages that already did. Raw error faults and internal guards are
  left unprefixed.
- Describe chat-attached context as "context" throughout the user-facing
  wording, instead of bouncing between "context" and "reference". The
  copilot-chat-add-file-reference command family keeps its names, which mirror
  the server's `references` field.

[Fix #508] Send the chat model on every conversation turn

Only conversation/create carried the model; follow-up
conversation/turn requests omitted it. Older servers remembered
the model across the conversation, but recent language-server
versions resolve it per turn and reject turns without one with
"A model id is required".

Send the model on every turn through a shared helper, using the
modern modelInfo.id field and keeping the deprecated model field
as a fallback for older servers.

[#509] Warn when agent mode uses a model that can't call tools

Agent mode only works with a tool-capable model. When the resolved model
can't call tools, Copilot just describes the commands to run instead of
running them, which reads as agent mode being broken (see discussion
#509).

Detect this at conversation creation via the model's
capabilities.supports.tool_calls flag and warn, pointing the user at
copilot-chat-select-model. The check is best-effort: it stays silent
when tool support can't be determined and never blocks starting a chat.
Also document the requirement in the README.

Show a status header line in the chat buffer

The header shows whether Agent or Ask mode is active, which model
answers, and in agent mode how many tools are available, so it's no
longer guesswork whether agent mode is actually on (see discussion
#509). Disable it with copilot-chat-show-status-header.

Polish the status header after review

Memoize the client-tool count so the header allocates nothing per
redisplay, inherit only shadow in the header face (inheriting
header-line too would paint active colors into inactive windows once
Emacs 31 splits the faces), exercise the :eval element in the tests,
and document that the toggle applies to new chat buffers.

Add one-shot chat task commands

copilot-chat-review, copilot-chat-fix, copilot-chat-doc,
copilot-chat-optimize, and copilot-chat-write-tests send the region (or
the defun at point) to the chat with a canned prompt, so common asks
don't require composing a message. copilot-chat-task picks a task with
completion and the prompts live in copilot-chat-task-prompts.

Harden the task commands after review

Gate the defun-at-point fallback on prog-mode so markdown sections and
parenthesized prose fragments are never sent as code, reject empty
interactive task input, and offer only symbol keys for completion.

Add commit message generation from the staged diff

copilot-chat-insert-commit-message sends the staged diff to Copilot in a
throwaway conversation and inserts the reply at point, so it works from
a Magit commit buffer without opening (or disturbing) the chat panel.
The instruction is customizable via copilot-chat-commit-message-prompt.

Harden the one-shot machinery after review

Run git via process-file in default-directory so TRAMP buffers diff the
remote repository and linked worktrees resolve their own index instead
of the main checkout's. Unregister a function sink before invoking its
callback so a signaling callback can't leak the entry, register the
sink only after the request was issued (and skip it when the error
handler already fired), and guard against double callbacks. Teach
copilot-chat-stop to cancel a pending one-shot instead of resetting the
chat conversation, copy the reply to the kill ring when the target
buffer is read-only, strip four-backtick fences, and render request
errors through copilot-chat--error-text. The staged-diff tests now run
real git in temp repositories instead of stubbing out the code under
test.

Add a transient menu for the most common commands

M-x copilot-menu collects completions, chat, agent mode, account, and
server management commands in one magit-style menu, with the current
state (copilot-mode, agent mode, chat model) shown inline.

transient is a soft dependency: current releases require Emacs 28.1,
where it's bundled anyway, so making it a hard dependency would break
the package's Emacs 27.2 floor. The menu definition is stored as data
and evaluated only when transient loads; without it copilot-menu
signals a clear user-error and everything else works as usual.

Polish the menu after review

Use function symbols for the dynamic descriptions, retry loading
transient from the fallback command so installing it mid-session works,
and assert the exact suffix count in the layout test so a walker gap
can't silently drop commands from the check.

Add opt-in chat session persistence

Record completed chat turns and, when copilot-chat-save-history is
enabled, save the transcript after each turn to a per-workspace file
under copilot-chat-history-directory. copilot-chat-restore renders the
saved conversation and replays its turns on the next conversation/create
so the server picks up the full context; copilot-chat-clear-history
deletes the saved file.

Harden session persistence after review

Guard copilot-chat against sending while a turn is in flight, so
interleaved turns can't pair one request with another's response in
the session log (or lose an answer outright); the same guard protects
copilot-chat-restore. Strip text properties from history read off
disk, so a tampered or synced file can't inject keymap/display/
read-only properties into the chat buffer. Pin the history root on
the session the first time it's resolved, so saving and restoring can
never target two different files. Skip recording errored or empty
turns, clear capture state on request errors and cancellation, only
let a create response clear the exact restored turns it sent, and
write history files chmod 600 in a chmod 700 directory.

Document the server's custom instruction files

The language server reads .github/copilot-instructions.md, AGENTS.md
(including nested ones), CLAUDE.md, scoped .instructions.md files, and
.github/git-commit-instructions.md on its own; nothing was documented
about this on our side. Explain what's picked up and how to turn it
off via copilot-lsp-settings.

Handle the copilot/codingAgentMessage request

The server sends this when a chat conversation is delegated to GitHub's
cloud coding agent and it opens a pull request to continue the work in.
Previously the request was silently dropped as an unhandled method; now
the update is echoed and logged, with the PR link, to the
*copilot-coding-agent* buffer.

Preserve point in the coding agent log after review

save-excursion around the append, matching the other log buffers, plus
specs for the missing-title fallback, percent signs in titles, and
point preservation.

Add copilot-chat-rewrite

Rewrite the active region per a free-form instruction: the proposed
change is previewed as a diff and applied only after confirmation,
with the region tracked via markers so unrelated edits made while the
request is in flight don't shift the target. Runs through the one-shot
chat machinery, so it stays out of the chat panel and a pending
rewrite is cancellable with copilot-chat-stop.

Harden the rewrite flow after review

Re-check the region after the confirmation prompt (y-or-n-p blocks
while timers and process filters run, so auto-revert can swap the
buffer contents mid-prompt), widen before comparing and applying so
narrowing can't signal in the process filter, salvage to the kill ring
when read-only text properties make delete-region signal, clear the
markers in an unwind-protect, refuse an empty region, and size the
request fence past any backtick run in the region.

Add native Copilot Code Review commands

The language server exposes GitHub's code review service directly via
the copilot/codeReview/reviewChanges and reviewSnippets requests, which
return structured comments (file, line, message, suggested change)
instead of a streamed chat reply.

copilot-chat-review-changes sends the uncommitted diff (staged and
unstaged, against HEAD) and copilot-chat-review-region sends the
selection widened to whole lines.  Both render the comments in the chat
buffer without consuming a chat turn, so they never disturb an ongoing
conversation.  Binary and oversized files are skipped, and the server's
error is surfaced when the account has no Code Review access.

Harden the native review flow after review

Give the review request a 130s timeout with a visible timeout handler
(jsonrpc's 10s default silently dropped any review that took longer,
which is most of them), skip directory entries like dirty submodules
when collecting changes, pass --no-relative so diff.relative can't
break path resolution from a subdirectory, detect a repository with no
commits, refuse to interleave with a streaming chat answer, size
suggestion fences past embedded backtick runs, and send absolute line
numbers from narrowed buffers.

Add copilot-chat-presets for switching between chat setups

Named bundles of chat settings (model, agent mode, auto-approved
tools) that copilot-chat-apply-preset switches between in one step.
A preset only touches the keys it lists; the model and agent mode
take effect on the next new conversation.

Correct the preset docs and validate auto-approve-tools after review

The model is sent on every turn (since #508), so a preset's model
takes effect on the next message even in a live conversation, not only
on a new one; only agent mode is pinned at conversation create. Fix
the docstring, README, and CHANGELOG to say so, and reject a non-list
:auto-approve-tools before applying anything instead of half-applying
and then erroring.

Let users edit a client tool's input before it runs

At the agent-mode confirmation prompt, the tools copilot.el runs itself now
offer an "edit" choice alongside yes/no/always: the shell command of
run_in_terminal, the content of create_file (in a temporary buffer), or the
URLs of fetch_web_page. The tool then runs once with the edited input.

The server reads only the accept/dismiss result at confirmation time and
sends the input in a separate invocation request, so the edit is stashed at
confirmation and consumed at invocation, matched by the toolCallId both
requests carry. Server-executed and MCP tools are unchanged, since the
server never reads a modified input back.

Decline cleanly when a tool edit is cancelled

Cancelling the edit (C-c C-k or C-g) raises quit, which the jsonrpc
dispatcher does not turn into a reply, so the server would wait forever
for the confirmation result. Catch it in the confirmation handler and
dismiss the tool call instead. Adds specs for the cancel path and for
editing a fetch_web_page URL list.

Notify when a Copilot Chat turn finishes and you looked away

Raise a desktop notification at the end of a streamed chat turn, but
only when it ran at least copilot-chat-notify-after-seconds and the
chat buffer is not the one in the selected window, so you get pinged
when a long answer finishes while you're doing something else and
never when you're already watching it stream.

The backend prefers D-Bus, falls back to osascript on macOS and to
message elsewhere, and is overridable via copilot-chat-notify-function.
A failing backend is logged and swallowed so it can't disrupt the turn.

Make the notification backend cascade after review

Route each notification backend to the next on failure instead of
picking one by capability: a dbus-enabled Emacs with no session bus
would take the D-Bus branch, fail at call time, and never reach the
osascript fallback it was written for. Also escape newlines in the
AppleScript quoter so a multi-line body can't break the literal, clear
the turn start time on cancel/error/reset, and read the selected
window's buffer directly for the focus check.

Let users pick the chat mode, including InlineAgent

Add copilot-chat-select-mode to choose among the modes the server
reports via conversation/modes (Ask, Agent, InlineAgent, plus any
custom project modes) instead of only the agent on/off toggle. The
selection is stored in copilot-chat--mode and sent as chatMode (with
customChatModeId for non-built-in modes) when a conversation is
created; without a selection the existing copilot-chat-use-agent-mode
boolean still decides between Agent and Ask.

Both Agent and InlineAgent are agent-kind modes, so a new
copilot-chat--agent-mode-p predicate now gates tool registration, the
tool-call confirmation, the tool-support warning, and the agent-panel
template scope in place of the raw boolean. The status header shows the
effective mode name and keeps the tool count for any agent-kind mode.

Polish chat mode selection after review

The menu's agent-mode toggle now clears an explicit mode selection, so
it isn't a no-op when a mode is active; the status header falls back to
the mode kind when a custom mode has no name; and a custom Ask-kind
mode is covered by a test.

Add copilot-chat-frontend to render the chat as Org

Let org users set `copilot-chat-frontend' to `org' so the *copilot-chat*
buffer is rendered as Org rather than GitHub-flavored Markdown. The
markdown frontend stays the default and is unchanged: same You:/Copilot:
scaffolding and the same GFM font-lock borrow.

The org frontend writes each exchange as a `* You' heading with a nested
`** Copilot' heading, borrows Org font-lock the same way markdown borrows
GFM (copying font-lock-defaults from a temp org-mode buffer), and turns
on outline-minor-mode so turns fold. The buffer stays special-mode
derived in both frontends, so the keymap and read-only handling are
intact, and the streamed assistant body is left exactly as the server
sends it, so code-block commands keep working.

The frontend is read at buffer setup, so it applies to new chat buffers.

Make the org frontend actually highlight Org markup

Borrowing font-lock-defaults from a temp org buffer copied only the
globally nil org-font-lock-keywords symbol, so the org frontend
rendered as unhighlighted plain text. Populate Org's keywords in the
chat buffer with org-set-font-lock-defaults (which needs org-element)
instead, so headings, emphasis, and code get real Org faces. This also
drops the temp-buffer org-mode call and its org-mode-hook side effects.
Add a test that asserts a face is actually applied, which the earlier
setup-only test missed.
Release 0.8.0

casos.body:
Release notes:

- https://crate.io/docs/crate/reference/en/6.0/appendices/release-notes/6.0.4.html

Download on:

- https://crate.io/download
mensagens_commits: Bump version to 6.0.0-SNAPSHOT

Create RoutineInfos on-demand in InformationSchemaIterables

It was created on each cluster state update but that's not really
necessary.
It can be created once and use the latest metadata state whenever it is
used.
Allow dynamic addition of nested array columns
Update maven plugins to their latest version
Remove unused code from NotPredicate

Use shard created version in ColumnFieldVisitor

Storage formats are per-partition, so we need to ensure we use the
correct version when loading data.  Currently the version is only
used for reading streamed data from stored fields, and we have no
data types that have a versioned streamer, so there are no data
issues with using the table version.  However, this may change in
future.
Generate Lucene queries for AllEqOperator

Fix NPE in StoredRowLookup when _raw was requested before doc lookup

FullStoredRowLookup would set docVisited to true in an asRaw() call, but
would not actually parse the document, so subsequent calls to asMap()
would return null.  This reworks things so that docVisited is checked
and set entirely within loadStoredFields(), and asMap() instead checks
the value of parsedSource directly.
Add support for lowercase patterns to the to_char scalar function

Update netty to 4.1.117

https://netty.io/news/2025/01/14/4-1-117-Final.html
Bump bundled JDK to 23.0.2

Fix issue when binding the same values to PK lookup

When querying by PK (also when additionally using _seq_no and
_primary_term), and bound parameters are used, then since the
WHERE clause optimization takes place before binding values to the
params, a query like: `SELECT * FROM tbl WHERE pkCol = ? OR pkCol = ?`
will result in 2 DocKey entries, since at that point we don't know the
actual values which will be bound, and therefore normalize and eliminate
duplicates. As a consequence, and since PkAndVersion objects were
returned in a `List`, if duplicate values are bound, the `PKLookupPhase`
will fetch duplicate records.

Use `LinkedHashSet` (to keep also the order of the values) instead of
`List` to eliminate `PkAndVersion` resuling duplicates after query
parameters are bound (in `Get#build()`).

Fixes: #17266

Fix issue when binding the same values to PK lookup

When querying by PK (also when additionally using _seq_no and
_primary_term), and bound parameters are used, then since the
WHERE clause optimization takes place before binding values to the
params, a query like: `SELECT * FROM tbl WHERE pkCol = ? OR pkCol = ?`
will result in 2 DocKey entries, since at that point we don't know the
actual values which will be bound, and therefore normalize and eliminate
duplicates. As a consequence, and since PkAndVersion objects were
returned in a `List`, if duplicate values are bound, the `PKLookupPhase`
will fetch duplicate records.

Use `LinkedHashSet` (to keep also the order of the values) instead of
`List` to eliminate `PkAndVersion` resuling duplicates after query
parameters are bound (in `Get#build()`).

Fixes: #17266

Fix handling of unallocated shards during number_of_shards resize

The resize operation didn't check if the shards are acknowledged before
triggering the "swap and drop" operation. This led to data loss if the
shards of the resized index weren't allocated.

Solution:

- Add a check if the resize was acknowledged (plus shards acknowledged)
- Add a sanity check in the drop+swap operation that the source has all
  primaries allocated
- Remove the ChainableAction mechanism, because none of the operations
  had a undo action
- Filter away `.resized` indices when retrieving the index names for a
  table. These shouldn't be included on a `select * from tbl` and would
  lead to `IndexName.decode` errors

Closes https://github.com/crate/crate/issues/17278

Allow precision=scale in NumericType; Fix avg aggregation errors

During an `avg` operation it can happen that we get a `BigDecimal` value
with scale==precision.

This caused streaming to fail because it creates a `NumericType` derived
from the `BigDecimal` value and `NumericType` so far enforced that
`scale > precision`.

This relaxes the restriction.
Closes https://github.com/crate/crate/issues/17271
CI: Use `uv` on RTD
CI: Use `uv` on GHA
Chore: Fix broken link error for https://dev.mysql.com

Add SchemaMetadata and RelationMetadata for blobs

This doesn't do much yet except introduce some components which will be
required for:

- https://github.com/crate/crate/pull/16964
- https://github.com/crate/crate/issues/11939

Change some IndexNameExpressionResolver to use metadata.getIndices

Should help migrating away from named indices to RelationMetadata / uuid
based resolving
Resolve BlobTableInfo via RelationMetadata
Migrate more IndexNameExpressionResolver to metadata.getIndices

Fixes a handshake issue between different major versions

To support rolling upgrades between different major versions
which in general can have a different `minimumCompatibilityVersion`
(lower compatibility bound), the handshake logic must also take
the version into account (upper compatibility bound).

Additionally, this changes the channel version responded as
the agreed-on-version to be the maximum version both versions
are supporting instead of always using the defined lower bound.
Use metadata.getIndices in TransportDropTableAction

Use metadata.getIndices in TransportRenameTableAction

Preparation for https://github.com/crate/crate/pull/17127
Use metadata.getIndices in TransportResizeAction
Use metadata.getIndices in more places in TransportCloseTable
Use metadata.getIndices in OpenTableClusterStateTaskExecutor

Remove v/5.6 from mergify backport rules

5.6 is EOL and doesn't receive bugfixes anymore, even if they are
severe.
Fix fetch outputs resolution in the Fetch operator

Suppress missing key errors when accessing child of an object literal from aliased table

Regression from `5.10` caused by https://github.com/crate/crate/pull/17052.
The root cause is the object literals returned from functions are missing
inner types. Adding a workaround so that such object literals' types would be
ObjectType.UNTYPED and catching them during subscript expression analysis
in order to fall back to subscript functions instead of searching inner types
for keys.

Adds details to the repository rate limiter settings

Documents how to disable thottling and that the recovery settings
are also related.

Fix link to HLL++ publication, use archive, original starts failing

Original link is redirected to a broken new google link from today
on. Use static archive link to fix this.

Fix BWC streaming of the Metadata

Follow up of https://github.com/crate/crate/commit/bb09dbc.
Reflect 5.7.6, 5.8.6, 5.9.9 releases

Fix persistence of metadata's schemas

The new schemas weren't taken into account when checking if the
global state changes. By this, schemas weren't persistet at all.

Follow up of https://github.com/crate/crate/commit/bb09dbc.

Upgrade to Lucene 10.1.0 (#17327)

User facing changes:
- Removal of `dutch_kp` and `lovins` stemmers - users will need to reindex with different stemmers before upgrade
- `german` and `german2` stemmers now both fold umlauts - users will need to reindex after upgrade

Add native access/vector flags to jvm settings in debug config

To avoid warnings from Lucene

Fix NPE in RETURN SUMMARY handling leading to stuck queries

Fixes a regression introduced with https://github.com/crate/crate/commit/c7fb24dd00e0f14c8a2ab6f9c99ef5c663e85e8b

The entries in the `failures` of `ShardResponse` can be `null` - that
led to a (uncaught) NPE within the `SummaryCollector`.

This also happened more often than it should have due to the failure
count in `errorCount >= BULK_RESPONSE_MAX_ERRORS_PER_SHARD ? null :
error` being based on the size of `failures` - and there being 1 entry
per bulk item.

Remove lock objects from UpsertResultCollectors

It looks like the intention is to protect against concurrent access to
the `UpsertResults` instances.

We can use these directly for synchronization. That avoids the `lock`
objects and has the advantage that it would also work if there were
different collector instances accessing the same `UpsertResult`
instances.

Fix SubQueryResults.merge(), result values of both sides must be used

When merging 2 SubQueryResults, the result values of both sides
must be taken into account and merged.

Fixes #17307.

Add storage compat change to release notes

That tables created in 4.x won't work is already mentioned in the
warning block further above, but having no mention of it in the breaking
changes sections seems strange.

Add BWC code to blob tables resoltion

Follow up to https://github.com/crate/crate/commit/bb09dbc18b915a7feaf5c85282334bdd89a32438 and https://github.com/crate/crate/commit/f0fdbbccd3fcc0f2b1dbba83fa49c4963af55b19

Fix BWC handling in MetadataDiff for schemas

`schemas` must be a `ImmutableMapDiff` instance. The
`apply(immutableMap)` call fails otherwise.

Fix issue with ScopedSymbol subscript and FetchRewrite

In `Eval.rewriteToFetch` when we have an output which is a
`ScopedSymbol` and is a child (subscript) of an output of the `source()`
plan of `Eval`, previously we failed to properly rewrite the
`ScopedSymbol` as a reference (subscript function) to the `FetchStub`
generated. e.g.:

```
-- tbl2#noRows > tbl1#noRows tables are switched in the join and Eval
-- is added on top of the HashJoin.

cr> EXPLAIN SELECT vw1.field2['arr']
    FROM (SELECT * FROM tbl1) as vw1
    INNER JOIN tbl2 on vw1.field1 = tbl2.field1
    LIMIT 10;
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| QUERY PLAN                                                            |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Fetch[field2['arr']] (rows=10)                                        |
|   └ Limit[10::bigint;0] (rows=10)                                     |
|     └ Eval[vw1._fetchid] (rows=1400)                                  |
|       └ HashJoin[INNER | (field1 = field1)] (rows=1400)               |
|         ├ Collect[doc.tbl2 | [field1] | true] (rows=210000)          |
|         └ Rename[vw1._fetchid, field1] AS vw1 (rows=150)              |
|           └ Collect[doc.tbl1 | [_fetchid, field1] | true] (rows=150) |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

To fix it, properly resolve the subscript `ScopedSymbol` as a reference
to the generated `FetchStub` in `MapBackedSymbolReplacer`.

Fixes: #17267

Deprecate usage of _version

Since` _version` has already been deprecated in docs
for optimistic concurrency control, which was the actual
purpose of the column, we deprecate its usage at any place
of a query, so that it can be removed completely in the future.

Treat geo distance_error_pct as double instead of float

Tiny subset of https://github.com/crate/crate/pull/17127
Switching from xcontent/mapping based cluster state serialization to
`GeoReference` `Writable` serialization would lead to precision errors
in tests due to double/float conversion.

Ensure tables are gone after wipeAllTables in tests

This helped spot some issues in https://github.com/crate/crate/pull/17127

Expose primary keys in CreateTableRequest as column ident list

Makes it easier to introduce `RelationMetadata.Table` where we won't
store primary keys as fully qualified name but use the column ident
directly.

Return existing SharedShardContext if a FetchTask tries to create a new one with same shardId/readerId

Co-authored-by: Mathias Fussenegger <f.mathias@zignar.net>

Fix transport handshake, handshake response sent wrong version

Fix the handshake response and outbound message handler to sent
the minimum compatible version in the handshake response header
to allow the handshake transport message decoding to work before
a possible higher version is used after the handshake.

Follow up of https://github.com/crate/crate/commit/1773a41.

Fix eval projection to support fewer outputs than its source

The Eval projection has a logic to add casts to its source outputs
to a given list of target types (its own outputs). This is e.g.
needed for Union's to ensure that all source outputs are cast to
the same type.
In some situtions the source can contain more symbols than the
given target types to cast to.

Closes #17341.

Use Join Relations to build JoinPlans

Explicit joins are now always created before implicit joins to ensure
to preserve the original join order of the query.

Flush instead of synced-flush inactive shards

With peer recovery retention leases and sequence-number based replica
allocation, a regular flush can speed up recovery as a synced-flush.
With this change, we will flush instead of synced-flush when a shard
becomes inactive.

ES backport of: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/commit/725dda37ea5

Tidy up Store#trimUnsafeCommits

This change removes unused parameters and simplifies the logic.

ES backport of: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/commit/65374c9c010

Add missing change entries for 5.9.10

from https://github.com/crate/crate/pull/17365/commits/f841d33e808cbde7859c28a4480d615808821bfd

and https://github.com/crate/crate/commit/5e1bc6c9d8ed874baa4fc99500561c4e94c37d9d

Fix MIN/MAX for NUMERIC values

Previously, there was no `NUMERIC` signature registered, and as a
result, the `NUMERIC` values where implicitly casted to `STRING`
leading to wrong results, as an alphanumeric ordering was used instead
of the numeric one.

Fixes: #17360

Use default min/max implementations for numeric

There's nothing special about numeric that requires dedicated instances.
The precision/scale returnType binding is correct without inferring it
from the argument.

All that's needed is the `compare` implementation on the `DataType`

Fix wrong join results for CASE in join condition

Previously, a query like the following:
```
SELECT * FROM t0
LEFT JOIN (SELECT 2 AS col2 FROM t0) AS sub0
ON CAST((CASE t0.c0 WHEN sub0.col2 THEN t0.c1 ELSE t0.c1 END )
```
would be wrongly executed with HashJoin instead of NL.
As a result, multiple rows could end up with the same hash value, but
some of them could evaluate to `true` and others to `false`, thus
right side NULLed rows wouldn't be emmitted.

some special cases like AND/OR/NOT operators and CAST) only if those
scalars are under a top level Equality operator (`=`).

Encapsulate dropped cols skipping for SourceParser in lookupName function

The `SourceParser` had a list of dropped columns and used this to check
if a column was dropped whenever it encounters a new field in the
source.

This worked so far because:

- Dropping columns is only allowed if there are OIDs
- Dropped columns had a `_dropped_` name prefix in the metadata mapping
  because the name of a column was used as key. This allowed to
  disambiguate between a dropped column, and a re-added column.

Concrete example:

      Initial state:
        Column: oid=1, name=x
      Drop x:
        Column: oid=1, name=_dropped_x
      Add x
        Column: oid=1, name=_dropped_x
        Column: oid=2, name=x

      sourceParser encounters oid=1 -> lookupName returns _dropped_x -> matches dropped columns
      sourceParser encounters oid=2 -> lookupName returns x -> doesn't match dropped columns

In https://github.com/crate/crate/pull/17127 columns can be stored as
`List<Reference>`, that means we no longer need to prefix columns with
`_dropped_`, but as a side effect of that, we'd have:

      Initial state:
        Column: oid=1, name=x
      Drop x:
        Column: oid=1, name=x
      Add x
        Column: oid=1, name=x
        Column: oid=2, name=x

      sourceParser encounters oid=1 -> lookupName returns x -> matches dropped columns
      sourceParser encounters oid=2 -> lookupName returns x -> matches dropped columns again !

To resolve this, this changes the lookup function to return `null` for
dropped columns.

ShingleTokenFilter can produce multiple tokens at each position of
differing lengths, which means downstream consumers that expect a
well-formed token graph, such as FixedShingleFilter or query parsers,
may produce nonsensical output. To prevent this, ShingleTokenFilter
will mark its TokenStream with a DisableGraphAttribute if it produces
output that cannot be coerced into a graph.

The concrete implementation class for this attribute was missing,
meaning that attempts to use a shingle filter with output_unigrams=true
or with differing min and max shingle sizes would cause errors on
ingest.

Remove GET threadpool in favour of SEARCH

GET was mostly used for sys.shards/sys.nodes with the intention of
having a separate queue/pool to ensure these queries get scheduled
independent of how occupied the SEARCH pool is.

The problem with that approach is that although they'll get scheduled
faster because of the separate queue, they compete for CPU time with
all the running SEARCH activities, including new arrivals.

This removes GET, with the intention to follow up integrating a
`PriorityQueue` so that system queries can skip ahead of the queue, and
then have to compete with fewer active tasks for CPU time.

Fix race causing context leak on node disconnects

Adds the node-ids for the upstreams information to `MergePhase` so that
each node can autonomously take care of the full task life-cycle and
abort tasks if there's a disconnect of an upstream node.

MergePhases are the only passive component driven by upstream activity,
and if a upstream dies it would wait forever for a result.

Before the `NodeDisconnectJobMonitorService` monitored for disconnects
and triggered a kill to account for that, but there is a suspected race
condition:

- Query gets planned and job requests are fired off
- Node dies
- NodeDisconnectJobMonitorService kicks in but there's no task yet so it
  doesn't do anything.
- Job request is processed and creates tasks, which will be stuck
  forever

The reworked logic also checks immediately after creating a task if all
participating nodes are still there and the `TasksService` itself also
listens to disconnects, replacing the `NodeDisconnectJobMonitorService`.

Fix issue with IP values normalization

When a `String` value is stored on a table `IP` column is
normalized in the `IpIndexer`, but this normalization was not
applied to the value when the `IP` column is part of the `PRIMARY KEY`
of the table and is encoded in the value stored as the `_id`.
As a result, a value `::ffff:192.168.0.1` would be stored as is in
the `_id` but would be stored as `192.168.0.1` (normalized) in the
actual column of the table, and therefore `Collect` queries would
yield different matching rows than `Get` queries since in one case
the normalized value would be used, and in the latter the un-normalized
value stored in `_id` would be used instead.

Always normalize the values in the `IpType#implicitCast()` method to
resolve this issue.

Fix issue with BOOLEAN in PARTITION BY

When a table was partitioned by and a `BOOLEAN` column was included in
the `PARTITIONED BY` clause, then the encoding to create the partition
ident, was different when creating the partition (used `"false"` and
`"true"`) than when trying to retrieve the partition when querying the
table (use `"t"` and `"f"`).

Fix the issue, by unifying the encoding, by always using the
`StringType#implicitCast` in all cases where such encoding takes place.

Expose indices with non-active primary shards in publications

Once an index is restored on the subscriber side, it must always
be included in the publication state response, otherwise it
will be treat as dropped, which in turn causes the tracking to
stop and turn the table into a normal writable one.
Such, the index must even be exposed when it has some non-active
primary shards.
But indices with non-active primary shards will fail on restoring,
so each index will contain a marker setting to express this.
This way, such an index will not be tried to restore, and
already subscriped tables will continue to be tracked (retry).
