Add tasks missing on kill to `recentlyFailed` cache

This speeds up query completion in the following distributed query
execution scenario:

- handler-node: mergeOnHandler starts
- handler-node: collect starts
- handler-node: collect finishes with a failure and:
  - forwards the failure to the participating downstreams
  - propagates the failure to sibling tasks to clean them up

- handler_node: Given that the local task failed, remote task
  initialization is skipped, instead it immediately sends out a kill to
  the other nodes

- remote node: kill received, but is a no-op, because context is missing
- remote node: receives the failure forwarded by the collect, but given
  that the task context is missing it retries.

To speed up the context cleanup in such a scenario, this changes the
TasksService to track the failed job within its `recentlyFailed` cache.

Fix: Don't register CURRENT_CATALOG also as a normal function with `()`

Fix request mutation interfering with primary operation retry logic

This is a follow up to https://github.com/crate/crate/pull/17973

Primary retries can happen in two places:

- Triggered from within the primary operation (e.g. shard not found, due
  to a race where it is being moved)
- Triggered due to the replica operation failing

Both scenarios were problematic with the mutations happening on the
primary request. Items could have had their seqNo changed to
SKIP_ON_REPLICA and insertColumns/insertItems could also change, making
a retry unsafe.

To solve this, this introduces a dedicated replica request which will
only contain items actually inserted on the primary. The original
request is no longer mutated to ensure it can be reused for a retry.

As a side effect of this change, it also fixes another issue where a
statement like:

    INSERT INTO tbl (id, value) VALUES (?, ?)
    ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value

With a table that has the columns:

- id
- value
- other
- rnd_col (being undeterministic generated using something like `random()`)

This could lead to serialization errors if used in a bulk operation where
some items ran into a conflict and others did not.
The update items had insertValues for `[id, value, other, rnd_col]`, while
the non-conflict items had insertValues for `[id, value, rnd_col]`, the
third position having a mix of string/int caused the streaming errors.

Fix flaky testPrimaryTermIsIncreasedOnReplicaPromotion

Test failed with seed `D9B7E91DF5B8C37A:524AE1236DE758B` because it can
happen that the first update completes after the disruption recovery.

The test scenario was like this:

- It simulates a network disruption
- Executes an update that runs into a client timeout because it targets
  the isolated node. On the server side the statement can continue with
  retries.
- Waits for the replica to be promoted to primary due to the disruption
- Executes two more updates against the master node. These succeed
  because they hits the working part of the network partition
- Disruption is stopped
- The first update could succeed with a retry, bumping the seqNo to 3
  instead of 2. Before https://github.com/crate/crate/pull/17973 this
  always failed due to a version conflict, but now it is using the
  unassigned seqNo/version for the primary retry and can succeed - which
  is allowed as long as the client receives the correct response in
  proper order.

To account for this case, this changes the test to execute the first
statement async and checks its completion state throughout.

Improve memory accounting in StreamBucket

RamAccounting used to rely on size() difference before and after write to compute ram usage of the added Row.

BytesStreamOutput has ramBytesUsed() method providing precise memory usage of the underlying ByteArray,
so switching to this method to make accounting more precise.

size() eventually catches up but there can be windows where it lags behind.
For example:
out.size(): 21, out.ramBytesUsed: 1080
out.size(): 42, out.ramBytesUsed: 1080
out.size(): 63, out.ramBytesUsed: 1080
out.size(): 84, out.ramBytesUsed: 1080
out.size(): 105, out.ramBytesUsed: 1080
…
out.size(): 987, out.ramBytesUsed: 1080
out.size(): 1008, out.ramBytesUsed: 1080
out.size(): 1029, out.ramBytesUsed: 1216
…
out.size(): 16401, out.ramBytesUsed: 32768
out.size(): 16422, out.ramBytesUsed: 32768

For big buffers this difeference can lead to a series of add(Row row) calls with a notable underaccouting
which can lead to OOM-s on nodes under high memory pressure.

Fix pgwire message ordering hiccups

The PostgreSQL wire protocol had the issue that the channel handler's
already processed the next incoming messages while outgoing messages
were still being computed asynchronously.

For example in:

    -> Parse
    <- ParseComplete
    -> Bind
    <- BindComplete
    -> Execute
    -> Parse
    <- ParseComplete*1
    <- CommandComplete*2 (referring to execute)

We used the `DelayableWriteChannel` to delay `ParseComplete*1`, to
ensure it would be sent _after_ `CommandComplete*2`

It was somewhat difficult to reason about its correctness given that
most of the `Session` is built under the assumption that there is only
one component at a time calling methods in a strictly sequential order,
not concurrently. (With the exception of cancellation)

This replaces the `DelayableWriteChannel` approach with explicit read
control. To simply no longer process new messages while an async
execution is in progress.

Revert "Fix pgwire message ordering hiccups"

This reverts commit aa029bff3f82f82b2df02d4b00ae6a917a4a6996.

The auto-read wasn't fully disabled because the `PgDecoder` could still
read multiple messages. There is an option to disable that
(`setSingleDecode` of `ByteToMessageDecoder`), but that doesn't work
either because of the following scenario covered by npgsql tests in
crate-qa:

    CrateContext.ConnectionString = conn.ConnectionString;
    using CrateContext context = new();
    for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++)
    {
        context.Test.Add(new TestEntity());
    }
    await context.SaveChangesAsync();

Causes a message flow like:

    -> Parse
    -> Bind
    -> Describe
    -> Execute

    -> Parse
    -> Bind
    -> Describe
    -> Execute

    -> Sync

Each `execute` doesn't actually start execution, but defers it to `sync`
for batch execution. The future returned by `session.execute()` which
 was used to trigger a manual `read` would never be called with
 singleDecode set because we'd never process the `sync` message.

Without `singleDecode`, the next messages are immediately processed and
we send messages, leading to `commandComplete` arriving out of order:

    sentParseComplete
    sentBindComplete
    sentNoData
    sentParseComplete
    sentBindComplete
    sentNoData
    sentCommandComplete
    sentCommandComplete

Conclusion:

We need to keep the delay mechanism

Fix hash join deadlock scenario

It could happen that a hash join got stuck when executing on more than
one node and if the number of rows within a page was smaller then the
expected block size despite having `allLoaded() = false`.

This happened if the page size didn't divide cleanly by the number
of nodes, resulting in one downstream receiving fewer rows.

One downstream would then move from the build phase to the probe phase,
and process the right side, while the node who received fewer rows would
attempt to fetch more from the left side.

This left/right fetch-more mix caused the deadlock because the upstreams
were then waiting for `DistributedResultResponse` answers from the
_other_ downstream.

Fix distributed execution of window functions with PARTITION BY on object subscripts

The comment in https://github.com/crate/crate/pull/17226#discussion_r1922009393 was correct

The bucketing logic on object columns doesn't work as it can lead to
data being split that ought to belong together.

For example with an object `data` with two columns `attribute` and `id`.

If partitioning on `data` instead of `data['attribute']`:

    bucketIdx=0 value={attribute=a-1, id=1844} hash=13034888
    bucketIdx=0 value={attribute=a-1, id=1838} hash=13034894
    bucketIdx=1 value={attribute=a-1, id=1851} hash=13034873

The correct partitioning on would `data['attribute']` would send all
data to the same bucket:

    bucketIdx=1 value=a-1 hash=94661
    bucketIdx=1 value=a-1 hash=94661
    bucketIdx=1 value=a-1 hash=94661

To fix the issue, this extends `DistributionInfo` / modulo bucketing to
support arbitrary expressions on >= 6.1.1.
For < 6.1.1 it switches the plan to execute without distribution.

Fix out-of-order response messages for bulk execution via pgwire

Fix intermittent subscription loss in logical replication during rolling upgrades

PublicationsStateAction.Response instances may be passed between
publisher nodes before being forwarded to subscriber node. During
rolling upgrades, this forwarding behaviour leads to a chain of
cross-version conversions of the Response instance: 5.10 -> 6.0 -> 5.10.

Use indexUUID as an index identifier instead of the indexName

In order to support metadata only modifications like table name
renames, indices must be purly addressed by their indexUUID,
especially at the shard routing to avoid any shard allocation
re-processing.
Relation name handling should be only based on the recently added
RelationMetadata entities.

The `indexName` property is still written to the IndexMetadata
for backward compatibility, mainly to read and upgrade older indices.
It's marked as deprecated and should be fully removed in future.

Relates to #17518, #17075.

Replace shardId.getIndexName() usages by resolving-by-indexUUID

Instead of decoding table schema, name and partition values from
the shard's indexName, resolve related metadata by the shard's
indexUUID.

Add indexUUID related BWC code for the cluster state and node operations

When running in a mixed cluster, any cluster state read or written
from/to nodes which uses the indexName to resolve indices must be
converted to the current format which uses the indexUUID instead.
This affects:
  - RoutingTable
  - ClusterBlocks

Additionally, any job request must also change it's format,
especially the Routing of ExecutionPhases, when sending or receiving
to/from older nodes.

All is done on-the-fly based on the sending/receiving node's version.

Improve memory accounting in StreamBucket

RamAccounting used to rely on size() difference before and after write to compute ram usage of the added Row.

BytesStreamOutput has ramBytesUsed() method providing precise memory usage of the underlying ByteArray,
so switching to this method to make accounting more precise.

size() eventually catches up but there can be windows where it lags behind.
For example:
out.size(): 21, out.ramBytesUsed: 1080
out.size(): 42, out.ramBytesUsed: 1080
out.size(): 63, out.ramBytesUsed: 1080
out.size(): 84, out.ramBytesUsed: 1080
out.size(): 105, out.ramBytesUsed: 1080
…
out.size(): 987, out.ramBytesUsed: 1080
out.size(): 1008, out.ramBytesUsed: 1080
out.size(): 1029, out.ramBytesUsed: 1216
…
out.size(): 16401, out.ramBytesUsed: 32768
out.size(): 16422, out.ramBytesUsed: 32768

For big buffers this difeference can lead to a series of add(Row row) calls with a notable underaccouting
which can lead to OOM-s on nodes under high memory pressure.

Fix pgwire message ordering hiccups

The PostgreSQL wire protocol had the issue that the channel handler's
already processed the next incoming messages while outgoing messages
were still being computed asynchronously.

For example in:

    -> Parse
    <- ParseComplete
    -> Bind
    <- BindComplete
    -> Execute
    -> Parse
    <- ParseComplete*1
    <- CommandComplete*2 (referring to execute)

We used the `DelayableWriteChannel` to delay `ParseComplete*1`, to
ensure it would be sent _after_ `CommandComplete*2`

It was somewhat difficult to reason about its correctness given that
most of the `Session` is built under the assumption that there is only
one component at a time calling methods in a strictly sequential order,
not concurrently. (With the exception of cancellation)

This replaces the `DelayableWriteChannel` approach with explicit read
control. To simply no longer process new messages while an async
execution is in progress.

Revert "Fix pgwire message ordering hiccups"

This reverts commit aa029bff3f82f82b2df02d4b00ae6a917a4a6996.

The auto-read wasn't fully disabled because the `PgDecoder` could still
read multiple messages. There is an option to disable that
(`setSingleDecode` of `ByteToMessageDecoder`), but that doesn't work
either because of the following scenario covered by npgsql tests in
crate-qa:

    CrateContext.ConnectionString = conn.ConnectionString;
    using CrateContext context = new();
    for (int i = 0; i < 2; i++)
    {
        context.Test.Add(new TestEntity());
    }
    await context.SaveChangesAsync();

Causes a message flow like:

    -> Parse
    -> Bind
    -> Describe
    -> Execute

    -> Parse
    -> Bind
    -> Describe
    -> Execute

    -> Sync

Each `execute` doesn't actually start execution, but defers it to `sync`
for batch execution. The future returned by `session.execute()` which
 was used to trigger a manual `read` would never be called with
 singleDecode set because we'd never process the `sync` message.

Without `singleDecode`, the next messages are immediately processed and
we send messages, leading to `commandComplete` arriving out of order:

    sentParseComplete
    sentBindComplete
    sentNoData
    sentParseComplete
    sentBindComplete
    sentNoData
    sentCommandComplete
    sentCommandComplete

Conclusion:

We need to keep the delay mechanism

unexpected `commandComplete` message, which caused the client to stop
receiving the remaining results.

Fix hash join deadlock scenario

It could happen that a hash join got stuck when executing on more than
one node and if the number of rows within a page was smaller then the
expected block size despite having `allLoaded() = false`.

This happened if the page size didn't divide cleanly by the number
of nodes, resulting in one downstream receiving fewer rows.

One downstream would then move from the build phase to the probe phase,
and process the right side, while the node who received fewer rows would
attempt to fetch more from the left side.

This left/right fetch-more mix caused the deadlock because the upstreams
were then waiting for `DistributedResultResponse` answers from the
_other_ downstream.

    bucketIdx=0 value={attribute=a-1, id=1838} hash=13034894
    bucketIdx=1 value={attribute=a-1, id=1851} hash=13034873

    bucketIdx=1 value=a-1 hash=94661

Restrict symbol.cast to one cast mode; unify explicit/implicit Function representation

Changes `cast(Symbol, CastMode ... modes)` to `cast(Symbol, CastMode)`
because it is not possible to mix CastMode.TRY with CastMode.IMPLICIT, instead
the cast modes are all exclusive and TRY is always explicit with `null`
fallback on failures.

This also changes the `Function` representation for implicit casts to
match that of explicit casts: Using a `null` literal symbol that carries
the type information instead of using a string with type signature.

Clear DFA cache on memory pressure

The ANTLR DFA cache is unbounded and grows with new unique statements.
That could lead to OOMs or high GC activity caused by a large cache that
can't be GCd.

Accounting the size of the DFA cache itself after each query would add
quite a lot of overhead - and that overhead increases with the size of
the cache.

This instead simply triggers a cache reset once high GC load is
detected. This will cause subsequent queries to parse slower but should
avoid out of memory errors.

Fix fetch rewrite for Eval operators injected by hash join reordering

The `Eval.rewriteToFetch` implementation either:

- Removes its own outputs which will be fetched later instead
- Retains outputs that can be evaluated using the available source
  outputs.

The latter didn't account for expressions containing multiple columns.
For example in `CASE WHEN (x = y)` it's possible that `x` is available
in the source outputs, but `y` isn't and needs to be fetched instead.

This caused a `Can't handle Symbol [SimpleReference: y]` error

Eval is typically the top-most operator of a relation (or sub-relation),
so this rarely caused an issue, but with the `ReorderHashJoin` rule we inject an `Eval` operator to retain the output order. That caused the latent issue to manifest.

Add a hint about defaultReadAdvice setting to 6.0 release notes

Lucene started using ReadAdvice.RANDOM by default in
https://github.com/apache/lucene/commit/a2676b1b26aab5a8bb655031f2ce0299e5207e00

This can cause 2 types of regressions
1. When access pattern doesn't fit RANDOM.
For example, RecoverySourceHandler was meant to use READ (sequental chunks)
but in 10.0 upgrade https://github.com/crate/crate/commit/4918f3c228adf13e8e3d065cd3266f499f242b85 we started using DEFAULT
to reflect the fact that READ was replaced by DEFAULT in Lucene in https://github.com/apache/lucene/commit/32d692049fc4ea3a34ad25ef116c8148f7c055ac

However, once RANDOM became default, we implicitly started using not-fitting access pattern
and got performance drawback on recovery, similar to https://github.com/opensearch-project/OpenSearch/issues/19156#issuecomment-3288799192

2. If flag is set back to NORMAL and this is still not enough,
it means RANDOM is used **explicitly** somewhere (and flag is not affecting it)
and MGLRU is enabled in Linux kernel (see https://github.com/apache/lucene/issues/14408).

In this case, MGLRU can be diabled with "sudo sh -c 'echo 0 > /sys/kernel/mm/lru_gen/enabled'"

However, code where ReadAdvice.Random is used in 10.0 (https://github.com/apache/lucene/commit/4ea2bae1198bb3052912e08faa3a4c2cdaa67db0)
was backported to 9.11.0 in https://github.com/apache/lucene/commit/bb52dcbbc24ed4acce72f6236f417e889aee2f92
CrateDB uses this since 5.8.0 https://github.com/crate/crate/commit/de9cb2ec8fe1fe143704a8001d2a9788269a7d43
and no regression have been reported, so not includsing this hint to the release notes

Undefined type must not overwrite a concrete type on schema updates, it's handled by DocTableInfo.staleUndefined

Add a breaker.policy to kill the top consumer instead of current query

If a user runs one heavy query like a join or a group by it can happen
that other queries which would be cheap get rejected with a circuit
breaker exception.
This continues until the heavy query either completes or also trips the
breaker mechanism.

This adds a `indices.breaker.policy` setting which can be set to
`top_consumer` to change the circuit breaker behavior to instead kill
the top consumer instead of the query tripping the breaker. A cheap
query tripping the breaker would then instead kill the heavy query.

Fix resolving of input column for aggregations with params in Filter operator

In a query like:

    select 1 from sys.summits group by height having count(?) = ?

The `Filter` operator for `count(?) = ?` retained the `count(?)`
aggregation despite it being part of the incoming `GroupHashAggregate`.
This led to a `UnsupportedFeatureException[Function [..] is not a scalar
function.]` error.

The `InputColumns` logic didn't resolve the aggregation to an
`InputColumn` because the parameter binding inferred, changing
`count(?)` to `count(<literal-value>)` - causing it to no longer match
the `source.outputs()` symbol.

Solution:

Create input column symbol first, and replace params and subquery values
afterwards.

Fix issue with col oids on old tables when upgrading to >= 6.0.0

Tables created before `5.5.0` didn't have col oids, so their Lucene
fields names matched the col names. With `5.5.0` we introduced col oids
so each col is assigned one, and the Lucene fields are stored using
those oids instead of column names. Due to a bug in
`Metadata.setTable()` where we don't pass an `oidSupplier`, certain
actions like delete partitions, alter table settings etc. which call
this method, would assign incrementing col oids to those old tables.
As a result when trying to retrieve data, from then on, the col oids
would be used but the existing data is stored in Lucene using the col
names, thus returning `NULL`.

Add similar logic, that we use in other places, to the problematic flavor
of `Metatada.setTable()` to check the `version created` of the table
and don't assign oids for those older tables.

Add Largest Triangle Three Buckets initial implementation

The Largest Triangle Three Buckets (LTTB) algorithm is a downsampling method
designed to preserve the shape of the data while reducing its resolution
[1, 2].

This commit implements LTTB as an aggregation function in CrateDB.

Some notes about this implementation:

- This implementation requires all data relevant to the
  query to be buffered in memory. Once the the data is gathered, then the LTTB
  algorithm can be run over that data.

- Downsampling is not done during the `reduce` phase of the
  aggregation because the aggregation function is still in the process of
  gathering all relevant data at that time.
  LTTB needs all the data available in order to run accurately.

- A simple experiment to downsample 1 million data points to 100 points
  on a locally run crate node shows the UDF implementation of LTTB
  from [2] completes in ~2 sec while the native implementation from this
  commit completes in about < 500 ms

[1]: https://skemman.is/bitstream/1946/15343/3/SS_MSthesis.pdf
[2]: https://community.cratedb.com/t/advanced-downsampling-with-the-lttb-algorithm/1287

- limited: used `getLongRtt`

used in insert-from-values back to `getLongRtt` to address the

Reject restore snapshot when target schema is incompatible

Restoring a partition into a table with an incompatible schema used to
silently succeed and produce unreadable Lucene segments, surfacing later
as engine-level errors at SELECT time.

A new SnapshotSchemaValidator runs at the top of
RestoreSnapshotUpdateTask.execute() before any cluster state mutation:
shared columns must have matching name, OID and value type, target may
not be stricter on nullability; relation-level checks cover the primary
key, pkConstraintName, partitioned-by and CLUSTERED BY columns. Nullable
extras on the target are preserved across the restore; NOT NULL extras
are rejected.

Errors map to HTTP 409 (new HttpErrorStatus.RESTORE_SCHEMA_INCOMPATIBLE)
and SQLSTATE 42P17 invalid_object_definition, matching PostgreSQL's
ATTACH PARTITION rejection.

Fix resolving of input column for aggregations with params in Filter operator

In a query like:

    select 1 from sys.summits group by height having count(?) = ?

The `Filter` operator for `count(?) = ?` retained the `count(?)`
aggregation despite it being part of the incoming `GroupHashAggregate`.
This led to a `UnsupportedFeatureException[Function [..] is not a scalar
function.]` error.

The `InputColumns` logic didn't resolve the aggregation to an
`InputColumn` because the parameter binding inferred, changing
`count(?)` to `count(<literal-value>)` - causing it to no longer match
the `source.outputs()` symbol.

Solution:

Create input column symbol first, and replace params and subquery values
afterwards.

Fix issue with col oids on old tables when upgrading to >= 6.0.0

Tables created before `5.5.0` didn't have col oids, so their Lucene
fields names matched the col names. With `5.5.0` we introduced col oids
so each col is assigned one, and the Lucene fields are stored using
those oids instead of column names. Due to a bug in
`Metadata.setTable()` where we don't pass an `oidSupplier`, certain
actions like delete partitions, alter table settings etc. which call
this method, would assign incrementing col oids to those old tables.
As a result when trying to retrieve data, from then on, the col oids
would be used but the existing data is stored in Lucene using the col
names, thus returning `NULL`.

Add similar logic, that we use in other places, to the problematic flavor
of `Metatada.setTable()` to check the `version created` of the table
and don't assign oids for those older tables.

Fix INSERT INTO perf regression; restore 5.10 backoff behavior

In 5.10 we've had two different back-off policy behaviors:

- unlimited: used `getLastRtt`
- limited: used `getLongRtt`

https://github.com/crate/crate/pull/17943 tried to unify this to:

- unlimited: used `getLongRtt`
- limited: used `getLongRtt`

But that caused some issues (unclear what exactly), leading to:

https://github.com/crate/crate/pull/18049

Which changed it to:

- unlimited: used `getLastRtt`
- limited: used `getLastRtt`

This caused the `specs/partitioned_bulk_insert.py` case from
crate-benchmarks to show a huge slowdown with linearly increasing
request times.

This restores the 5.10 behavior by changing the limited case which is
used in insert-from-values back to `getLongRtt` to address the
performance regression.

Reject restore snapshot when target schema is incompatible

Restoring a partition into a table with an incompatible schema used to
silently succeed and produce unreadable Lucene segments, surfacing later
as engine-level errors at SELECT time.

A new SnapshotSchemaValidator runs at the top of
RestoreSnapshotUpdateTask.execute() before any cluster state mutation:
shared columns must have matching name, OID and value type, target may
not be stricter on nullability; relation-level checks cover the primary
key, pkConstraintName, partitioned-by and CLUSTERED BY columns. Nullable
extras on the target are preserved across the restore; NOT NULL extras
are rejected.

Errors map to HTTP 409 (new HttpErrorStatus.RESTORE_SCHEMA_INCOMPATIBLE)
and SQLSTATE 42P17 invalid_object_definition, matching PostgreSQL's
ATTACH PARTITION rejection.

creating a partition on a swapped table:

    create table tbl1 (x int, p int) partitioned by (p);
    create table tbl2 (x int, p int) partitioned by (p);

    at org.elasticsearch.snapshots.SnapshotShardsService.lambda$startNewShards$0(SnapshotShardsService.java:250)

Fix ORDER BY on aliased view column over a join

`ORDER BY <view column>` resolves to an `AliasSymbol` wrapping the
underlying column, e.g. `foo AS bar`. When the source of the `Order`
operator is a join that already outputs the plain `foo`, the alias is
not `equals` to any source output. This had two consequences:

- `Order` appended the alias as an extra output. `rewriteToFetch` then
  treated it as a computed output and mapped it to a fetch stub, even
  though the value is already carried by the source.
- `OrderByPositionVisitor` and `PositionalOrderBy.tryMapToNewOutputs`
  found no position for the alias, so the statement failed with
  `Must have an orderByPosition for each symbol`.

Treat a symbol and the same symbol wrapped in an `AliasSymbol` as
equivalent when resolving order-by positions, and don't add an order-by
symbol to `Order.outputs` if the source already provides it unaliased.
`InputColumns.SourceSymbols` already registers both forms under the same
index, so the sort projection resolves the alias to the source column.

mensagens_commits: Bump version to 6.4.4-SNAPSHOT

Fix UNION pruning dropping outputs kept by its sources

Keep the outputs the sources ended up with, instead of the requested
ones, so that the outputs of the UNION always mirror the outputs of its
sources; the `Eval` on top of the UNION removes them from the result.
If an output cannot be mapped back, or the two sources kept different
ones, skip the pruning as before.

Fixes: #19852
(cherry picked from commit 0784c20e3360c795a453352ce38f27ebd45f3854)

Don't push down filters containing non-deterministic functions

Prevent non-deterministic filter parts from beign pushed down
beneath operators which compute values over a set of rows, i
as it changes the semantics and therefore their result:

- `MoveFilterBeneathWindowAgg`: such a filter contains no column at all,
  therefore `windowDefinition.partitions().containsAll(...)` was
  trivially true and the part was treated as partition based.
- `MoveFilterBeneathGroupBy`: the filter would be evaluated per source
  row instead of per group.
- `MoveFilterBeneathProjectSet`: the table functions can generate
  multiple rows per input row, so the filter would be evaluated before
  the row generation.

The push down of the remaining, deterministic parts of the filter
takes place as before, since all three rules already split the query
on `AND`.

Fix null = ALL(<empty>) incorrect results

Fixes https://github.com/crate/crate/issues/19922 and
Fixes https://github.com/crate/crate/issues/20013

The `ALL` operator should return true when the right value is
empty even if the left value is null[1]. This commit fixes a couple
scenarios where the incorrect results were returned when `null =
ALL(<empty>)`.

1. When the left value is a column that evaluates to null

There are different code paths that can be taken to evaluate
the `ALL` operator depending on the table being queried.

From the reported issue, when the outer query is on a base
table ("b"), the query plan is:

```
cr> explain SELECT id FROM b WHERE id = ALL (SELECT id FROM t WHERE FALSE);
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| QUERY PLAN                                                                    |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| MultiPhase (rows=unknown)                                                     |
|   └ Collect[doc.b | [id] | (id = ALL((SELECT id FROM (s))))] (rows=unknown)   |
|   └ Rename[id] AS doc.t (rows=unknown)                                        |
|     └ Rename[id] AS s (rows=unknown)                                          |
|       └ Eval[max(id) OVER (PARTITION BY x) AS id] (rows=unknown)              |
|         └ OrderBy[max(id) OVER (PARTITION BY x) AS id ASC] (rows=unknown)     |
|           └ WindowAgg[id, x] | [max(id) OVER (PARTITION BY x)] (rows=unknown) |
|             └ Collect[doc.b | [id, x] | false] (rows=unknown)                 |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
Note `Collect[doc.b | [id] | (id = ALL((SELECT id FROM (s))))] (rows=unknown)`

Here, we push the `ALL` evaluation
down to lucene. That causes the `ALL` operator to be evaluated by `AllEqOperator`,
(in the examples in the issue). This code path has a check for an empty
right value (the output of the subquery) and ultimately returns the correct data.

However, when the outer query is on a view that is on a window function, we do not push the
`ALL` evaluation to lucene.

Here is a query plan demonstrating this ("t" is a view built from a
window function):

```
cr> explain SELECT id FROM t WHERE id = ALL (SELECT id FROM b WHERE FALSE);
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| QUERY PLAN                                                                                       |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| MultiPhase (rows=0)                                                                              |
|   └ Rename[id] AS doc.t (rows=0)                                                                 |
|     └ Rename[id] AS s (rows=0)                                                                   |
|       └ Eval[max(id) OVER (PARTITION BY x) AS id] (rows=0)                                       |
|         └ Filter[(max(id) OVER (PARTITION BY x) AS id = ALL((SELECT id FROM (doc.b))))] (rows=0) |
|           └ WindowAgg[id, x] | [max(id) OVER (PARTITION BY x)] (rows=unknown)                    |
|             └ Collect[doc.b | [id, x] | true] (rows=unknown)                                     |
|   └ OrderBy[id ASC] (rows=unknown)                                                               |
|     └ Collect[doc.b | [id] | false] (rows=unknown)                                               |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
Note the ALL operator is handled by the Filter and not the Collect in
this plan.

This latter code path will go through `AllOperator::evaluate`.
The problem is that this would return early once it saw the leftValue == null.
We now prioritize the right value check for empty to fix this issue.

2. The other scenario where the wrong results were returned for the ALL
operator is when the query has a null literal on the left value

The `Operator::normalizeSymbol` method returns early if there is an argument that evaluates to NULL.
That is relevant for most operators, but not for the ALL operator. We
now override `normalizeSymbol` in `AllOperator` so that the code falls
through to `AllOperator`

[1]: "The result of ALL is "true" if all rows yield true (including the case where the subquery returns no rows)."
[postgres docs](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/9.0/functions-subquery.html#AEN16897:~:text=The%20result%20of%20ALL%20is%20%22true%22%20if%20all%20rows%20yield%20true%20(including%20the%20case%20where%20the%20subquery%20returns%20no%20rows).)

Fix filtered nested CROSS JOIN rewrite to nested INNER JOINs

RewriteFilterOnCrossJoinToInnerJoin generated an invalid HashJoin condition for
filtered nested CROSS JOINs.

For example, it produced this plan:

    Eval[x, y, z]
      └ HashJoin[INNER | (((x = y) AND (x = z)) AND (y = z))]
        ├ NestedLoopJoin[CROSS]
        │  ├ Collect[doc.t3 | [z] | true]
        │  └ Collect[doc.t2 | [y] | true]
        └ Collect[doc.t1 | [x] | true]

The `y = z` predicate references only one side of the top-level HashJoin.
During hash matching, it affects the hash calculation for only one side,
causing the hash lookup to miss matching rows.

The intended plan is:

    Eval[x, y, z]
      └ HashJoin[INNER | ((x = y) AND (x = z))]
        ├ HashJoin[INNER | (y = z)]
        │  ├ Collect[doc.t3 | [z] | true]
        │  └ Collect[doc.t2 | [y] | true]
        └ Collect[doc.t1 | [x] | true]

Fix this by:

1. Preserving equi-join filters in RewriteFilterOnCrossJoinToInnerJoin if they
   do not reference both sides of the current cross join.
2. Allowing MoveFilterBeneathJoin to push the preserved filter below the outer
   join, so RewriteFilterOnCrossJoinToInnerJoin can be applied again.

Fix clustered by handling on columns with default clause omitted from inserts

With a primary key column with default clause the statements:

- insert into tbl (pk_column, other_col) values (?, ?)
- insert into tbl (other_col) values (?)

Routed to different shards - the first statement routing based on the
pk_column value, but the second didn't.

In the second statement this could prevent the record from being found
using a `select * from tbl where pk_column = ?` because the query would
get optimized to a `Get` plan. `Get` is looking for records on the
shards they're supposed to be in.

Fixes https://github.com/crate/crate/issues/20105

(cherry picked from commit 5268a1e7bbf445e778175d96c8e235064b090c90)

Revert "Fix filtered nested CROSS JOIN rewrite to nested INNER JOINs"

This reverts commit 106f9174737bc66bf9f71149526b5c94bd18b84b.

Because it generated worse join plan for joins with > 4 tables:

    EXPLAIN
    SELECT *
    FROM t1, t2, t3, t4
    WHERE t1.a1 = t3.a3
      AND t2.a2 = t4.a4
      AND t3.a3 = t4.a4;

+------------------------------------------------------------+
| QUERY PLAN                                                 |
+------------------------------------------------------------+
| HashJoin[INNER | ((a2 = a4) AND (a3 = a4))] (rows=unknown) |
|   ├ Eval[a1, a2, a3] (rows=unknown)                        |
|   │  └ NestedLoopJoin[CROSS] (rows=unknown)                |
|   │    ├ HashJoin[INNER | (a1 = a3)] (rows=unknown)        |
|   │    │  ├ Collect[doc.t1 | [a1] | true] (rows=unknown)   |
|   │    │  └ Collect[doc.t3 | [a3] | true] (rows=unknown)   |
|   │    └ Collect[doc.t2 | [a2] | true] (rows=unknown)      |
|   └ Collect[doc.t4 | [a4] | true] (rows=unknown)           |
+------------------------------------------------------------+

(cherry picked from commit 2a5959aca38b04f28f2c9120c8115702e0d168c5)

# Conflicts:

Fix handling of bitstring params when creating views

`Literal.fromObject` didn't handle `bitstring` values - creating a
`StringLiteral` with the bitstring value instead. For `CREATE VIEW`
statements containing parameter placeholders `Literal.fromObject` is
used to inline the values for the placeholders. Due to the missing
handling, that step failed.

`Literal.fromObject` is also used in a few other places (`show create
table` to convert setting values), but these are unproblematic as far as
I can tell.

With asyncpg this caused failures like:

    xs = asyncpg.BitString('0101')
    await conn.execute("create view v1 as select ?::bit(4)", xs)
    asyncpg.exceptions.InternalServerError: Cannot cast `'B''0101'''` of type `text` to type `bit(4)`

casos.name: v4.2.1
casos.body:
## What's Changed

A small maintenance release: a new model and a couple of fixes.

### Added

- **Kimi K3** is now available as a built-in model.

### Fixed

- Codex CLI authentication is restored.
- The tool and variable lists in the thread playground now scroll within a
  bounded height instead of pushing the layout.

## Install

Two editions. Install either, or both — they share the same `~/.llm-space` data, so switching keeps your threads and settings.

- **LLM Space** — uses the system WebView. Small download (~27 MB), light on memory and battery.
- **LLM Space Performance** — embeds its own rendering engine (~130 MB). Rendering stays consistent across macOS versions, and usually performs better.

Download a DMG below. Existing installs update in place.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/deer-flow/llm-space/blob/v4.2.1/CHANGELOG.md
mensagens_commits: fix: support macOS 14 release packages

fix(thread-tabs): move pathRef sync out of render in thread-tab-pane

no-ref-current-in-render: assign pathRef.current in a passive useEffect
instead of the render body. The ref is read only post-commit (debounced
write flush, refresh refetch, rename handler), so this preserves behavior
while removing the render-time mutation React can replay/discard.
fix(models): restore Codex CLI authentication

Merge pull request #84 from deer-flow/react-doctor/2026-07-18-scan

[react-doctor] Fix no-ref-current-in-render in thread-tab-pane (pathRef)

Merge pull request #85 from lihaozheCharlie/main

fix(models): restore Codex CLI authentication

Merge pull request #69 from singchia/codex/fix-macos-14-compatibility

fix: support macOS 14 release packages (#53)
chore: remove runHistory
Revert "fix: support macOS 14 release packages (#53)"

Merge pull request #86 from deer-flow/revert-69-codex/fix-macos-14-compatibility

Revert "fix: support macOS 14 release packages (#53)"

feat(web): embedded mode for shared thread viewer (#87)

Open the shared-thread viewer in a chrome-free "embedded" mode when the
URL opts in (`#/shared/.../threads/...?embedded`) or the viewport is
<= 850px. Embedded mode drops the site header and meta block, lets the
playground fill the frame, and renders image attachments as clickable
`[Image #N]` placeholders (numbered across the thread) instead of inline
thumbnails. The decision is made once at open so there's no reflow/flash
after the thread loads, and the loading skeleton matches the embedded
layout.

Plumbed via a new `compactImages` prop on ThreadPlayground and a small
ImageDisplayContext consumed by the image renderer; defaults off, so the
desktop app is unaffected. Also sets `document.title` to
"{title} - LLM Space" while a thread is open.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(web): enhance NotFound component for better error handling

Updated the NotFound component to accept optional `eyebrow` and `title` props, allowing for more descriptive error messages. Modified the ThreadViewer to differentiate between "not found" and load failures, displaying appropriate messages based on the error type. This improves user experience by accurately labeling transient errors like rate limits or network issues.

fix(thread-playground): adjust max height for tool and variable lists

Updated the max height for the tool and variable lists in the ThreadPlaygroundContent component to improve layout and usability. Added comments to clarify the intended behavior of the height restriction, ensuring that the lists will scroll when exceeding the specified height.
feat: support Kimi K3

casos.name: v4.6.3
casos.body:
## What's Changed

A maintenance release with clipboard and tool-response improvements, refreshed
MiniMax models, and a steadier streaming UI.

### Added

- Copy a file reference to the OS clipboard directly from a thread tab's context
  menu.
- Tool responses can now carry image content.

### Changed

- MiniMax providers now target their OpenAI-compatible chat endpoints. MiniMax-M3
  is refreshed with updated pricing, a 1M-token context window, text/image/video
  input, and adaptive/disabled thinking; MiniMax-M2.7 stays an always-on
  reasoning model.
- Codex CLI now supports API-key mode, with inline run-validation guidance and a
  more explicit desktop startup order.

### Fixed

- `todo_write` rendering stays stable while streaming: incomplete items are kept
  out of the preview, cancelled states are preserved, and its parsing is isolated
  from generic tool-call rendering.

## Install

Two editions. Install either, or both — they share the same `~/.llm-space` data, so switching keeps your threads and settings.

- **LLM Space** — uses the system WebView. Small download (~27 MB), light on memory and battery.
- **LLM Space Performance** — embeds its own rendering engine (~130 MB). Rendering stays consistent across macOS versions, and usually performs better.

Download a DMG below. Existing installs update in place.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/deer-flow/llm-space/blob/v4.6.3/CHANGELOG.md
mensagens_commits:
feat: add copy file functionality to thread tabs

Introduces a new feature that allows users to copy file references to the OS clipboard from the thread tabs. This includes the implementation of a `handleCopyFile` function in the `PageWorkspace` component and updates to the `ThreadTabs` component to integrate the new copy file command in the context menu.

feat: improve Codex setup and run validation (#97)

* feat(models): support Codex CLI API key mode

* refactor(desktop): make startup order explicit

* feat(ui): add inline run validation guidance

* fix(models): preserve Codex API-key overrides

fix: stabilize todo_write rendering while streaming (#98)

Keep incomplete todo items out of the preview, preserve cancelled states, and isolate parsing from generic tool-call rendering.
feat: support image content in tool responses (#101)

Refresh MiniMax providers to the OpenAI-compatible endpoints (#100)

Move the global and CN MiniMax providers out of the locked
@earendil-works/pi-ai catalog into local factories so the current
parameters can be applied. Both regions now target their
OpenAI-compatible chat endpoints
(https://api.minimax.io/v1 and https://api.minimaxi.com/v1) over the
OpenAI Completions API.

MiniMax-M3 is refreshed to /bin/bash.6/.4//bin/bash.12 input/output/cache-read
pricing, a 1M-token context window, text/image/video input, and
adaptive/disabled thinking. MiniMax-M2.7 stays an always-on reasoning
text model at /bin/bash.3/.2//bin/bash.06.

casos.name: v4.18.0
casos.body:
## What's Changed

This release upgrades the Pi agent runtime and completes the first broad
internationalization pass, bringing a Chinese interface across the desktop app
and shared Thread Playground.

### Added

- A Chinese interface language now covers the desktop shell, settings,
  dialogs, and Thread Playground, with bilingual command-palette matching and
  localized provider names.
- The bundled cross-project Memory plugin gives agents an opt-in durable store
  for preferences, project conventions, and decisions.
- Search settings now include Exa, AnySearch, and Zhihu MCP providers alongside
  the existing search integrations.
- The built-in Aliyun Qwen provider uses the DashScope OpenAI-compatible API,
  discovers `DASHSCOPE_API_KEY`, and includes Qwen 3.8/3.7 plus selected
  DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM, and MiniMax models.
- A short-drama writer example demonstrates a structured creative-writing
  workflow in the Thread Playground.

### Changed

- Updated `@earendil-works/pi-ai` and `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core` to
  0.85.1, the latest registry release checked on 2026-09-07, while retaining
  the local Responses compatibility patch.

### Fixed

- Zhihu search handles server-initiated JSON-RPC requests on its SSE stream.

## Install

Two editions. Install either, or both — they share the same `~/.llm-space` data, so switching keeps your threads and settings.

- **LLM Space** — uses the system WebView. Small download (~27 MB), light on memory and battery.
- **LLM Space Performance** — embeds its own rendering engine (~130 MB). Rendering stays consistent across macOS versions, and usually performs better.

Download a DMG below. Existing installs update in place.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/deer-flow/llm-space/blob/v4.18.0/CHANGELOG.md
mensagens_commits: fix: use unattended npx MCP presets and update 4.17 downloads

feat(i18n): add app i18n with a Chinese UI language

- Add I18nProvider and an en/zh message tree (apps/desktop/src/i18n); the
  language persists via localStorage, defaults from the browser
  languages, and is switchable in Settings > General (previously a
  disabled placeholder).
- Localize the settings dialog chrome, the General/Account/Network/
  Experimental pages, the shared API key field, the command palette,
  and command labels; palette search matches in either language.
- Localize the native menu by OS display language via the shared
  command label map.
- Add unit tests for message-tree parity, language detection, and
  command label coverage; update the settings docs.

Larger pages (Models, MCP, Plugins, Skills, Remote Servers) and the
thread playground still hold inline English strings and will migrate
in follow-ups.

feat(plugins): bundle a default cross-project Memory plugin

- Add the @llm-space/memory plugin (memory_save / memory_search /
  memory_forget tools plus a proactive memory skill), stored inline and
  written to <home>/plugins on first launch, mirroring the bundled
  skills seed. Seeding is once-only and never overwrites.
- Memories persist in the plugin data directory
  (data/plugins/@llm-space/memory/memories.jsonl), which is shared by
  every workspace and survives plugin updates - cross-project by
  design.
- Tag each memory with the originating working directory.
- Seed tests cover file layout, no-overwrite semantics, and a real
  save/search/forget round-trip that imports the seeded tool sources
  the same way the plugin runner does; docs updated (en + zh-CN).

Merge pull request #162 from zcai7675-bot/feat/default-memory-plugin

feat(plugins): bundle a default cross-project Memory plugin

fix(i18n): match palette entries in either language in command palette search

The Save to / Import from palette entries were filtered against
English-only literals ("Save to", "Import from") while rendering the
localized label, so a Chinese query like 保存 or 导入 hid the entry.

Add paletteLabels() returning both the en and zh labels (mirroring
commandLabels() for CommandType entries) and match the search against
both, so the palette answers queries in either language.
docs: define UI internationalization boundaries

feat(i18n): localize the high-visibility entry points named in review

Localize the surfaces users hit immediately after switching to Chinese:

- File tree: the node/root dropdown menus (reveal, import, copy,
  duplicate, rename, move-to-trash with per-OS names, refresh), the
  Share menu item, the empty state, and the delete/replace confirm
  dialogs.
- Thread tabs: the context menu (refresh, close/others/all, copy file,
  share, reveal, move-to-trash) plus the open/close tab aria labels.
- Thread playground header (packages/ui): run/undo/redo controls, the
  More-actions dropdown (run history, compact, generate project,
  share), and the run-settings menu, through a new
  PlaygroundLabelsProvider whose English defaults keep the web viewer
  working; the desktop injects zh via the app layout. Model-facing
  strings (tool names/descriptions, prompts) are untouched.
- Start-from-Example dialog: all chrome plus template cards, whose
  display names/descriptions localize through an id-keyed zh map --
  PROMPT_EXAMPLES and every seeded prompt/filename stay unchanged.
- Welcome screen and the Settings > Skills page title/description.

Tests: playground label parity/drift, example-localization coverage,
and provider hardening for navigator-less DOM shims; full suite,
typecheck, and lint green.
Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' into feat/i18n-chinese

feat(search): add Exa, AnySearch, and Zhihu MCP search providers

- Extend SearchSettings with the three MCP-backed providers and wire
  them into the provider factory, the search settings persistence, and
  the Settings > Search page (with Get API key links and optional/required
  key semantics: Exa and AnySearch work anonymously at lower rate
  limits; Zhihu requires an Access Secret from its developer console).
- Add a minimal MCP client inside the web tools module covering both
  transports: Streamable HTTP (Exa, AnySearch; handles JSON and
  SSE-framed responses plus mcp-session-id affinity) and the legacy SSE
  transport (Zhihu's official zhihu_search server, whose per-session
  message endpoint arrives via the endpoint event).
- web_fetch on MCP providers delegates to Firecrawl for safe page
  extraction, matching the Brave provider.
- Parse each server's result format (Exa Title/URL blocks, AnySearch
  headed lists, Zhihu XML search_item documents) into the shared
  WebSearchResult shape, covered by mock-fetch tests including the
  initialize handshake and session endpoint resolution.
fix(search): update server rpc test settings fixture for new providers

fix(search): handle server-initiated JSON-RPC requests on the Zhihu SSE stream

The live Zhihu SSE endpoint sends JSON-RPC requests such as
{"id":1,"method":"ping"} after the endpoint event. waitFor() matched
on id alone, so a ping was mistaken for our initialize response (and the
next ping for the tools/call response), surfacing an empty search result
before the real one arrived.

Distinguish server-initiated frames (method) from responses
(result/error) in waitFor(), answer pings with an empty result on the
session endpoint, reply -32601 to unknown server requests so the server
does not stall, and ignore notifications. The Zhihu test fixture now
includes the live server's ping frames (with colliding ids) as a
regression test.

feat(search): route the search settings page through the i18n layer

Per the AGENTS.md internationalization boundaries, the new provider
labels and the changed helper copy must not be inline English. Move the
whole Settings > Search page (title, description, provider names, key
labels, footer, and the save-failure toast) into the en/zh message tree;
provider ids, $VAR names, and endpoints stay canonical. The branch is
rebased on #161 so the page can consume the i18n provider; once #161
lands this commit's diff is search-page.tsx plus the new message keys
only.

Merge pull request #163 from zcai7675-bot/feat/mcp-search-providers

Add Antigravity ACP provider (#314)

* Add Antigravity ACP provider

Antigravity speaks Agent Client Protocol over stdio via the
agy_acp_server.par wrapper, joining the existing ACP provider family.
It surfaces real permission requests to the approval UI, matched by
advertised option kind; mode downgrades fail closed so a rejected
session/set_mode cannot leave yolo active.

- Rust resolver prefers ~/.local/bin/agy_acp_server.par so the
  server's resource directory is set correctly.
- Catalog probes initialize + session/new configOptions so the model
  picker reflects live provider values; seed models cover offline.
- Skills discovery gains ~/.gemini/antigravity/skills.

Transport and lifecycle hardening:

- Generation-scoped child ids (thread#N) isolate output from retired
  processes so late stdout/exit can never reach a replacement client.
- sessionEpoch/cancelEpoch invalidate queued lifecycle work on
  cancel/stop/forget; startup re-checks retirement after binary
  resolution and before publishing, so a forgotten session can never
  resurrect a process.
- Turns are serialized per thread; turnActive spans model/config/mode
  selection through the prompt, and a mid-flight cancel marks the
  transport stale so the next send recycles and resumes.
- JSON-RPC writes race a 15s deadline; cancellation settles local
  pending requests before notifying the provider; permission-response
  write failures retire the generation instead of leaving the prompt
  parked.
- A silence watchdog surfaces a status hint on long quiet turns while
  the 30-minute prompt timeout recycles the generation; the next send
  resumes the provider session on a fresh process.
- harness_write runs on the blocking thread pool via spawn_blocking so
  a child that stops draining stdin cannot starve the async workers
  dispatching harness_kill.

Covered by mocked lifecycle tests, a real-binary suite (AGY_REAL=1)
and a 10-scenario soak suite (AGY_SOAK=1): thread fleets, rapid queued
sends, cancel/stop/forget cycles, mid-turn process kills, cwd drift
and queued-send suppression.

* Preserve config options on malformed ACP updates

* Harden Antigravity ACP launch and permissions

Feat/customizable keybindings (#438)

* Add per-command keybinding override storage

Persist a custom shortcut or a disabled flag per command in localStorage, reject duplicates, and expose matching helpers used by the key handlers.

* Show real modifier names for recorded shortcuts

Render Ctrl, Alt, and Shift as words on Linux and Windows and keep the macOS symbols.

* Route keybinding overrides through app and editor handlers

Map custom shortcuts back to workspace commands, keep Ctrl+Tab separate from the adjacent tab cycle, and gate every app, editor, transcript, and picker handler on the stored override.

* Apply keybinding overrides to the macOS menu

Rebuild the native menu without an accelerator for a disabled command and with the recorded combination for a custom one, leaving menu clicks untouched.

* Show current shortcuts in the web menu bar

Render the recorded combination, or no shortcut at all when the command is disabled, and refresh across windows on the storage event.

* Record, disable, and reset shortcuts in Keybindings settings

Turn the key cell itself into the recorder, drop the per-row toggle, disable with Delete, and show a small reset only when a command differs from its default. The recording hint is anchored beside the cell so rows keep a fixed height.

* Match recorded shortcuts against real keyboard events

Keyboard events expose modifiers as prototype accessors, so spreading the event dropped all of them: no custom shortcut matched, and the default it replaced died with it. Copy the fields explicitly and cover it with a prototype-backed event plus a handler-level test.

* Honor custom shortcuts in the direct app key handlers

The Settings, Search, Go to File, Command Palette, Find in Files, Open Project, New Window, sidebar, and Reload blocks compared a hard-coded key before consulting the stored override, so a rebound chord never entered the block. Let the override be the sole predicate and pass the default chord as the fallback match.

* Reject shortcuts that shadow a default binding

Conflict detection only compared recorded chords with other recorded chords, so rebinding a command onto another command's default silently killed it. Derive each row's documented default, validate the incoming chord against every default and override, normalise modifier order on read, and require a digit for the grouped activate row.

* Record Alt chords for app shortcuts

The recorder required Command or Control, so Alt combinations returned null and were dropped without any feedback. Treat Command, Control or Option as a primary modifier, keep the OS-wide Quick Composer hotkey on Command or Control, and say so instead of silently ignoring the press.

* Keep composition and key-repeat guards on rebound chords

A rebound shortcut bypasses tabCommand, so it lost the isComposing guard and the archive repeat check, letting it fire mid-IME and auto-archive while the key was held.

* Cache parsed keybinding overrides

Every keystroke re-read localStorage, JSON.parsed the map and rebuilt a 45-entry command Set, several times per event. Cache the parsed value per raw string and hand out a fresh object so callers cannot corrupt it.

* Surface keybinding save failures

A failed localStorage write and a failed macOS menu update were both swallowed, so the UI claimed success while the change was lost or the native menu disagreed with the webview. Let the recorder's error tooltip report both, and log the startup sync instead of dropping it.

* Make the shortcut recorder keyboard and screen-reader safe

Recording swallowed every key including Tab, so it was a soft keyboard trap; Delete disabled even when a modifier was held, so Cmd+Delete could never be recorded; the busy state moved focus with disabled; and the error tooltip was never announced. Exit on unmodified Tab, disable only on a bare Delete, use aria-busy, and alert errors. Recording a Quick Composer chord no longer re-enables a feature switched off in General, and the workspace trigger keeps a valid aria-keyshortcut token.

* Reuse the shared keybinding label in the web menu bar

The menu bar re-implemented override resolution instead of calling the exported helper, so the two could drift.

* Fix macOS build in keybindings_set_overrides

set_menu returns Result<Option<Menu>, tauri::Error>, so the ? could not convert the error into String and the Option did not match the () return type. Map both errors explicitly and discard the previous menu. Caught by macOS CI: this code is cfg-gated and never compiled on Linux.

* Resolve rebound zoom chords outside the Cmd/Ctrl guard

Alt is a valid primary modifier, so an Option-only or Ctrl+Alt zoom binding could be recorded and displayed but never fired, because the whole zoom block sat behind the modifier guard the browser-standard defaults need. Resolve the custom zoom first and keep the guard only for the default path.

* Protect every owned chord through a shared conflict validator

The grouped activate row returned no default, so Cmd/Ctrl+1-8 could be claimed and silently shadow tab activation, and the Quick Composer chord was only checked as a table default rather than its live value. Both save paths now share validateKeybindingShortcut over one shortcutOwners() map covering grouped rows, the live Quick Composer chord and existing overrides.

* Re-enable and re-register the default when resetting Quick Composer

onReset reused the apply path that deliberately skips registration while the feature is off, so resetting a disabled row left it disabled. Reset now restores the enabled flag, re-registers the default chord and persists it. Also covers the recorder refusing a chord another command already owns.

* Derive aria-keyshortcuts from the active binding

The workspace trigger kept advertising the default chord after the command was rebound. It now comes from keybindingShortcutTokens, which maps the live override to ARIA token form and is omitted when the command is disabled.

* Test rebound zoom chords through an extracted resolver

Moves the zoom decision out of the App key handler into resolveZoomKeybinding so the Option-only case is covered by an automated test rather than only a headless-browser check: Option-only zoom in and reset fire, the replaced default stops firing, and disabled and composing are honoured.

* Cover the live Quick Composer chord in conflict detection

Adds the missing regression test for the reviewer's specific case: a chord stored outside the override table must still count as taken. Verified to fail without the fix.

* Validate Quick Composer conflicts before native registration

saveQuickComposerShortcut validates and can throw, but it ran after the awaited setQuickComposerShortcut call, so a conflicting chord registered an OS global hotkey and then failed to persist, leaving the OS holding a live shortcut that settings did not know about. Pre-validate with validateKeybindingShortcut in both apply and reset. The model keeps its own guard. Regression test asserts invoke is never called for a rejected chord.

* Skip app shortcuts while an IME is composing

Setting customCommand to null only disabled the custom routing path; keybindingPressed could still match a default or rebound chord and interrupt composition. The handler now returns early, and the ten direct app handlers move into resolveAppShortcut, which carries its own guard, resolves a rebound chord before the default table, and is covered by tests. Both composition tests were verified to fail without the guard.

Refine compact sidebar icons and activity indicator

- Add masking to prevent the activity dot overlapping icons

Run the same claude the user's shell does (#448)

* Run the same claude the user's shell does

MonoCode resolved `claude` by trying fixed paths first and only consulting the
login shell last, so an install the user had moved on from silently won. On
this machine `~/.local/bin/claude` is 2.1.50 from February while the shell
resolves 2.1.221 — the app ran a CLI ten months older than the terminal did.

That is not only a version number. Remote control does not exist in 2.1.50:
across the session files on this machine, 2.1.50 produced a `bridge-session`
record in 0 of 14 sessions and 2.1.221 in 69. Enabling remote control worked
everywhere except sessions started from MonoCode, with nothing to explain why.

The shell's answer now comes first. The fixed paths remain for a GUI launch
that never sees a shell.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0193GRNRwFWSM4dDKafs5Szz

* Search the inherited PATH before the fixed install dirs

The login-shell read is not guaranteed: it runs `zsh -lic printenv` with a
five second timeout, and on failure `gui_search_path` fell straight through
to its hardcoded dirs. `~/.local/bin` leads that list, so an install the
user had abandoned beat a current one sitting on the PATH the app was
launched with — the same stale-binary bug, reached through the fallback.

Our own PATH now comes second, after the login shell and ahead of the
guesses. A Finder launch is unaffected: launchd hands it a bare PATH that
holds no agent CLI, and those dirs are in the fixed list regardless.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0193GRNRwFWSM4dDKafs5Szz

* Respawn once more when Linux calls a fresh binary busy

`execve` fails with ETXTBSY while any process holds the file open for
writing, and in a threaded process that is not a state we control: a sibling
thread's spawn inherits our write handles for the moment before it execs its
own program. A binary written a moment ago is then briefly unrunnable, and
`validate_harness_binary_version` reported that as a binary whose version is
invalid — a permanent verdict on a transient condition.

This is why `configured_binary_paths_fail_closed_and_stay_exact` fails on
Linux CI only: it writes a script and probes it while the rest of the suite
spawns git in parallel threads. macOS does not enforce ETXTBSY and the test
is `#[cfg(unix)]`, so the other two runners never see it. Retrying costs
nothing when the error does not occur, and the window it waits out is
microseconds wide.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0193GRNRwFWSM4dDKafs5Szz

Let the turn go once an inline subagent has reported back (#452)

* Let the turn go once an inline subagent has reported back

A subagent Claude ran inline is registered from `task_started` like any
task, but nothing ever removed it: only `task_updated`, `task_notification`
and `background_tasks_changed` settle a task, and Claude sends none of those
for one that ended within the turn. Its report arrives on the parent's own
tool result instead, which marked the row completed and left the task in
`agentTasks`, so `maybeFinishTurn` refused to end the turn for good.

The session then stayed busy forever. Everything gated on that stayed
disabled, including the Build control on a plan the app had just captured
from a denied ExitPlanMode: the plan was there and readable, the button was
not clickable. Quitting appeared to fix it because `busy` is in-memory only
and a reloaded session comes back with `busy: false`, while the plan block
itself was persisted as ready all along.

Settle such a task when its tool result lands. A subagent that was
backgrounded still reports "Backgrounded" there and keeps running, so it is
left alone, as are shells and monitors.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0193GRNRwFWSM4dDKafs5Szz

* Key a turn's plan block so it cannot collide across restarts

A plan event carries a key so its later snapshots reach the block the turn
already created, even after a mid-turn follow-up appends a user block past
it. That key was `turn:${gen}`, and `gen` comes from a ref-held Map that is
empty on every app start, while the key is saved with the transcript.

So a session whose first turn produced a plan came back holding the key
`turn:1`, and the next run's first plan turn asked for `turn:1` again. The
match in upsertPlan tests the key against every plan block, not only the
current turn's, so the new plan overwrote the old one high up in the
transcript: the finished turn showed no plan at all, and a plan already
built reverted to ready.

Make the key unique per turn instead of per counter. Plans saved before
this keep their old keys and still render; nothing matches a key once its
turn is over, so a new turn simply appends its own block, which is what it
should have done all along.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0193GRNRwFWSM4dDKafs5Szz

* fix: move MCP Registry publish into Build workflow to fix race condition

The MCP Registry publish and Docker image build were both triggered
independently by tag push events. The publish completed in ~30s while
the Docker build took ~5min, causing the MCP Registry to reject the
publish because the Docker image didn't exist yet.

Moving the publish into the Build workflow as a job with `needs: build`
guarantees the Docker image is pushed before attempting to publish.
The standalone workflow is kept for manual re-publishing only.

Manual re-publishing can be done by re-running that job from a Build run.

fix: [TKC-5329] failFast aborted workers shown as passed instead of aborted (#7418)

* fix: [TKC-5329] failFast aborted workers shown as passed instead of aborted

When failFast is enabled on a parallel step and one worker fails, the
remaining workers were incorrectly shown as "passed" in the UI. This
happened because cancel() was called after ExecuteWorker returned, which
blocked on cleanup (~25s), by which time other workers had already
reported "passed" status.

Fix: Add onResult callback to ExecuteWorker that fires immediately after
processWorkerNotifications returns but before deferred cleanup. This
allows failFast to cancel the context promptly. Also override worker
status to ABORTED when context is cancelled, both in the ctx.Done()
handler and when a worker reports "passed" after cancellation.

* fix: resolve pre-existing lint issues (drive-by)

* fix: only override to aborted if worker hadn't already finished

Workers that genuinely completed (passed/failed) before fail-fast
cancellation now keep their real status. Only workers still running
when cancel fires are marked as aborted. This prevents inflating
the FailedWorkers count with workers that legitimately passed.

fix: configure git credential store to survive HTTP redirects during clone (#7475)

* fix: configure git credential store to survive HTTP redirects during clone

When cloning repositories over HTTPS with username/token credentials,
Git embeds credentials in the URL. However, when the remote server
(e.g., GitLab) returns HTTP redirects (301/302), Git strips credentials
from the URL for security. Combined with GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, this
causes intermittent 'could not read Username' failures.

This commit:
- Adds a credential.helper store backed by a temp file, so Git has a
  reliable fallback source for credentials even after redirects.
- Fixes http.extraHeader quoting for the 'header' auth type: removes
  erroneous single quotes that were sent literally (exec.Command does
  not invoke a shell).
- Adds tests for the new setupCredentialStore function.

* fix: make credential store setup best-effort to avoid blocking clone

The credential store is a fallback mechanism - if creating the file or
configuring git fails, log a warning and proceed with URL-embedded
credentials instead of failing the entire clone operation.

* fix: building/escaping value safely

Made-with: Cursor

* feat: add --interactive/-i flag to marketplace install

Lets users walk every spec.config parameter exposed by a marketplace
TestWorkflow and supply a value at the prompt. --set values, if any,
become the pre-filled default for each prompt; empty input keeps the
current value. Parameters marked sensitive are read with masked input
and their current value is never echoed back to the terminal.

The prompting helper takes an injectable Prompter interface so the
collection logic can be unit-tested without pterm.

Made-with: Cursor

* feat(marketplace): offer to run workflow after install

After a successful `testkube marketplace install`, prompt the user "Run
the workflow now? [Y/n]" and kick off an execution if they confirm. Add
a `--run` tristate flag so the prompt can be bypassed:

- `--run=true`  skip the prompt and run
- `--run=false` skip both the prompt and the run
- flag unset    prompt interactively (default Yes)

This keeps the default UX friendly while making the install command
fully automatable for CI/scripted use.

CreateOrUpdateFromBytes now returns the resolved workflow name so the
install command knows what to execute; a new RunWorkflowByName helper
in the testworkflows package performs a minimal ExecuteTestWorkflow
call and prints the execution ID alongside a watch hint. The Prompter
interface gains a Confirm method (pterm-backed at runtime), and the
resolveRunDecision helper is covered by unit tests for all four paths.

Made-with: Cursor

* feat(marketplace): prompt for install params by default on a TTY

The previous opt-in `-i / --interactive` flag meant running
`testkube marketplace install <name>` on a terminal silently used
workflow defaults, which was surprising when the workflow exposed
configurable parameters.

Make `--interactive` a tristate so the command is self-guiding on a
terminal while remaining scriptable in CI:

  - flag unset + stdin is a TTY + workflow has parameters -> prompt
  - flag unset + no TTY (CI, piped input)                  -> skip
  - `--interactive=true` / `-i`                            -> force prompt
  - `--interactive=false`                                  -> force skip

Introduces a package-level `isStdinTTY` hook (mattn/go-isatty) that
tests can override, and a `shouldPromptForParameters` helper covered
by seven table-driven cases for each branch. Promotes go-isatty from
indirect to direct in go.mod to reflect the new import.

Made-with: Cursor

* feat(marketplace): add -f/--follow to install to stream execution logs

Mirror the `testkube run testworkflow -f` UX on the install command so
users can install-and-watch in a single step. `-f` streams logs until
the workflow finishes and exits with the workflow's exit code.

Precedence for the run decision is now:

  1. `--run` explicit (either true or false) wins.
  2. `-f` supplied without `--run` implies `--run=true`; otherwise
     following an install that did not start a run would produce no
     output.
  3. Otherwise ask the user interactively.

`RunWorkflowByName` gains a `follow bool` parameter and reuses the
existing `uiWatch` helper from run.go, plus `render.PrintTestWorkflowExecutionURIs`
for the post-run summary. New table cases cover --run=false beating -f
and -f without --run implying a run.

fix: escape {{ and }} in CRD descriptions before Helm template rendering (#7549)

The `js/scripts/crd-postprocess.js` postprocessor wraps generated CRD
YAMLs into a shared Helm library template (testkube-crds). It reads
each CRD YAML and embeds the content verbatim inside a `{{- define
... -}} ... {{- end }}` block.

controller-gen copies Go struct comments into the CRD's OpenAPI
`description` field. When one of those comments contains Testkube
expression-language examples like `{{resource.spec.replicas}}` — as
the recently added WorkflowTrigger CRD in api/workflowtriggers/v1/
workflowtrigger_types.go does — the resulting `.tpl` file has that
text intact. Helm then parses the file and tries to evaluate
`{{resource.spec.replicas}}` as a Go template action, failing with:

  parse error: function "resource" not defined

The failure happens on every consumer of the testkube-crds library:
testkube-operator, testkube-runner, and any downstream chart that
depends on either. Currently that makes `helm template` on the
testkube umbrella, testkube-runner, or testkube-operator charts
error out as soon as the descriptions are included.

Fix: add a single-pass escape step in the postprocessor that converts
every `{{` to `{{\`{{\`}}` and every `}}` to `{{\`}}\`}}` inside the
CRD content before wrapping it in Helm template syntax. When Helm
renders the library, the backtick-quoted strings emit the literal
braces back into the final CRD output — description text round-trips
unchanged.

Re-ran `make generate-crds` to regenerate the three `.tpl` files
(library + operator+runner synced copies). No behavior change to the
resulting CRDs; only the intermediate template now renders cleanly.

Verified with `helm template k8s/helm/testkube` and
`helm template k8s/helm/testkube-runner` — both succeed.

### `@liveblocks/chat-sdk-adapter`

- Introduce the package. Install with
  `npm install @liveblocks/chat-sdk-adapter`. Provides a
  [`chat-sdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/chat)-compatible backend adapter
  backed by Liveblocks Comments: webhooks, posting and editing messages,
  reactions, paginated fetches, thread and channel helpers, and optional
  `resolveUsers` / `resolveGroupsInfo` hooks.

### `@liveblocks/react`

- Add Feeds hooks: `useFeeds`, `useFeedMessages`, `useCreateFeed`,
  `useDeleteFeed`, `useUpdateFeedMetadata`, `useCreateFeedMessage`,
  `useDeleteFeedMessage`, and `useUpdateFeedMessage`.

### `@liveblocks/node`

- Add REST client methods for Feeds: `getFeeds`, `getFeed`, `createFeed`,
  `updateFeed`, `deleteFeed`, `getFeedMessages`, `createFeedMessage`,
  `updateFeedMessage`, and `deleteFeedMessage`.

### Python SDK

- Add Feeds REST API support on the sync and async clients (`get_feeds`,
  `get_feed`, `create_feed`, `update_feed`, `delete_feed`, `get_feed_messages`,
  `create_feed_message`, `update_feed_message`, `delete_feed_message`) with
  matching request/response models.

### `@liveblocks/client`

- Add **Feeds**: room-scoped feeds with metadata and messages and APIs to list,
  create, update, and delete feeds and messages (`fetchFeeds`,
  `fetchFeedMessages`, `addFeed`, `updateFeed`, `deleteFeed`, `addFeedMessage`,
  `updateFeedMessage`, `deleteFeedMessage`).

### `@liveblocks/react-ui`

- Add `body` prop to `Comment` to allow overriding only the default rich-text
  comment body while still keeping attachments, reactions, and
  `additionalContent` as is, unlike when using the `children` prop.
- Fix `AvatarStack` negative margin breaking alignment.

casos.body:
For full upgrade instructions, see the [3.18 upgrade guide](https://liveblocks.io/docs/platform/upgrading/3.18).

### `@liveblocks/client`

- **Breaking:** `useStorage` now returns plain objects for `LiveMap` values instead of `Map` instances. Legacy APIs have been removed: `.toImmutable()`, `.toObject()`, `.toArray()`.
- New `.toJSON()` on all Live structures, returning a cached JSON-compatible snapshot. `JSON.stringify(root)` now just works.
- New `LiveObject.from(obj)` to create a LiveObject from plain JSON, recursively converting nested objects/arrays to Live structures.
- New `.reconcile(obj)` to efficiently reconcile a LiveObject tree to match a JSON snapshot, only mutating what changed.
- `initialStorage` accepts `LiveObject.from()` result directly.

### `@liveblocks/react-flow/node`

- New `mutateFlow()` API for reading and mutating React Flow data from a Node.js backend. Install via `npm i @liveblocks/react-flow`, import from `@liveblocks/react-flow/node`. See the [docs](https://liveblocks.io/docs/api-reference/liveblocks-react-flow#server-side).

### `@liveblocks/react-ui`

- Add standalone `Avatar` component to complement `AvatarStack` for more fine-grained customization.
- Add `variant` prop to `AvatarStack` to support outlined avatars.

### `@liveblocks/zustand` and `@liveblocks/redux`

- Fix: Initial storage seeding no longer creates an undo frame.
- Fix: Presence updates are now batched with storage updates.
