casos.body:
### Patch Changes

-   6f5b7a9: Fix production panic regressions
mensagens_commits: fix wasm pre-commit aliasing (#939)

fix: production panic regressions (#943)

* Fix stale DAG causal iteration after node splits

* Fix richtext cursor updates at fragment tails

* Add list import regression for split tracking

* Recover document locks after panic poisoning

* Add unpoisoned lock helpers across core internals

* Fail fast on poisoned core locks

* Return errors for snapshot encoding edge cases

* Fix loom lock helper usage

* Fix three March-2026 import panics (kim, mads, pr929 fixtures)

Three production blobs in loro-debug reliably panic inside doc.import on
loro-crdt@1.10.6:

- DagCausalIter assertion at dag/iter.rs: when a peer has multiple node
  segments in the target span and the later segment's deps fall outside
  the span, both segments reach the initial stack with zero in-degree and
  LIFO pops the higher counter first. Fix: in DagCausalIter::new, after
  out_degrees and succ are built, synthesize per-peer ordering edges so
  the lower counter must drain before the higher one is released.

- OnceCell::set(..).unwrap() double-set at oplog/loro_dag.rs:917 during
  ensure_vv_for on a diamond dep (loro-dev/loro#929): a shared ancestor
  gets pushed onto the iterative-DFS stack by multiple paths and the
  second pop tries to initialize an already-filled cell. Fix: skip nodes
  whose vv is already Some at the top of the loop and swallow the Err
  from the final set as a defensive measure.

- list_state Index-out-of-range panic for the mads-bootstrap fixture:
  the ListDiffCalculator cold-starts its RichtextTracker via
  new_with_unknown() and never learns about the snapshot's real list
  content. During replay the tracker's per-change checkouts temporarily
  retreat some snapshot ops, so a new op's fugue anchor lands inside the
  unknown prefix. CrdtRope::get_diff() then emits Retain(N) where N is
  larger than ListState.len(). Fix: change ContainerState::apply_diff
  (and DocState::apply_diff, init_with_states_and_version) to return
  LoroResult<()>; ListState::apply_diff pre-validates the delta against
  current length and returns LoroError::internal(..) on mismatch so
  doc.import surfaces the error instead of panicking. Root cause in the
  tracker cold-start path still needs follow-up.

Regression tests for all three live in crates/loro/tests/march_2026_panics.rs
with the captured production blobs in fixtures_march_2026/. Additional
targeted unit tests in dag/iter.rs and oplog/loro_dag.rs cover the
smallest synthetic DAG shapes that triggered each bug.

Allows measuring a pre-built or published azmcp binary (e.g. extracted
from a GitHub release) instead of always building the local
servers/Azure.Mcp.Server/src project. When -ServerExecutable is supplied,
the local server build step is skipped (the measurer tool is still built
unless -SkipBuild is also passed), enabling side-by-side comparisons of
current-source vs. a previously released server by running the script
twice with different -OutputDirectory values.

feat(azurebackup): add vault private-endpoint command group (#3345)

* feat(azurebackup): add vault private-endpoint command group

Adds 5 new commands under 'azmcp azurebackup vault private-endpoint':

- create: provisions Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints resource in a customer VNet subnet and optionally auto-approves the connection on the RSV.

- get: retrieves one or all Private Endpoint Connections (PECs) attached to a Recovery Services vault.

- approve/reject: manages the PEC state on the vault.

- delete: removes the vault-side PEC object.

All commands support --vault-type rsv|dpp. Backup vaults (DPP) return a NotSupportedException with clear guidance to use RSV.

Includes:

- Unit tests for all commands (Vault/PrivateEndpoint/*)

- Recorded live tests (AzureBackupPrivateEndpointCommandTests) using the RecordedCommandTestsBase pattern

- Bicep test infrastructure additions (RSV + VNet + subnet) for Private Endpoint scenarios

fix: resolve default subscription from Azure CLI on Windows (#347)

AzCommand launched the Azure CLI with FileName = "az" and
UseShellExecute = false, which routes to Win32 CreateProcess. That only
appends ".exe", ignores PATHEXT and cannot execute batch files at all.
The MSI/winget install of the Azure CLI ships az.cmd -- there is no
az.exe -- so Process.Start() threw and every subscription-based command
failed with "unable to retrieve from Azure CLI" even for users who were
correctly logged in. On Windows the CLI is now launched through the
command interpreter (%ComSpec%, falling back to cmd.exe).

Also fixes three related defects in the same method:

- The "az account show" call did not pass --output json, so a user with
  'az configure --defaults output=table' (or AZURE_CORE_OUTPUT=table)
  got non-JSON back and the same generic failure. Cross-platform.
- stderr was only read after WaitForExit(), so the CLI deadlocked if az
  filled the stderr pipe buffer with warnings or upgrade notices. Both
  pipes are now drained concurrently, with a 30 second timeout.
- CommandHelpers used Guid.Parse inside catch (Exception), conflating
  "az is unusable" with "az returned something unexpected", and
  swallowed the reason entirely. It now uses Guid.TryParse and appends
  the underlying cause to the validation error so the failure is
  diagnosable.

BuildStartInfo is exposed internally with an explicit isWindows flag so
the Windows launch path is covered by tests on non-Windows CI.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

mensagens_commits:
refactor: address review feedback on the Azure CLI subscription lookup

Follow-up to #349. No behavioural change on the happy path.

- Injectable resolver. ValidateAndResolveSubscription takes an optional
  Func<string> for the subscription lookup, defaulting to the Azure CLI.
  The previous test could only assert when 'az' resolution happened to
  fail, so it was a no-op on any machine with a logged-in Azure CLI, and
  forcing failure by mutating PATH/ComSpec would have been flaky given
  test parallelization is enabled. Success, throwing and non-GUID paths
  are now covered deterministically.

- Startup failure message. It reported process.StartInfo.FileName, which
  on Windows is the command interpreter, so it read as though cmd.exe
  were the Azure CLI. It now names 'az' and describes the interpreter
  separately as the launcher.

- Command interpreter resolution. ComSpec is trimmed of surrounding
  quotes, since ProcessStartInfo.FileName is not parsed as a command
  line and a quoted value would fail to start. The fallback resolves
  cmd.exe from the system directory instead of relying on a PATH lookup.

- Timeout path. After Kill the process is given a short grace period to
  actually terminate and the in-flight pipe reads are observed, rather
  than throwing immediately and leaving both dangling.

Also extracts ParseSubscriptionId so the exit-code, non-JSON and
missing-id branches are unit-testable without spawning a process.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: observe pipe read faults independently of the grace-period wait

Task.WaitAll(tasks, timeout) returns false on timeout rather than
throwing, so a read faulting after the grace period elapsed was left
unobserved -- exactly what KillAndObserve claimed to prevent. Faulted
continuations are now attached up front, so observation no longer
depends on the wait completing.

Extracts ObserveFaults so the behaviour is covered by tests.

casos.body:
This is the first release ahead of the automated release process that will be implemented in #4393.

Going forward, releases will be generated matching [pontoon.mozilla.org](https://pontoon.mozilla.org/) deployments, at most once a day.

## What's Changed

These are the main changes from the latest deployment on 2026-08-14.

### Features
* Composed Machinery is used to autofill translation in case of 100% match (#4417). The 100% notification has been moved (#4413).
* Create lock in DB instead of cache to prevent multiple sync operations (#4418).
* Check permissions on individual strings in the All Projects view (#4412).

### Bug fixes
* Fixed issues with machinery and suggestions on locales using a different category than `other` as default (#4405, #4407).
mensagens_commits: Bug 1514691: Change wording of the empty translation warning (#1150)

Fixes bug 1486497 - Add a Locales tab (#1139)

Adds a tab structure for helpers, adds the Locales tab, changes the way History and Locales are fetched and refreshed on entity change. This also starts putting API Flow types into a separate file, to be used in the rest of the app.

Bug 1468997: Disable Request Locale, r=me (#1153)

We should reconsider the UX for requesting new locales in order to meet
requirements from the PM team.

Fix bug 1397377: Restore ability to delete translations (#1152)

Translation can only be deleted, if it's rejected. That means we're
implicitly introducing a confirmation step for any non-rejected
translation. If you want to delete an approved or unreviewed
translation, you need to reject it first, and then delete it.

This approach also keeps Approve & Reject as the only first-rate
actions. The Delete action should be used in edge cases, more rarely,
and is hence, discouraged. 

Other changes:
* Make <menu> height always the same, even for non-authenticated users
  and read-only translations. That makes the helpers height occupy the
  entire available height across all pages.
* Unify the way of getting translations from the DB.
* Improve some comments.
Fix bug 1514479: [FTL] Reset to the right original string on empty search (#1154)
Fix bug 1516165: Hide email address from profile page for unauthenticated users (#1155)
No bug - Split links into different cell. (#1156)
Fix bug 1478307: Remove unused priority field from the Resource model.
Fix bug 1473749: Add date_created and date_obsoleted fields to Resource & Project.

Fix bug 1518749 - Update bleach to version 3.0.2. (#1160)

* Fix bug 1518749 - Update bleach to version 3.0.2.

Note that from version 3, bleach does not require html5lib anymore, as it vendors it. We thus remove it from our requirements as well.
Fix bug 1394194: Order locales in Admin by code (#1159)
Fix bug 1518749 - Put back webencodings dependency. (#1161)

Fix bug 1490351 - Add actions on status icons in History tab. (#1137)

This enables approve, reject, unapprove and unreject actions, accessible from the status icons next to each translation in the History tab. It correctly updates the status on the server and the local state. It also creates a new view dedicated to approving translations, in order to not have to use update_translation, which requires a lot of parameters for just changing a status. It refreshes History data from the server, to make sure that the data is correct instead of trying to fix it locally.

Bug 1486504 - Navigation for Translate.Next (#1148)

- Rename navigation type and selectors to free the name Navigation for a component.
- Add a simple Navigation component.

This is just a simple breadcrumb element that allows to go back to the Team and Project dashboards.

Update browser support matrix to reflect CSS Grid.
Fix bug 1520050: Remove User model custom managers (#1164)
Update to Django 1.11.18, r=me (#1166)

Fix bug 1433994 - Show an Ace editor for Fluent strings (#1162)

When the format of a string to translate is Fluent, render an Ace editor instead of a simple <textarea>. We use Ace as it is better supported with React, and Stas already wrote some plugins to go with it for the Fluent playground, plugins that we reuse here.

Fix bug 1492163 - Add support for RTL languages to Translate.Next. (#1165)

* Fix bug 1492163 - Add support for RTL languages to Translate.Next.

* Make locale.direction lower case, add clearfix from translation header.

Fix bug 1566869: Reset ignored state on unsavedchanges update (#1358)

Fix bug 1547274: Implement a 'nanoscopic' NProgress bar at the top (#1387)

Unlike in Translate.Current, where we show the progress bar for almost any AJAX call,
in Translate.Next we only show it when changes are made to a single translation,
i.e. on save, (un)approve, (un)reject and delete operations.

We already show different progress bars/loaders when searching or filtering entities,
switching resources or performing batch actions and there's no reason to duplicate them.

In fact, duplicating loaders might negatively impact perceived performance. So does
"extending" the progress bar in Translate.Current, which starts at Translation save
and ends only when Helper tabs end loading for the next entity.

We should however consider:

2. Removing existing loaders in the string list and using the combination of NProgress bar and content placeholder.

No bug - Allow changing files from volumes in docker. (#1502)

When creating containers with docker-compose, volumes containing the source code from the host are created. From inside a docker container, it was not possible to make changes in those volumes, because of a permission issue. This commit sets the GID of the pontoon group so that it matches what will, in most cases, be the group of the user in the host (1000). That allows to make changes inside volumes. Note that if a user has a different group GID (for example, 1001, because they are the second user created on the host) then this will not work. But most folks work on their personal computer so that should not happen too often, and I do not have a good solution for that anyway. This is strictly better than before.

Fix bug 1611666 - Prevent loss of letters while typing in the search input. (#1569)

There was a concurrency issue created by the fact that the search input content was being loaded from the URL params every time those changed. That meant that, if the user was typing at just the right time, they would 1. update the search state variable 2. trigger a search after a delay, which updates the URL 3. update the search state variable with a new letter 4. the search content gets set to the previous state because of the URL update, erasing the last letter the user typed. This patch fixes this problem by only updating the search state variable on mount or if it is empty in the new URL.

Fix bug 1633149: Detect changes to translated resources on sync (#1753)

When detecting changes to translated resources in VCS, we need to
identify which of the changed paths belongs to a localizable resource.

The logic that does that makes assumptions about the file and folder
structure which are not valid for projects using project configuration.

Hence this patch adds a new logic for such projects, which makes use of
the ProjectFiles matcher of the compare-locales library.

The logic also converts the changed paths to the canonical form for
representing resources used across Pontoon codebase (reference path
insted of l10n path) and assigns the list of changed locales to each
path.

This patch also fixes bug 1608045, which was another symptom of the
very same problem.

Fix bug 1688570: improve performance of initial editor change

Changing from/to initial textarea values would result in redundant
re-renders due to subscribing to `unsavedChangesExist` and
`unsavedChangesIgnored` redux state changes.

Implementation-wise, this accesses `unsavedchanges` state directly,
without subscribing to its changes because the state members are not
used for rendering purposes.

For direct store access react-redux strongly suggests to leverage the
`useStore()` API, because accessing the store via context is an
implementation detail and it might change in the future. That's why the
components connecting redux state -> props have been converted to hooks.

It'd also have been possible to avoid these intermediate components and
co-locate redux state directly within components, however that would
require more invasive changes, creeping the scope of this change
considerably.

Refs. https://react-redux.js.org/using-react-redux/accessing-store

Fix bug 1688573: reduce renundant re-renders caused by typing (#1854)

Because typing constantly updates `editor.translation`, the idea is to
subscribe to its changes as less as possible. When `editor.translation`
must inevitably be read but the data won't be used as-is but rather
derived into some other piece of data, the calculation is done behind a
selector to avoid extra re-renders.

Likewise, the `withDiff` HoC has been wrapped around `React.memo`,
because rendering a diff can take ~3ms, and with a higher number of
History/Helpers entries, rendering of every entry will otherwise be
considerably slower.

* style: Apply updated Prettier styles

If you need to rebase work past this style change, do as follows:

0. Consider this to be commit `commitA`, replacing that with its id in the following.
1. To make sure mistakes aren't fatal, assign a second branch to your current work.
2. Rebase your branch on the commit immediately before this one, commitA~
3. Run the following command at the root of the repo:

    git rebase --strategy-option=theirs \
      --exec 'npx prettier --write . && git add -u && git commit --amend --no-edit' \
      commitA

That will take a short while esp. if you have multiple commits,
as it runs Prettier on everything for every commit.
If you've deleted files, the rebase may drop down to interactive mode
and have you `git rm` as appropriate, then `git rebase --continue`.

You should end up with just your changes in your branch,
prettily formatted. To validate that,
apply the same Prettier config change to your original branch,
reformat the files with `npm run prettier`,
and then compare the results with the rebased branch.

Keep AutoML Translate latency low (#2659)

Fixes #2655.

The Google AutoML Translation has latency of ~15s caused by the loading time of a custom model into the chip. Since there
are replicas, the high tail latency occurs for first N requests - one replica may successfully load the model, but the
request may be routed to other replicas which are still loading. Once all replicas load the model, the normal latency
should be 200 - 500ms.

Also, since the chips are shared with other models, models gets evicted from the chips if they aren't used for a longer
period of time, resulting in high latency on the next following request.

To keep latency low, we need to make regular dummy warm-up requests using a management command, which needs to run at least every 10 minutes.

Optimize filters by introducing Resource.order (#3130)

String filters can be slow, especially because ordering entities by Resource.path is slow. It turns out that:
- Adding DB index to Resource.path doesn't bring performance gains.
- Sorting entities by any other Resource.field is fast.

The reason for slowness is probably that Resource.path can be a pretty long text field.

So we're now introducing Resource.order, which to represent the alphabetic order of resources in the project. We reorder resources when new resources are added to the project.

Update Term.entity after updating Term.text (#3133)

Problem:
When updating the Term.text, the associated entity was not correctly
updating to point to the newly created entity. This led to Term.entity
property still pointing to the previous, now obsolete entity.

Solution:
In the `create_entity()` method of the Term model, explicitly set the
term property of the associated entity to the current term instance
before saving it. This ensures that the entity is correctly associated
with the updated term instance.

Additionally, removed the `update_fields` argument from the
`entity.save()` call to ensure that all fields are properly saved,
including the `obsolete` flag if the entity is not newly created.

Changes:
- Added `entity.term = self` before updating the `entity_id` in the `create_entity()` method.
- Removed the `update_fields` argument from `entity.save()` call to ensure all fields are saved.

Use proper paging for entities (#3129)

We currently use a weird way of paginating entities - in each request we include a list of already loaded entities, which we exclude from the matching entities in Django and then return the first page of the remaining entities. This is a relic of the react-infinite-scroller library which we no longer use.

We should implement proper paging, i.e. drop exclude_entities and only return the relevant page.

That should also speed up loading of entities, because NOT IN DB queries tend to be slow and because less data will be transferred.

Speed up Project Notifications tab (#3146)

We make the Project Notifications tab faster by loading past Project Notifications
more efficiently. We do so by retrieving only one past project Notification per instance,
and by prefetching related Project and User data.

Each project notification is stored in one Notification instance per user. To
identify unique project Notifications, we now use the identifier stored in the
Notification.data field.

PostgreSQL allows us to retrieve Notifications with unique Notification.data
fields by combining .order_by(*fields) and .distinct(*fields) calls. Read more:
https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/3.2/ref/models/querysets/#distinct

That approach doesn't allow us to order Notifications by their timestamp, so
we have to do that with Python.

Speed up /notifications page (#3147)

1. Reduce the number of DB queries by prefetching all relevant data

2. Load /notifications page in two steps. Only load first 100 notifications initialiy, and then load any remaining notifications via AJAX. That makes the page usable much faster and improves perceived performance. By the time the user scrolls to the bottom of the page, the remaining notifications are likely to be loaded already.

Fix validation message on translation creation (#3151)

Prevent possible AttributeError when Entity or Locale validation fails.

Speed up permissions page (#3149)

1. Use simpler and faster DB query to retrieve team contributors. We now use direct DB query rather than the expensive `users_with_translations_counts()` function, which also collects data that we don't use (e.g. counts and roles).

2. Use direct DB query rather than more complex `Locale.project_permissions()` function to retrieve Project translators and contributors. The amount of data transmitted is greatly reduced by not rendering the contributors for projects without custom permissions. Previously, they were just hidden, but still rendered. Now they are copied to the Project-permission user selector widget from the General-permission widgets.

3. Drop unused extra parameter in ContributorSelectorList.

Do not exclude specific TM entries (#3154)

Each request to fetch Translation Memory matches excludes TM entries that belong to Translations that are Fuzzy or not-Approved.
That is not necessary, because we remove TM entries when translations get Unapproved, Rejected or become Fuzzy.
It could also speed up Translation Memory requests, because join with the Translation table is no longer needed.

Also included is a data migration to remove any legacy TM entries
that belong to Translations that are Fuzzy or not-Approved.

Use default Gunicorn worker timeout setting (#3293)

The Heroku router drops a long-running request after 30 seconds, but the dyno behind it
continues processing the request until completion.

Adding a timeout to the webserver ensures that the dyno itself drops the long-running request,
creating capacity for other requests.

A while ago the webserver timeout was set to 120 seconds, in order to potentially help
with long request like downloading TMX files via curl. It's not clear if this was actually
helpful, but it increases a chance of Applcation Errors under heavy load.

Refactor sync status logging (#3529)

Here, sync status logging is collapsed into a single table of events, which is written to only from sync_project_task(), with the following states:

* IN_PROGRESS
* DONE - sync complete, with some changes to DB or repo
* NO_CHANGES - sync complete, with no changed to DB or repo
* NO_COMMIT - sync complete, but commit=False was set while a repo write should've occurred
* PREV_BUSY - skipped due to previous sync still running
* FAIL - an exception was raised
* INCOMPLETE - sync never completed; set by a subsequent successful run

For FAIL, an error message is retained in the error field.

The logs are made available via the following views:

* /sync - latest sync status and start time for each project
* /sync/projects/<project> - sync events for each project
* /sync/errors - all anomalous sync events with a status other than DONE or NO_CHANGES

Old sync events are ported to the new format, setting the status as NO_CHANGES for all that were "skipped" and INCOMPLETE for ones with no end time set.

Also included:
* Do not clear ChangedEntityLocale during a sync with commit=False
* Add Sync Log menu entry to the Profile menu

Co-authored-by: Matjaž Horvat <matjaz.horvat@gmail.com>

Refactor stats, removing aggregate fields from project, projectlocale & locale (#3536)

Based on unscientific local testing, the rendering speed benefits from eagerly populating the aggregated stats into Project, ProjectLocale & Locale don't exist, compared to collating the data on the fly from TranslatedResource objects. Therefore, we should not be doing this complex extra work. This significantly simplifies the logic around stats updates, and makes the stats much easier to reason about.

The AggregatedStats class no longer extends Model, and it's mostly a crutch for reducing the risks in this change; hence its move from base/models/ to base/. With it, fields like total_strings and strings_with_errors will continue to work for the Django models from which the corresponding DB fields were removed.

Use MF2 syntax for plural gettext messages (#3635)

This is an intermediate step towards #3538, de-specializing gettext .po plural message handling.

Previous to this PR, each gettext plural message had its source plural form stored as Entity.string_plural, and for each target locale, each of its variants was separately translated, with Translation.plural_form indicating the variant identifier. These fields are not used by any other format, and they are removed from the database in this change.

To represent plural source and target messages, Unicode MessageFormat (MF2) syntax representation is now used internally for all gettext messages, but this is never revealed to users. Placeholders like {0} or %(type)s are not parsed as such, but treated as a literal part of the string.

The translator front-end is modified to use the "rich editor" also for gettext plurals; this was previously only used by Fluent messages with variants. The FTL source view is not enabled for gettext plurals.

Also:
* Drop unused Locale.cldr_* methods + simplify & fix what remains. Previously, Locale.cldr_plurals_list() would return ['one'] if cldr_plurals was empty. This is clearly wrong, and it now returns ['other'].
* Disable pretranslation for plural gettext messages (see #3694)

Skip GAR tag and push on forks in Docker Build (#4233)

The "Tag image for GAR" and "Push Docker image to GAR" steps depend on
the GCP_PROJECT_ID repository variable, which only exists on
mozilla/pontoon. On forks the variable is empty, so the constructed tag
becomes "us-docker.pkg.dev//pontoon-prod/..." and the step fails with
"is not a valid repository/tag: invalid reference format", producing
failed workflow runs and notification emails on every fork.

Guard both steps with github.repository == 'mozilla/pontoon' so they
run only on the upstream repo. Forks still build the image (validating
the Dockerfile) but skip tagging and pushing.

Multi-value entries, i.e. Fluent messages with attributes or selectors, had no Machinery entry that filled every field at once: each leaf got its own TM or MT match, and translators copied them one by one.

Add automatic LLM-generated suggestions Machinery (pilot) (#4394)

Until now the LLM was pull-based: the translator opened the AI dropdown
on the Google Translate row and picked an option, and the result replaced
that row's text in place.

The suggestion is now generated automatically and shown as a row of its
own. It is limited to strings without an approved translation, to
authenticated users, and to the locales listed in
OPENAI_AUTO_SUGGESTION_LOCALES, so that spend stays bounded while the
approach is evaluated.

The AI dropdown is unchanged and keeps working in every locale.

To support evaluation, the endpoint logs duration, cache hit and token
counts, and copies from Machinery are logged for every source. The two
are needed together: machinery_sources only records a source when the
suggestion is saved unedited, and a cached response costs nothing but
still counts as a suggestion shown.

OpenAIService now takes references as a dict[str, list[str]] rather
than a single machine translation, so that the reference can later be
dropped, or extended with other Machinery results, without changing the
request shape. A single reference renders exactly as before, leaving the
prompt untouched for every caller that exists today. The cache key now
contains model version and prompt

"gpt-transform" / "OpenAI" / "LLM" code references are now consolidated as 
"OpenAI ChatGPT" to make them consistent with other Machinery sources.

Includes a data migration, so historical `machinery_sources` attributions are
rewritten rather than left under the old name.
Compare translations on .value & .properties during sync (#4402)
Don't warn when leaving an autofilled translation (100% TM match) (#4410)
Fix a typo in notifications.md (#4415)

Name catchall plural variants after target locale (#4405)

Pretranslation expands a plural selector to the target locale's
categories, but left the catchall carrying the source's name, e.g.
`other` from en-US. For a locale whose last category is not `other` (uk,
ru, pl, be) that puts the variants out of sync with the plural fields in
the editor.

Move the 100% match indicator into the editor menu (#4413)

The indicator pushed the menu down by its own height on every string
that had a perfect match, and let it back up on every string that didn't.
Moving between such strings made the menu jump, which #4410 made worse by
removing the confirmation dialog that used to slow that movement down.

Show it next to the translation length instead.

Autofill editor from composed Machinery matches (#4417)

Expand autofilling of untranslated string editor with a perfect TM match to
composed (multi-field) Machinery suggestions. Composed Machinery suggestions
are perfect matches only when every one of its fields comes from TM.

Show the match indicator in the source view too

404 when resource path in the URL path doesn't exist (#4409)

* 404 when resource path in the URL path doesn't exist

The translate view validated the locale, the project and the
ProjectLocale, but took the resource straight from the URL. A path that
the locale has no resource for rendered the view with the path in the
navigation and an empty string list, which reads as an empty resource
rather than as a wrong URL.

Require the path to name a resource the locale has a TranslatedResource
for, unless it is `all-resources` — the same set the paths menu offers. A
resource that is obsolete is a 404 too, and so is one belonging to a
locale still waiting for its first sync, which has nothing to translate..

* 404 on a path in the All Projects view, too

And only allow "all-resources" as the valid path for "all-projects",
because nothing links to a path in that view, and because resource
paths are not unique across projects.

Serve system projects to translate endpoints (#4408)

The History, Comments, Locales and Sibling strings endpoints looked the
entity up in `Project.objects.visible()`, which is
`available().filter(system_project=False)`. The tutorial is a system
project, so all four returned 404 for every user, and the panels showed
nothing rather than reporting a failure.

What these endpoints need to know is whether the user can reach the
project, not whether it is listed on the dashboards. `available()` still
excludes disabled and resource-less projects, and `visible_for` still
hides private ones from non-superusers.

Fix copying translations naming its plural catchall after the source into the editor (#4407)

Check translator rights per string in All Projects (#4412)

Don't let one failed entity abort pretranslation (#4406)

A pretranslation is serialized with Fluent syntax escaping off, so a TM
or MT result carrying an unescaped brace produces a string that
`parse_source_string_to_json` rejects with "Source is not a Fluent
entry". That call was unguarded, unlike the `get_pretranslation` calls
above it, so a single entity ended the whole project's pretranslation,
which surfaced as a sync failure and left the remaining locales
unpretranslated.

Skip the entity instead, and name the entity and locale in all three
log messages.

Write resources without fetch, using data model fields (#4391)

* Update to moz-l10n 0.14.1
* Write resources using only database data
* Use Translation.value & .properties for serialization
* Download translated resources directly
* Send files as text/plain, not zipped
* Only allow downloads for active Project + Resource + TranslatedResource files
Set initial value for hidden "sources" radio button in /admin (#4440)

Fix tutorial entity values (#4446)

Fixes #4445.

Similar to the regression with terminology fixed in 6727ff3, the same
problem affected the tutorial project in which `entity.value`s were not
populated.

We add a new data migration to backfill tutorial project's
`entity.value` rows from `entity.string`.

casos.name: v2.167.0
casos.body: # node-opcua Release Notes: v2.165.1 → v2.167.0 ## v2.167.0 ### ✨ Features - **server-config**: Accept certificate chain in `TrustListClient.addCertificate` — enables full chain trust management via the GDS push model [135902c] - - **core**: Thread `ISessionContext` through `ApplyChanges` event chain — allows consumers to identify which session triggered a configuration change [4033f97] ### 🐛 Bug Fixes - **server**: Harden `register_server_manager` against null/missing values [95b5aa5] - **server**: Use explicit length check for certificate chain instead of truthiness guard — prevents edge cases with empty arrays [ef3f04e] - **core**: Harden certificate validation and fix `Certificate[]` migration [d276591] - **core**: Resolve `tsc --noEmit` errors in node-opcua-end2end-test test suite [e34bbb1] ### 🔧 Refactor - **server-config**: Self-contained test certificates — tests no longer depend on external PKI state [13f310f] --- ## v2.166.1 ### 🐛 Bug Fixes - **client**: Fix "Callback was already called" race condition during connection abort — prevents double-callback crash when a connection is terminated mid-handshake [c487bf5] ### 🧹 Chores - Update `node-opcua-pki` / `node-opcua-crypto` dependencies [713f852] --- ## v2.166.0 ### 🐛 Bug Fixes - **secure-channel**: Add TTL eviction to nonce cache — prevents unbounded memory growth on long-lived servers with many reconnections [b82c293] - **server**: Add nonce verification to `UserNameIdentityToken` password extraction — hardens against replay attacks [c6b0573] ### 🧹 Chores - Minor fixes [e4c3c87] - Update packages [6ac3120] ### ⚠️ Security - **Nonce verification for password tokens** [c6b0573]: The server now verifies that the nonce embedded in `UserNameIdentityToken` matches the nonce issued during `CreateSession`. This is a security hardening measure that protects against credential replay attacks. - **Nonce cache TTL eviction** [b82c293]: Stale entries in the secure-channel nonce cache are now evicted after a configurable TTL, preventing memory exhaustion on servers handling many short-lived client connections. --- ## v2.165.2 ### 🧹 Chores - Update packages — support for OpenSSL > 3.5 [e625c48] --- ## Test Fixes (across versions) - Fix hardcoded namespace index in AddIn instantiation test [25ab1b6] - Fix chained certificate test to expect success instead of failure [c0f5f35] ## Upgrade Notes > [!TIP] > **OpenSSL 3.5+ support**: v2.165.2+ includes updated `node-opcua-pki` and `node-opcua-crypto` packages that are compatible with OpenSSL 3.5+. If you were seeing crypto-related errors on newer Node.js builds, this update resolves them. > [!NOTE] > **Certificate chain support**: If you use GDS push certificate management, `TrustListClient.addCertificate` now correctly handles full certificate chains (not just leaf certificates). No API changes required — existing code continues to work.
mensagens_commits: chore: update packages (support for openssl >3.5)
chore: minor fixes

fix(server): add nonce verification to UserNameIdentityToken
password extraction

After RSA-decrypting the UserNameIdentityToken password
blob, the server now verifies that the trailing bytes
match the session's serverNonce.

Refactored the password extraction logic into a standalone
pure function `extractPasswordFromDecryptedBlob` for
testability. Added unit tests.

fix(secure-channel): add TTL eviction to nonce cache

The process-global nonce store grew without bound because
entries were never removed. Replaced unbounded plain object
with a Map that has lazy TTL-based eviction (4 hours) and a
maxSize cap (50,000 entries) with oldest-first eviction.

Extracted nonce tracking into `nonce_cache.ts` module.
Public API preserved via re-exports. Added unit tests.
chore: update packages
chore: update node-opcua-pki/crypto

feat: thread ISessionContext through ApplyChanges
event chain

Pass the optional ISessionContext from the OPC UA
method handler through the entire ApplyChanges call
chain so that applyChangesCompleted event listeners
can access the provisioning client's certificate and
application URI.

Changes:
- push_certificate_manager.ts: add optional
  ISessionContext param to applyChanges() interface
- push_certificate_manager_server_impl.ts: forward
  context and update event type signature
- apply_changes.ts: accept context and emit it with
  applyChangesCompleted event
- push_certificate_manager_helpers.ts: pass context
  from _applyChanges handler to applyChanges()

All changes are backward-compatible — the context
parameter is optional everywhere.

fix(client): Fix Callback was already called race condition during connection abort

Wrapped the callback inside ClientSecureChannelLayer.create to prevent the backoff module and concurrent socket events from executing the async.series callback multiple times when abortConnection is triggered.

test(address-space): Fix hardcoded namespace index in AddIn instantiation test

Removed the hardcoded namespace index '2' from getChildByName calls in test_object_instantiate_with_addin.ts. When an AddIn is instantiated into a different namespace, its browseName correctly reflects the instance namespace, causing the strict index lookup to return null and crash the test suite.

fix: harden certificate validation and fix Certificate[] migration

- addCertificate: pass combined DER chain (combine_der) for
  CA-signed certificates so full chain validation works
- verificationStatusToStatusCode: add missing mappings for
  BadCertificateRevocationUnknown and
  BadCertificateIssuerRevocationUnknown to prevent silent
  fallthrough to BadCertificateInvalid
- test CertificateManagers: set ignoreMissingRevocationList
  to true since test environments have no CRLs loaded
- test_server_endpoint: fix Certificate[] migration - pass
  empty array instead of Buffer.alloc(0) to match the
  migrated type signature
- configurator.ts: fix addCertificate call to use
  combine_der() and clean up duplicate imports
- fake_certificate_authority: use unique directory per
  invocation to prevent private key reuse

﻿fix: resolve tsc --noEmit errors in node-opcua-end2end-test test suite

Replace optional chaining with non-null assertions
and add null-coalescing operators across end-to-end
test files to fix TS18048, TS2322, TS2532, TS2454.

Key changes:
- Fix possibly undefined monitoredItems map results
  with ?? [] in deadband, ctt018, monitoring, and
  set_triggering tests
- Fix possibly undefined notification data and
  monitored items access in SubscriptionUseCase and
  ResendData tests
- Fix browse path target access in session
  diagnostics and security diagnostics tests
- Fix session diagnostics count comparisons
- Add definite assignment assertion for callback
  variable in test_issue_1344
- Fix addressSpace/namespace access in subscription
  setup blocks

﻿fix(server): use explicit length check for certificate
chain instead of truthiness guard

serverCertificateChain is typed as Certificate[] which is
always truthy, even when empty. The old truthiness guard
would let an empty [] through to combine_der, silently
producing a zero-length (invalid) certificate buffer.

Replace the guard with .length > 0 so that an empty chain
correctly yields undefined instead of a bogus empty buffer.

Also remove redundant runtime asserts in
_makeEndpointDescription (types already enforce these
constraints) and apply biome formatting fixes.

﻿fix(server): harden register_server_manager against
null/missing values

- Replace non-null assertions (!) with nullish
  coalescing (??) or proper guards to satisfy biome
  noNonNullAssertion rule
- Guard selectedEndpoint.endpointUrl with an explicit
  throw instead of silently falling back to empty
  string, which would hide configuration bugs
- Add explicit null guard for this.server before use
- Simplify selectedEndpoint assignment after endpoint
  discovery
- Remove redundant assert after if-check

﻿test(e2e): fix chained certificate test to expect
success instead of failure

The second test was written to pass only when the
secure connection fails, locking in the buggy behavior
where the server couldn't extract the CA from the
client's chained certificate. Update the test to expect
success: a server in configuration mode should accept
the connection.

Also add CA issuer + CRL to the client certificate
manager so the client can verify the server's
certificate chain (without this the client rejects
with BadCertificateChainIncomplete).

Both tests now pass (2 passing, 0 failing).

feat(server-config): accept certificate chain in
TrustListClient.addCertificate

Update addCertificate to accept Certificate | Certificate[]
instead of a single Certificate. When an array is provided,
it is combined into a composite DER buffer using combine_der
before being sent to the server.

- Return BadInvalidArgument for empty certificate arrays
- Update test to pass full certificate chain via combine_der
- Add missing file existence assertion in test

refactor(server-config): self-contained test certificates

Replace external certificate file dependencies with on-the-fly
certificate generation in test_server_configuration.ts.

The test suite previously depended on certificate files from
node-opcua-samples/certificates/ generated by the `prepare`
build step, causing CI/CD failures when these files were
missing.

Changes:
- Generate test certificates at startup using existing helpers
  (produceCertificateAndPrivateKey, produceSignedCertificateChain)
- Add produceSignedCertificateChain() helper to create CA-signed
  certificate chains using readCertificateSigningRequest
- Remove imports: fs, fileURLToPath, assert,
  readCertificateChainAsync
- Remove sampleCertificateFolder, sampleCert2048,
  sampleSelfSignedCert2048, sampleSelfSignedCert1024 constants
- Replace assert() calls with should.exist() + type guards
- Extract shared helpers to eliminate duplicated boilerplate:
  getDefaultTrustList, makeTrustListData,
  preloadIssuerCertificates, makeUnsecureSession,
  makeRestrictedServer
- Move installPushCertificateManagement into beforeEach

All 128 tests pass without requiring the prepare build step.

casos.name: v2.168.0: The Response That Kept Responding
casos.body:
# Release Notes - v2.168.0

**TL;DR:** 

Version 2.168.0 is a stability and performance release. It fixes a infinite recursion bug in response handling (#1490), fully migrates core packages from `async`/`lodash` to native modern JavaScript patterns, and introduces a more robust typed event system and certificate management architecture.

--- 
## ✨Features

- **Server**: Added `channelSecured` event for post-handshake notifications [af7ef3419].

## 🐛Bug Fixes

- **Core**: Prevented infinite recursion in `send_response` when chunking fails (#1490) [51ef025bc].
- **Secure Channel**: Implemented fallback to the latest valid token when a request's token expires [ae65dea32].
- **Server**: Deferred channel shutdown until after the `ApplyChanges` response is sent [8484b9853].
- **Address Space**: Fixed `address-space-base` imports and applied security hardening [d636f0cc3].
- **Maintenance**: Resolved various TypeScript and Biome violations across the codebase [16302c4be, 45a14062b, 887a42d3f, 1372b5cbb].
- **Tests**: Hardened server shutdown tests [c834243a0], added TokenStack fallback coverage [823f38d5c], and increased T73 secure channel renewal token lifetime to reduce flakiness [a13bbb014].

## 🔧 Refactoring & Improvements

- **Performance**: Replaced `async` library [3269940ac] and `lodash` [b99520d09] with native async/await, Promises, and targeted alternatives.
- **Type Safety**: Unified certificate chain providers [49b8736a4] and implemented typed `EventEmitter<T>` patterns for server events [1f7040e4b].
- **Structure**: Split conformance testing into focused modules [e4c5eb978] and cleaned up the address space conformance package [168a8f624].
- **Transport**: Enhanced type safety and removed unsafe patterns in the transport layer [785d89fa1].
- **Security**: Simplified push certificate management [dab64e9f5].
- **Debugability**: Internal channel callbacks are now hidden from the debugger for a cleaner debugging experience [e0d2b40a9].
- **Testing Infrastructure**: Hardened leak detector for Mocha 12 and tsx [c7170e507].

## 🧹 Chores

- Updated Biome formatting [465eb93a5] and fixed misused Mocha timeout configurations [eac92cc02].

---

## 👬🏽  Contributors

* Special thanks to @RatishKashyap of [#1490](https://github.com/node-opcua/node-opcua/issues/1490) for their detailed report

## What's Changed
* Refactor server by @erossignon in https://github.com/node-opcua/node-opcua/pull/1491
**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/node-opcua/node-opcua/compare/v2.167.0...v2.168.0
mensagens_commits:
﻿refactor: unified certificate chain provider for endpoints

Replace the dual-path certificate management (static copy vs
monkey-patched disk reader) with a pluggable
ICertificateChainProvider interface.

Architecture:
- ICertificateChainProvider extends ICertificateKeyPairProvider
  with invalidate() method
- StaticCertificateChainProvider: in-memory chain with #fields
- SecretHolder: now implements ICertificateChainProvider
  (added invalidate() alias for dispose())
- OPCUAServerEndPoint uses #certProvider and #combinedDerCache
- EndpointDescription.serverCertificate is always a dynamic
  getter via Object.defineProperty
- Default endpoint provider is SecretHolder (disk-backed),
  enabling runtime cert rotation without push cert management

DRY improvements:
- Eliminated DiskCertificateChainProvider (duplicated
  SecretHolder)
- Added invalidateServerCertificateCache() utility function
- Extracted CERT_PEM_RELATIVE_PATH constant
- Modernized __defineGetter__ to Object.defineProperty

Security:
- All cert/key caches use ES # private fields
- toJSON() and inspect overrides prevent secret leakage

File rename:
- install_push_certitifate_management.ts ->
  install_push_certificate_management.ts (typo fix)

New files:
- invalidate_server_certificate_cache.ts
- test_certificate_rotation.ts
- certificate_rotation_demo.ts (playground)

Tests: 20/20 server, 43/43 server-config, 198/198 GDS
chore: fix biome formatting

﻿refactor: simplify push cert management and fix issues

- Pass server object directly to SecretHolder (via

ew SecretHolder(this)) so endpoints follow
  Object.defineProperty redirects automatically.
  Documented harmless cyclic ref (V8 mark-and-sweep,
  endpoint.dispose() breaks it).

- Delete endpoint replacement loop and
  createCertManagerSecretHolder() — no longer needed.

- Delegate initial cert creation to base server's
  createDefaultCertificate() instead of duplicating
  inferior logic (was missing DNS hostnames,
  configured IPs, proper subject via makeSubject(),
  mutex locking).

- Fix fire-and-forget setTimeout in onCertificateChange:
  replaced with awaited delay so action queue properly
  waits for channel shutdown and endpoint resumption.

- Add enumerable: true on Object.defineProperty calls
  to preserve original property visibility.

- Make createDefaultCertificate() public on
  OPCUABaseServer (needed by push cert management).

- Fix missing space in error message.

Tests: 20/20 server, 43/43 server-configuration

﻿refactor: hide internal channel callbacks from debugger

- Replace _unpreregisterChannelEvent monkey-patch with a
  module-scoped WeakMap (preregisterAbortListeners).
  Eliminates the ServerSecureChannelLayerPriv interface
  and unsafe type casts.

- Convert _on_response public field to #onResponse private
  field with setResponseInterceptor() setter method.

- Move response interceptor installation from on_request()
  (per-request) to _on_new_channel (once per channel).

Both changes make internal state invisible to debuggers
and external code.

Tests: 20/20 server, 43/43 server-configuration

﻿feat: add channelSecured event for post-handshake notifications

The existing "newChannel" event fires after transport init
(HEL/ACK) but BEFORE the OpenSecureChannel handshake, so
securityPolicy, securityMode, and clientCertificate are not
yet available.

Add a new "channelSecured" event that fires after the
OpenSecureChannel handshake succeeds:

- ServerSecureChannelLayer: emit "open" when #status
  transitions to "open" after successful handshake
- OPCUAServerEndPoint: forward channel "open" as
  "channelSecured" event
- OPCUABaseServer: forward endpoint "channelSecured"
  to server level, install response interceptor here
  (after handshake) instead of at newChannel time
- OPCUAServer: add TypeScript event overload with docs

Usage:
  server.on("channelSecured", (channel, endpoint) => {
    // channel.securityPolicy and securityMode are
    // available here
  });

Tests: 20/20 server

﻿refactor: use typed EventEmitter<T> pattern for server events

Replace individual on() overloads on OPCUAServer with a typed
OPCUAServerEvents interface, using the same EventEmitter<T>
pattern as ClientSecureChannelLayer.

- Add OPCUABaseServerEvents interface in base_server.ts for
  events emitted by the base class (request, response,
  newChannel, channelSecured, closeChannel, etc.)
- Add OPCUAServerEvents interface in opcua_server.ts extending
  the base events with session and registration events
- Thread the generic through OPCUABaseServer<T> and
  OPCUASecureObject<T>
- Fix session_closed event arg type (was string, now boolean)
- Fix session_activated to include UserIdentityToken arg
- Remove ~94 lines of on() overload boilerplate

Tests: 20/20 server, 43/43 server-configuration

﻿fix: defer channel shutdown after ApplyChanges response

The OPC UA ApplyChanges method was synchronously awaiting
shutdownChannels() inside the CertificateChanged action
queue, which destroyed the admin client's own channel
before the method response could be sent.

Fix: move channel teardown + endpoint resumption to the
applyChangesCompleted event, scheduled via setImmediate()
so the method response is delivered first.

Also fix session_closed event signature in sample servers
(was string, should be boolean per the actual emit).

Tests: 5/5 push-cert, 43/43 server-configuration

fix: resolve TS2345/TS2339 errors in test type checks

- Remove `constructor: ConstructorFunc` from IExtensionObject
  interface in encode_decode_round_trip_test.ts, since
  TypeScript types all class constructor properties as
  `Function` which is incompatible with specific constructor
  signatures. Cast at the single usage site instead.
- Cast encode_decode_round_trip_test() return values to
  `Variant` in test_variant.ts where `.value` is accessed.
- Cast return value to explicit typed object in
  test_factory_registerObject.ts for Person properties.
- Fix session_closed event handler signature in
  build_server_with_temperature_device.ts.
- Remove invalid connectionError event listener in
  test_dos_attack test.

fix: prevent infinite recursion in send_response (#1490)

When `chunkSecureMessage` returns a bad StatusCode (e.g.
BadTcpMessageTooLarge or missing derived keys), `send_response`
tries to send a `ServiceFault` by calling itself recursively.
If the ServiceFault also fails to chunk (same root cause), the
recursion never terminates, causing:

  RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded

This was observed in production when `#_get_security_options_for_MSG`
returned null due to missing `derivedKeys`, causing every subsequent
`chunkSecureMessage` call to fail identically.

Fix: before recursing, check whether the response is already a
`ServiceFault`. If so, do not recurse — log the error and invoke
the callback with an Error instead. This limits `send_response`
to at most 2 calls (original response + one ServiceFault retry).

Added a reproduction test that stubs the chunker to always fail
and verifies the recursion guard works correctly.

Closes #1490

refactor: replace lodash with targeted alternatives

- Replace `lodash.isEqual` with `node:util.isDeepStrictEqual`
  in node-opcua-address-space and node-opcua-variant
  (zero-dependency, built into Node.js)
- Replace `lodash.partition` and `lodash.sortBy` with
  standalone `lodash.partition` and `lodash.sortby` packages
  in node-opcua-server
- Remove full `lodash` and `@types/lodash` dependencies from
  node-opcua-address-space, node-opcua-server,
  node-opcua-variant and root package.json
- Remove `underscore` and `@types/underscore` from
  node-opcua-variant
- Apply biome lint fixes: `Object.hasOwn()` over
  `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call()`,  template
  literals, `Number.isFinite()`, `2 ** 31`, prefix unused
  params with `_`, remove empty constructors, use `node:`
  protocol for built-in imports

fix(secure-channel): fall back to latest valid token
when request's token expires

When send_response needs to sign a response but the token from
the original request has expired (getTokenDerivedKeys returns
null), fall back to the most recent valid token in the stack.

This is the OPC UA-compliant behavior per Part 6 §6.7.3:
"Servers should use the existing SecurityToken to secure
outgoing Messages until the SecurityToken expires or the
Server receives a Message secured with a new SecurityToken."

This primarily affects PublishRequests, which can sit queued
for long periods waiting for subscription notifications. By
the time the PublishResponse is sent, the original request's
security token may have expired (125% lifetime threshold).

Changes:
- token_stack.ts: add getLatestTokenDerivedKeys() method
  that returns the newest non-expired token's derived keys
- server_secure_channel_layer.ts: update
  #_get_security_options_for_MSG to fall back to the latest
  valid token instead of returning null when the request's
  token has expired

test(secure-channel): add TokenStack fallback coverage

Verifies that when a request's token T1 expires beyond 125%
lifetime, getLatestTokenDerivedKeys falls back to the
newer token T2's keys. Covers:
 - valid token lookup
 - expired token returns null
 - newest valid token selection
 - full PublishRequest pipeline scenario (T1->T2 fallback)
 - all-tokens-expired returns null
 - removeOldTokens purges only expired tokens

fix: remove explicit any and fix biome/tsc violations

- server_subscription: replace __defineGetter__ with
  Object.defineProperty, type filter param, timerId,
  err casts, and add publishEngine null guard
- i_server_side_publish_engine: type TransferredSubscription
  fields (SequenceNumberGenerator, IServerSidePublishEngine),
  replace assert+non-null with proper guards
- server_secure_channel_layer: fix close event handler
  signature (Error|null vs Error|undefined), guard
  securityPolicy before getCryptoFactory
- test_token_stack_fallback: fix imports from dist/ to
  source/ for tsc --noEmit
- test_monitored_item: replace all any casts with explicit
  types and Mocha.Context
- test_server_engine: fix Float64Arrany typo, use
  Array.from for typed array comparison
- test_server_engine_add_method: fix invalid ?? throw
  syntax, add proper null guards
- test_server_publish_engine: make property helper generic
- helper_fake_publish_engine: replace any with unknown,
  prefix unused params
- typedarray_helpers: refactor to accept ArrayLike<unknown>
  natively, eliminating need for Array.from at call sites
- encode_decode_round_trip_test: update to ArrayLike cast

refactor: replace async library with native async/await and Promise patterns

- client_secure_channel_layer.ts: replace async.series with Promise chain for
  abortConnection
- client_publish_engine_reconnection.ts: replace async.whilst and async.forEachOf
  with native while/for...of loops
- reconnection.ts: replace async.series, async.forEach, and async.map with
  async/await and Promise-based patterns
- client_base_impl.ts: replace 2x async.series and async.map with Promise
  chains for findEndpoint, _internal_create_secure_channel, and
  _close_pending_sessions
- base_server.ts: replace 4x async.forEach with Promise.all for shutdown,
  shutdownChannels, suspendEndPoints, and resumeEndPoints
- server_engine.ts: replace async.map with
  Promise.all for refreshValues

Remove async dependency from node-opcua-client, node-opcua-server, and
node-opcua-secure-channel package.json.
Keep async in node-opcua-client-crawler (uses async.queue).

fix: harden server shutdown test and clean up findServers return types

- test_server_shutdown: fix race condition where
  shutdown notifications were lost before the
  client received them. Start shutdown without
  awaiting, poll for expected spy call counts
  during the grace period, then complete shutdown.
  Use greaterThanOrEqual for call count assertions.
- client_base_impl: clean up findServers and
  findServersOnNetwork return types, remove
  redundant return void 0, use explicit
  return undefined for noImplicitReturns.

refactor: clean up address_space_for_conformance_testing

- Replace all noExplicitAny violations with proper
  types (Record<string, unknown>, keyof typeof, etc.)
- Remove dead _setImage2 callback-based function
  (superseded by async setImage)
- Remove dangling variable references that served
  no purpose (nodes registered via side effects)
- Type function parameters with unknown instead of
  any for stricter type safety
- Remove unused DataValue import
- Type build_address_space_for_conformance_testing
  options parameter properly

refactor: split conformance testing into focused modules

Split the 1500+ line monolithic
address_space_for_conformance_testing.ts into 14 focused
sub-modules in a conformance_testing/ directory:

- helpers.ts: shared validators, random generators,
  variant construction, generic variable helpers
- type_defaults.ts: typeAndDefaultValue lookup table
- access_right_variables.ts: data-driven access levels
  (7 identical calls -> config array + loop)
- simulation_variables.ts: dynamic timer-based vars
- static_variables.ts: scalar/array/multidim + images
- mass_variables.ts: 100 items per data type
- analog_data_items.ts: DataItem/AnalogDataItem nodes
- discrete_variables.ts: TwoState/MultiState combined
  (5 identical calls -> loop)
- object_with_methods.ts: MethodNoArgs/IO/I/O
- enumeration_variable.ts: enum type + variable
- trigger_nodes.ts: event-raising nodes
- sample_view.ts: sample views
- node_with_references.ts: reference test nodes
  (IIFEs replaced with block scoping)
- path_and_large_arrays.ts: 10-deep path + large arrays

The main file is now a thin orchestrator (~85 lines).
Public API (build_address_space_for_conformance_testing)
is unchanged.

refactor(leak-detector): harden for mocha 12 + tsx

Refactored ResourceLeakDetector for mocha 12 compatibility
and biome conformance.

Root cause: tsx (TypeScript loader), when loaded via mocha
--require, refs stdout/stderr WriteStream handles. After
tests complete, these ref'd handles keep the event loop
alive. Mocha 12 no longer calls process.exit(), so the
process hangs indefinitely.

Fix: schedule process.exit() on an unref'd timer in stop().
start() cancels any pending exit timer from a previous
stop(), so multi-file and multi-block runs complete fully.
The timer only fires if something (tsx-ref'd stdout) keeps
the loop alive after all tests finish.

Changes:
- Lightweight setTimeout/setInterval tracking via Set +
  callback wrapping (auto-removes on natural fire)
- start() cancels pending exit timer from previous stop()
- Comprehensive in-process test suite (timers, handles,
  registry, multi-block, tsx proof)
- Subprocess integration tests spawning real mocha processes
  to verify: pass/fail exit codes, leak warnings, multi-file
  completion, tsx support, leaked sockets/fds/intervals/
  registry objects
- Added .mocharc.yml with tsx support
- Switched to mocha 12.0.0-beta-9.2 in root package.json

fix(e2e): increase T73 secure channel renewal token
lifetime from 200/250ms to 500ms

The 250ms token lifetime was too tight under load — the
server watchdog fired at 312ms, before the client renewal
round-trip could complete. Increasing to 500ms gives enough
headroom while still testing fast renewals (3+ renewals
within the test).

- address-space: biome conformance fixes, import ordering,
  non-null assertion replacements
- namespace_impl: fix TypeScript strict null checks
- u_test_e2e_issue_73: increase token lifetime from

- Replaced addFolder options: any with typed interface
- Added defensive default case in server secure channel
  #_prepare_response_security_header switch to reject
  unknown securityMode values (prevents DoS from
  malformed clients)
- certificate_rotation_demo: moved client.disconnect()
  to finally block, added try/catch in rotation timer
refactor(transport): cleanup type safety and remove unsafe patterns

fix: misc cleanup across address-space, secure-channel and server

- namespace_impl: handle numeric nodeId in toNodeId()
- namespace_impl: addYArrayItem infers dataType from value
  variant when not explicitly provided
- server_secure_channel_layer: add missing break in
  switch statement
- test_subscription: replace new Date().getTime() with
  Date.now(), extract makeSubscription helper
