Add memory-efficient tiled inference with spline blending and D4 TTA (#603)

* Add memory-efficient tiled inference with spline blending and D4 TTA

Implement a generic inference module (geoai/inference.py) for running
any PyTorch segmentation or regression model on large GeoTIFF rasters
with smooth tile blending and optional test-time augmentation.

Key features:
- Windowed rasterio I/O to avoid loading full input images into memory
- Four blending strategies (none, linear, cosine, spline) via BlendMode enum
- D4 dihedral group test-time augmentation (8-fold) for improved predictions
- Configurable pre/post-processing hooks for model-specific normalization
- Preserves GeoTIFF metadata (CRS, transform, nodata)

Closes #87

* Fix multi-class normalization bug and add output shape validation

- Fix critical bug: weight normalization crashed when num_classes > 1
  due to boolean index shape mismatch. Replace with np.where broadcast.
- Add model output shape validation on first batch to catch mismatched
  num_classes early with a clear error message.
- Handle models returning (B, H, W) by auto-expanding to (B, 1, H, W).
- Avoid reopening input raster; capture profile inside first with block.
- Add tests for multi-class normalization and zero-weight nodata.

* Fix spline weight mask and use deterministic demo models

- Spline blend now tapers only in overlap zones (flat plateau in center),
  matching linear/cosine behavior
- Replace random-weight demo models with fixed Sobel/directional kernels
  that produce spatially varying output for visible blending comparison

- Replace demo models with deterministic designs using global average

Dependabot branches live in this repository, so the existing fork guard
passes, but GitHub withholds repository secrets from Dependabot-triggered
runs. PREVIEW_DEPLOY_TOKEN is empty and the push to pages-preview fails
with "Invalid username or token". Guard on pull_request.user so the skip
also holds when a maintainer re-runs the job by hand, and mirror it in

Refactor claude-code-review.yml for improved security (#878)

Updated Claude code review workflow to enhance security and functionality.

ci: allow the Claude review workflow to check out fork PR heads (#879)

actions/checkout v7 refuses to check out fork PR code from a
pull_request_target workflow unless `allow-unsafe-pr-checkout` is set, so
since the v6 -> v7 bump in #863 the `claude-review` check has failed at the
checkout step on every PR opened from a fork:

    Refusing to check out fork pull request code from a
    'pull_request_target' workflow.

That is the population the review is most valuable for, and it fails before
Claude ever runs.

The guardrail targets "pwn request" vulnerabilities, where a fork's code is
*executed* with the base repo's token and secrets. This job never executes
the checked-out tree: it installs no dependencies, runs no build/test/linter,
uses no setup-* action, and Claude has no Bash tool (the action's subprocess
env scrub is documented at the top of the file). The head is on disk purely
so Read/Grep/Glob see the proposed file contents. Combined with
`persist-credentials: false`, the fork controls bytes Claude reads, not code
the runner runs — which is what the opt-in exists for.

Documented the reasoning inline, including the condition that would make the
opt-in unsafe: if any step is ever added that executes the checked-out tree,
this flag must be removed and that step moved to a `pull_request` workflow.

fix: avoid memory leaks caused by Thread.inheritedAccessControlContext

Thread.inheritedAccessControlContext inherits the caller ProtectionDomain, thus
it effectively holds its classloader.
There's no way to "unset inheritedAccessControlContext".

For Java 11+ use java.lang.ref.Cleaner-based approach via multi-release jar

We workaround that by going for ForkJoinPool + ManagedBlocker so it is JDK
that creates a thread, thus it should have no inheritedAccessControlContext.

The logic is as follows:
1) ForkJoinPool task runs on CPU and it processes the queue
2) If the queue is empty, the blocking call delegates to ManagedBlocker

It fits nice with FJP: CPU tasks do not create extra threads, and blocking
queue operations do not starve FJP CPU threads.

See https://stackoverflow.com/questions/78163385/does-postgres-jdbc-lazycleaner-cause-a-classloader-memory-leak/79835942

fix: make all Calendar instances proleptic Gregorian (#3837) (#3887)

* * fix: make all Calendar instances proleptic Gregorian (#3837)

Calendar instances created with Calendar.getInstance() or new GregorianCalendar() are by default a hybrid of the Julian and the Gregorian calendar. Java classes like java.sql.Date and SimpleDateFormat also (sometimes) use Calendar instances and therefore might also be affected. This differs from the java.time classes that use the proleptic Gregorian calendar by default. The postgresql server also uses the proleptic Gregorian calendar and therefore it makes sense to make all Calendar instances in the pgjdbc code proleptic Gregorian too.

## Security
* fix: Limit SCRAM PBKDF2 iterations accepted from the server.
pgjdbc was vulnerable to a client-side denial of service in SCRAM-SHA-256 authentication, where a malicious or compromised PostgreSQL server could specify an extremely large PBKDF2 iteration count, causing the client to consume unbounded CPU and potentially exhaust connection pools. The fix introduces a new scramMaxIterations connection property (defaulting to 100,000) to cap iteration counts before computation begins.
See the [Security Advisory](https://github.com/pgjdbc/pgjdbc/security/advisories/GHSA-98qh-xjc8-98pq) for more detail.
The following [CVE-2026-42198](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-42198) has been issued.

fix: release COPY lock on IOException to prevent connection hang (#3957)

When an IOException occurs during COPY operations (endCopy, writeToCopy,
flushCopy, readFromCopy), the COPY lock was not released, causing all
subsequent operations on the connection (e.g. isValid, rollback) to hang
indefinitely in waitOnLock(). This matches the existing pattern in
cancelCopy() which already releases the lock in its finally block.

are prioritized while non-default values still appear for coverage.

test: fix flaky LogicalReplicationStatusTest by polling pg_stat_replication

The tests were flaky because they assumed forceUpdateStatus() is
synchronous — that pg_stat_replication immediately reflects the sent
values. In reality forceUpdateStatus() only flushes data to the TCP
socket; the server needs time to process the standby status update.

During receiveMessageWithoutBlock(), readInternal() may trigger an
automatic timeUpdateStatus(). The server processes it and shows that
value in pg_stat_replication. When forceUpdateStatus() sends a newer
value moments later, the test queries the view before the server has
processed the second update, seeing the stale value.

Fix: add an optional expected parameter to getLSNFromView(). When
non-null, it polls until pg_stat_replication matches the expected
value (with a 2-second timeout). All tests that call
forceUpdateStatus() followed by a view query now pass the expected
LSN, eliminating the timing race.

Also replace getBackendPID() + string-concatenated pid filter with
a PreparedStatement that joins pg_replication_slots on slot_name,
keeping the PID lookup entirely on the server side.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: fix flaky replication restart tests by waiting for confirmed_flush_lsn

The replicationRestartFromLastFeedbackPosition* tests were flaky
because they called forceUpdateStatus() and then immediately closed
the replication connection. forceUpdateStatus() only flushes the
status update to the TCP socket — if the walsender has not read it
before the connection is closed, the slot's confirmed_flush_lsn is
not advanced and the slot replays from an earlier position on restart.

Fix: after forceUpdateStatus(), poll pg_replication_slots until
confirmed_flush_lsn matches the expected value before closing the
connection. This ensures the server has processed the feedback.

fix: Limit SCRAM PBKDF2 iterations accepted from the server

A malicious or compromised PostgreSQL server can advertise an
arbitrarily large PBKDF2 iteration count in its SCRAM
server-first-message, forcing the client to burn CPU inside
clientFinalMessage() before authentication can possibly fail. Combined
with an abandoned connect-thread on loginTimeout expiry, that CPU
continues spinning after the caller has given up.

We add a new `scramMaxIterations` connection property (default 100000)
and validate the iteration count from ServerFirstMessage against it
after parsing but before the PBKDF2-heavy clientFinalMessage() step.
Exceeding the cap throws a PSQLException with CONNECTION_REJECTED and
an error message naming the property so operators can raise it for
trusted servers that legitimately use a higher count.

Fixes CVE-2026-42198

casos.name: v42.7.12: security
casos.body:
### Silent channel-binding authentication downgrade (CVE-2026-54291)

`channelBinding=require` connections can be silently downgraded from SCRAM-SHA-256-PLUS (with channel binding) to plain SCRAM-SHA-256 (without it), losing the man-in-the-middle protection the setting is meant to guarantee. An attacker who can intercept the TLS connection triggers the downgrade with a certificate whose signature algorithm has no tls-server-end-point channel-binding hash. Examples are Ed25519, Ed448, and post-quantum algorithms.

Two issues combine in releases 42.7.4 through 42.7.11:

The bundled `com.ongres.scram:scram-client` (3.1 or 3.2) returns an empty byte array instead of failing when it cannot derive the binding hash for such a certificate. This is the library issue tracked as [GHSA-p9jg-fcr6-3mhf](https://github.com/ongres/scram/security/advisories/GHSA-p9jg-fcr6-3mhf).

pgJDBC does not enforce channelBinding=require where it matters. ScramAuthenticator checks only that the server advertised a -PLUS mechanism; it neither rejects the empty binding nor checks that the negotiated mechanism uses channel binding. The connection therefore downgrades silently.

Only connections that set channelBinding=require are affected. Under the default prefer policy, and under allow or disable, falling back to plain SCRAM is the documented behaviour. 

Releases before 42.7.4 are unaffected, because they do not support channel binding.
mensagens_commits:
chore: bump version to 42.7.12

[ci-skip]

Merge commit from fork

Under channelBinding=require, the driver silently downgraded to a non-PLUS
SCRAM mechanism when it could not derive a channel-binding hash from the
server certificate (for example an Ed25519 certificate, whose signature
algorithm has no associated hash under RFC 5929 tls-server-end-point).
TlsServerEndpoint.getChannelBindingData returns an empty array in that case,
which the SCRAM client treats as "no channel binding available" and
negotiates a bare mechanism.

Enforce channel binding on the pgjdbc side, keeping the existing scram-client
3.2 dependency (no ChannelBindingPolicy / getChannelBindingHash, which are
3.3+):

- When the binding hash cannot be derived under require, fail with a message
  that names the certificate signature algorithm and the remediation, instead
  of returning an empty array.
- After negotiation, require that the selected mechanism actually uses channel
  binding (isPlus). This is the authoritative guarantee: regardless of how
  negotiation resolved, require never connects over a non-PLUS mechanism.

The existing advertisedMechanisms check still rejects require early when the
server offers no -PLUS mechanism.

Ref: GHSA-j92g-9f8w-j867

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: `PgResultSet#getCharacterStream` wraps `String` in `StringReader` (#4063)

Previously returned new `CharArrayReader(value.toCharArray())`, which
allocates a `char[]` proportional to the string length.
`StringReader` wraps the String directly with no extra allocation.

revert: drop unrelated whitespace changes in CHANGELOG.md

fix: restore pre-describe for generated-key batches

Commit d232e605 removed the pre-describe round-trip from internalExecuteBatch() for wantsGeneratedKeysAlways batches. That left flushIfDeadlockRisk() estimating
only NODATA_QUERY_RESPONSE_SIZE_BYTES per query, which can severely underestimate large INSERT ... RETURNING responses and lead to client/server deadlock.

Restore the pre-describe step so batch response sizes are estimated from described result fields and flushing happens at safe intervals.

See https://github.com/pgjdbc/pgjdbc/issues/194

fix: avoid creating transient ResultSet for describe statement purposes

Previously the code created temporary ResultSet which might interfere with
statement.closeOnCompletion().

fix: improve batching when RETURNING contains varchar, numeric types

Previously, pgjdbc overestimated "max number of bytes returned" since
varchar types always have length=-1, and it is modifier that contains
the length.

Unfortunately, for "text" type, the maximum length is undefined, so
batch would still degrade to non-batching execution (sync after each query),
so for now users should refrain from "returning text_column" with executeBatch.

fix: correct estimatedReceiveBufferBytes accounting after forced Sync

After flushIfDeadlockRisk triggers Sync+processResults, the upcoming
query's response size must seed estimatedReceiveBufferBytes rather
than reset it to 0, otherwise the first post-flush query is not
counted against the receive buffer budget.

Also skip the deadlock check for the first query in a batch (nothing
is buffered yet).

test: add protocol-level regression checks to BatchDeadlockTest

Why: the existing test only catches outright deadlocks; regressions
that disable pipelining or fire Sync per row slip through.

What: count wire roundtrips (write→read transitions) via a new
CountingSocketFactory and FE Describe/Execute/Sync via TestLogHandler,
then assert upper bounds around executeBatch. Add a RETURNING id
variant (~3 roundtrips for 500 rows) to contrast with the large-data
cases (~251) so both regimes are covered.

How: the factory is keyed per-connection via SOCKET_FACTORY_ARG so
Counters do not leak between parallel runs; the class is @Isolated
because the JUL logger "org.postgresql" is JVM-global.

feat: flushCacheOnDdl — re-prepare server statements after CREATE/DROP/ALTER

When a server-prepared statement references a table that is later
modified via ALTER TABLE (or affected by CREATE/DROP of a referenced
object), PostgreSQL raises "cached plan must not change result type"
(SQLSTATE 0A000) on the next EXECUTE. Today pgjdbc surfaces that error
verbatim, and transparent recovery requires opting into autosave=ALWAYS
(which wraps every query in a savepoint).

This change adds a new connection property, flushCacheOnDdl (default
true), that makes the driver invalidate the prepared-statement cache
when it sees a CREATE/DROP/ALTER CommandComplete in the same session.
The next time the affected statement is executed, the driver re-PARSEs
it server-side, so callers never see the cached-plan error.

The bump piggybacks on the existing deallocateEpoch mechanism used for
DEALLOCATE ALL / DISCARD ALL. flushCacheOnDdl=false preserves the
pre-existing behaviour for users who rely on it.

Wiring:

* New PGProperty.FLUSH_CACHE_ON_DDL and matching
  BaseDataSource get/setFlushCacheOnDdl (PGPropertyTest enforces both).
* QueryExecutor.{is,set}FlushCacheOnDdl + QueryExecutorBase
  implementation, defaulting to true so non-PgConnection callers
  (e.g. ReplicationProtocol) inherit the improved behaviour.
* PgConnection reads the property in its constructor and forwards it.
* QueryExecutorImpl bumps deallocateEpoch on CREATE/DROP/ALTER
  CommandComplete when flushCacheOnDdl is enabled.

Test:

AutoRollbackTest now ties its existing flushCacheOnDeallocate
parameterization to flushCacheOnDdl 1:1, and the FailMode.ALTER
iteration no longer skips flushCacheOnDeallocate=false. Both legacy
("cached plan must not change result type" → IN_FAILED_SQL_TRANSACTION)
and new (transparent re-prepare) paths get coverage; the assertion in
executeSqlSuccess only flags the legacy hard-failure case when
flushCacheOnDdl is explicitly disabled.

Avoid direct java.lang.management dependency in maxResultBuffer parser (#4069)

Why a separate class works the same as reflection here:

- PGPropertyMaxResultBufferParser no longer has any verifier-visible
  reference to java.lang.management.*; it only references JvmHeapAccess.
- JvmHeapAccess is loaded lazily, on the first INVOKESTATIC of
  maxHeapBytes(). When loaded on a runtime that lacks
  java.lang.management (Android ART), class linking raises a
  LinkageError, which the caller catches and translates into the
  "max heap unavailable" sentinel (-1).
- No reflection, no boxing, normal compile-time visibility, regular
  IDE / Error Prone / Checker Framework support.

To preserve the "missing management factory" test path without spinning
up an isolated classloader, parseProperty now has a package-private
overload that accepts a LongSupplier. The runtime test passes
() -> -1L to model the missing runtime.

Also adds java.lang.management.** to the forbidden-apis signatures,
applied only to the production source set (forbiddenApisMain), so
regressions like #4068 are caught at build time. JvmHeapAccess is
the single authorized callsite and is excluded from the check.

fix: PGXAConnection no longer saves and restores the caller's autoCommit

PGXAConnection used to save and restore the JDBC autoCommit flag
around every XAResource call. The restore was inconsistent across
methods and missing on failure paths, which broke recovery on managed
datasources that pool connections with autoCommit=false:

  recover() ran SELECT pg_prepared_xacts through a plain Statement,
  so pgjdbc auto-prepended BEGIN and left transactionState=OPEN. The
  next commit(xid, false) then failed with "2nd phase commit must be
  issued using an idle connection", aborting recovery on TomEE,
  WildFly, and WebSphere Liberty after a crash-restart cycle.

Route every XA-protocol command (BEGIN, PREPARE TRANSACTION, COMMIT,
ROLLBACK, COMMIT PREPARED, ROLLBACK PREPARED, the recover() SELECT)
through BaseConnection.execSQLUpdate / execSQLQuery. Both already set
QueryExecutor.QUERY_SUPPRESS_BEGIN, so pgjdbc never prepends a BEGIN
of its own and never has to save or restore the caller's autoCommit. The flag
is now invariant across every XAResource call.

The naive alternative — wrapping recover() in setAutoCommit(true) /
setAutoCommit(restored) — was rejected because it would silently
commit a pending local transaction on the same connection. JTA 1.2
§3.4 forbids exactly that side effect.

Other lifecycle fixes folded in:

* prepare() now mutates XA state only after PREPARE TRANSACTION
  succeeds. A failed PREPARE used to leave the driver thinking the
  branch was already prepared, so the recovery rollback(xid) took the
  prepared-branch path and tried ROLLBACK PREPARED against a gid the
  server had never seen.

* ConnectionHandler now rejects setAutoCommit(false) (previously a
  permissive no-op) and setSavepoint(...) (the previous guard
  misspelled the method as setSavePoint, so savepoints silently went
  through during an active XA branch). Both match JTA 1.2 §3.4.

* commitPrepared and rollback-of-prepared return XAER_RMFAIL — not
  XAER_RMERR — when the connection arrives with a non-idle
  TransactionState. Transaction managers (Geronimo, Narayana,
  Atomikos) treat XAER_RMFAIL as retryable on a fresh XAResource and
  no longer abandon the prepared transaction.

Observable behaviour changes for downstream:

* setAutoCommit(false) and setSavepoint(...) on an enlisted Connection
  now throw, where they used to be a silent no-op / silent success.
* XAER_RMERR is replaced by XAER_RMFAIL on the dirty-connection
  precondition path for prepared commit / rollback.

Existing XADataSourceTest assertions stay green; 9 new tests cover
the recover / autoCommit interaction, the dirty-connection
precondition, and the failure-path invariants.

build: use explicit fileTree for gettext .po inputs

The poFiles input to remove_obsolete_translations was wired through
files(sourceSets.main.get().allSource).filter { it.path.endsWith(".po") }.
That collection is a poor fit for an incremental task input:

  - allSource is a SourceDirectorySet whose srcDirs change between runs
    — for example, build/jcp/preprocessVersion appears only after the
    preprocessVersion task has executed once.
  - Wrapping it in files(...).filter { ... } produces a FilteredFileTree
    whose snapshot depends on the upstream aggregation, not on the .po
    files themselves.
  - With @PathSensitive(PathSensitivity.NONE), Gradle has been observed
    to emit a +1/-1 pair of ADDED + REMOVED events for the same physical
    .po file across runs. The MsgAttrib/MsgMerge/MsgFmt tasks then run
    the REMOVED branch and delete the output the ADDED branch just
    produced, which cascades: add_new_messages_to_po loses ru.po,
    generate_java_resources never sees it, and generateGettextSources has
    no messages_ru.java to copy back into src/main/java. --rerun-tasks
    masks the issue by bypassing incremental change detection.

I was not able to fully reproduce the spurious ADDED+REMOVED on the
current checkout (allSource currently contains each .po exactly once),
so the precise trigger inside Gradle's snapshotter is not nailed down
here. Either way, the input is structurally unstable and the right
shape is an explicit, narrowly scoped FileTree.

Switch to fileTree("src/main/java/org/postgresql/translation") { include("*.po") }
so each .po file appears exactly once, the input is independent of any
SourceDirectorySet evolution, and the snapshot is stable run-to-run.

A more general fix belongs in vlsi-release-plugins/gettext-plugin
(collapse changes per output file, with ADDED/MODIFIED winning over
REMOVED) and would protect any other consumer of these tasks. This
commit takes the one-line pgjdbc-side route to unbreak the build chain
immediately.

fix: append default non-proxy hosts when socksNonProxyHosts is set

  When socksNonProxyHosts is set by the system (e.g., macOS sets it to
  "local|*.local|169.254/16|*.169.254/16"), HostSpec used it as-is,
  completely replacing DEFAULT_NON_PROXY_HOSTS. Since 127.0.0.1 wasn't
  in the system-supplied list, HostSpec would pass an unresolved
  InetSocketAddress through the SOCKS proxy. But SocksSocketImpl (via
  DefaultProxySelector) always appends its built-in defaults to the
  property value, so it would bypass the proxy for 127.0.0.1 and try
  to connect directly with the still-unresolved address, causing an
  UnknownHostException.

  Align HostSpec with java.net.DefaultProxySelector by always merging
  DEFAULT_NON_PROXY_HOSTS with the user-supplied socksNonProxyHosts
  value instead of treating them as mutually exclusive.

  Fixes #4044

fix: keep LazyCleanerImpl cleanup task alive across transient empty queue

When the reference queue briefly empties, the cleanup task previously
exited immediately (the loop was guarded by `while (!checkEmpty())`),
forcing the next register() call to re-submit a fresh ForkJoinPool task.
Under bursty load with constrained CPU (reproduces with
-XX:ActiveProcessorCount=2), the FJP submit + ManagedBlocker compensation
overhead dominates and cleanup falls so far behind that Node entries —
each holding the cleanup action lambda and the resources it captures —
accumulate to OutOfMemoryError.

The cleanup task now waits the full threadTtl on the reference queue
after the registry empties before terminating, matching the prior
dedicated-thread behavior and amortizing FJP startup cost across
register bursts.

Fixes #4037

caller now just calls get(timeout, MILLISECONDS); timeout, interrupt,

fix: avoid nulling contextClassLoader on shared commonPool workers

The cleanup task submitted to ForkJoinPool.commonPool() set the worker's
contextClassLoader to null and never restored it. Common-pool workers are
shared JVM-wide and reused, so this left unrelated tasks running with a
null contextClassLoader, breaking libraries that rely on it (for example
reflections8).

Clear the contextClassLoader on the submitting thread only, around the
execute() call, so a freshly created common-pool worker is not born
holding the caller's (possibly a web application's) classloader, then
restore it immediately. The worker thread's contextClassLoader is never
touched. This keeps the leak guard from #3953 (the worker no longer pins
the submitter's classloader) and also removes the
InnocuousForkJoinWorkerThread setContextClassLoader SecurityException
path, while fixing the regression where shared workers were left with a
null contextClassLoader.

fix: close socket when PgConnection setup fails after connect

PgConnection opens the network connection via
ConnectionFactory.openConnection, then runs a long sequence of setup
steps (SET SESSION CHARACTERISTICS, COMMIT/ROLLBACK preparation, type
cache initialisation, and so on) before registering the connection with
the Cleaner on the constructor's last line. If any of those steps threw
(a server error on a SET, a mid-setup network drop surfacing as
IOException/SQLException, a RuntimeException, or a thread interrupt), the
constructor failed without closing queryExecutor, so the open socket
leaked. The half-built PgConnection was never assigned to a variable and
the Cleaner was not yet registered, so nothing could close it.

Wrap the setup that runs after openConnection in a try/catch that closes
queryExecutor and rethrows the original failure, attaching any close
error as a suppressed exception. QueryExecutorBase.close checks
isClosed, so closing again on a path that already closed the executor is
a safe no-op.

an invalid stringtype value and asserts, through a recording
SocketFactory, that the socket is closed.

fix: reject overlong inputs in NumberParser.getFastLong instead of wrapping

The overflow guard checked that val was at most Long.MAX_VALUE / 10
before each multiply and add. Once val wrapped negative, for example
after parsing the nineteen digits of "9223372036854775808", every
negative value passed that guard and parsing continued with wrapped
arithmetic. Long.MIN_VALUE times 10 wraps to exactly zero, so the
accumulator effectively restarted from zero. As a result getFastLong
returned silently wrong values for certain overlong inputs rather than
failing over to the slow path. For example "92233720368547758081234"
parsed to 1234, "-92233720368547758080" parsed to 0, and
"92233720368547758089" parsed to 9.

This was reachable from PgResultSet.getLong, getInt, getShort, and
getByte on any text format column. Calling rs.getLong() on a numeric
column holding 92233720368547758081234 returned 1234 instead of
throwing "Bad value for type long".

The fix accumulates the value as a negative number, which is the same
approach used by Long.parseLong. Every valid input fits without
overflow because the absolute value of Long.MIN_VALUE is greater than
Long.MAX_VALUE. The exact bounds are checked before each multiply and
subtract. Out of range magnitudes now throw FAST_NUMBER_FAILED so the
caller falls back to the slow path, which raises the proper error.

test: add overflow boundary tests for NumberParser.getFastLong

These tests cover inputs whose magnitude exceeds the long range. The

instead of throwing, for example "92233720368547758081234" parsed to

still parse correctly when followed by a fractional part.

the instance directly, so the chained constructor is gone and the
one-way abandoned flag becomes a plain volatile boolean (it is only
ever set to true, so AtomicBoolean bought nothing).

fix: reject out of range and NaN values in PGInterval.setSeconds

PGInterval.setSeconds validated its argument against the long range in
microseconds, but the wholeSeconds field is an int and the cast after
division truncated without any check. Values beyond the int range of
whole seconds, about 68 years, silently wrapped. For example
new PGInterval(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 3000000000.0) produced a negative
interval with no exception. The old error message also described a
bound that the code never enforced on the stored field.

The whole seconds value is now computed as a long and checked against
the int range before being stored, so out of range values throw
IllegalArgumentException instead of wrapping. NaN is rejected
explicitly because it passed the old comparisons and Math.round mapped
it to zero, turning NaN input into a zero interval. Infinite values are
caught by the range check since Math.round saturates at the long
bounds. The isNull flag is now only cleared after validation succeeds
so a rejected value no longer mutates the object.

test: fix flaky sentLocationEqualToLastReceiveLSN replication test

sentLocationEqualToLastReceiveLSN asserted that pg_stat_replication.sent_lsn
exactly equals the last LSN received by the stream. That equality is racy: when
no decodable data is pending, the walsender advances sent_lsn with keepalive
messages to the current end of WAL, so any unrelated WAL (the second test
database, autovacuum, background activity) pushes sent_lsn past the client's
position. The polling helper added earlier cannot recover once sent_lsn has
overshot, because it waits for exact equality that never returns.

A client can never receive more than the server sent, so the robust invariant
is that sent_lsn is at least the received LSN. Assert greaterThanOrEqualTo and
poll the view until it reaches that bound. Factor the single-row read out of the
poll loop and drive both the equality and at-least pollers through one predicate
so the other tests keep their exact-match behaviour.

fix(ssl): build PKIX trust anchors without a KeyStore so FIPS JVMs work

Both LibPQFactory and SingleCertValidatingFactory built a transient,
in-memory truststore by creating a KeyStore, loading the sslrootcert (or
the pinned cert) into it, and handing it to a PKIX TrustManagerFactory.
The KeyStore type was incidental -- the store is never serialised -- yet
it forced a concrete provider: LibPQFactory hardcoded "jks", and both
paths ultimately depend on a general-purpose KeyStore being available.

FIPS-mode JVMs (Semeru FIPS 140-3, IBM SDK in FIPS mode, BouncyCastle
FIPS) offer no such type. Under -Dsemeru.fips=true connections failed
with NoSuchAlgorithmException: first on "jks", and -- as issue #4191
later showed -- on the default "pkcs12" too, so switching to
KeyStore.getDefaultType() is not enough.

Build the PKIX trust anchors straight from the parsed certificates with
PKIXBuilderParameters and CertPathTrustManagerParameters, dropping the
KeyStore entirely. The PKIX TrustManagerFactory derives the same trust
anchors it would have extracted from a keystore of trusted-cert entries,
so non-FIPS behaviour is unchanged, while FIPS JVMs no longer need any
KeyStore type at all.

SingleCertValidatingFactory now also requests the "PKIX" TrustManager
algorithm explicitly instead of TrustManagerFactory.getDefaultAlgorithm().
The KeyStore-free init passes ManagerFactoryParameters, which only the
PKIX factory accepts (SunX509 rejects them). The default algorithm is
already "PKIX" on a stock JDK, so this is a no-op there; it changes
behaviour only if a custom provider made another algorithm the default.

The two remaining KeyStore.getInstance call sites (PKCS12KeyManager,
DbKeyStoreSocketFactory) load real on-disk keystore files, where the
type is the file format and cannot be removed; they are out of scope.

Add Checker Framework nullness stubs for the JDK constructors whose
optional parameters are documented as accepting null: TrustAnchor's
nameConstraints and PKIXBuilderParameters' targetConstraints.

Closes #4191

fix: auto-detect SSL key format instead of relying on .key extension

The .key extension is generic and can contain either PEM or DER-encoded
keys. Rather than mapping .key to PEM format (which broke DER .key files
with MalformedInputException), auto-detect the format while preserving
libpq's preference for PEM before DER.

Format is now determined by file extension:
- .p12/.pfx -> PKCS-12
- .pem -> PEM
- .der -> DER/PKCS-8 (escape hatch to skip auto-detection)
- anything else (.key, .pk8, etc.) -> scan the first 64 KiB for a PEM
  private-key header, otherwise use DER/PKCS-8

Introduces Pk8OrPemKeyManager which wraps both PEMKeyManager and
LazyKeyManager. The delegate is resolved lazily on the first call to
any X509KeyManager method, so it works regardless of TLS engine call
order. The bounded scan avoids excessive work on malformed files and
avoids parsing the key during format detection.

Key-file permissions are validated once, before format detection, so the
DER/PKCS-8 fallback cannot bypass the permission check that PEM keys get.

fix: reject SQL_TSI_FRAC_SECOND with an explicit, explained error

The JDBC SQL_TSI_FRAC_SECOND interval has no portable size: ODBC and SQL
Server define it as nanoseconds, while MySQL treats it as microseconds.
PostgreSQL intervals have microsecond resolution, so any fixed mapping
would silently produce values off by a factor of 1000 for part of the
ecosystem.

error and timestampdiff to a SYNTAX_ERROR; neither said why. Replace both
with one message that states the reason and points to SQL_TSI_SECOND with
a fractional value as the workaround, and report NOT_IMPLEMENTED (0A000)
for both paths.

unsupported "since backend does not support it" and wrongly listed it as
supported for timestampdiff.

corruption.

test(replication): shrink big-transaction inserts to avoid CI timeouts

duringSendBigTransactionReplicationStreamCloseNotActive and its sibling
duringSendBigTransactionConnectionCloseSlotStatusNotActive each insert a
200k-row transaction, start logical replication, read the first message,
then close. stream.close() sends CopyDone and then drains the rest of the
in-progress transaction, because on current PostgreSQL the walsender emits
a committed transaction in full before it honours CopyDone. The drain cost
is therefore O(transaction size).

Measured on PostgreSQL 16 (test_decoding), stream.close() scales linearly
with the row count:

  20k  rows -> read 28ms,   close 154ms
  200k rows -> read 248ms,  close 1229ms
  1M   rows -> read 1908ms, close 4832ms

On a loaded CI runner with coverage instrumentation on the per-message
decode path, the 200k drain crosses the 60s @Timeout and the test flakes.
20k rows is still ~2.4MB, well above the socket buffers, so the server is
still mid-send when close() runs and the same code path is exercised, only
~8x faster. The test asserts that the slot becomes inactive after close,
which holds for any size, so the smaller transaction loses no coverage.

getPrimaryKeys reconstructed the key columns from pg_index.indkey and then
trimmed INCLUDE columns with a server-version-dependent count column
(indnkeyatts on v11+, indnatts otherwise, see #3434). pg_constraint.conkey
already lists exactly the primary-key columns, so reading from it removes the

neither indnatts, indnkeyatts, nor the reported server version.

query returns identical rows for every user table: single-column and composite
keys (including reversed key order), INCLUDE columns, named constraints,
ADD PRIMARY KEY USING INDEX, and partitioned tables. The only difference is
pg_toast tables, whose internal indexes have no pg_constraint row, and
getPrimaryKeys always takes a concrete table name that callers do not point at
pg_toast_*.

fix(core): detect search_path changes case-insensitively

The COMMAND_COMPLETE handler invalidates the prepared-statement plan
cache when it sees a SET that changes search_path, but it scanned the
SQL for the literal lower-case "search_path". An upper-case
SET SEARCH_PATH (or any non-lower-case form) went undetected, so the
cache kept stale entries. With autoCommit=false this surfaces as a
"cached plan must not change result type" error that aborts the
transaction, which the reparse-on-error fallback can no longer heal.

regionMatches scan (no allocation or regex on the execute path, same
1024-char window as before), and also handle RESET search_path and
RESET ALL, which change the effective search_path too. The existing
fast path that skips repeated identical SET search_path statements is
kept.

The detection is shared, so the type-cache epoch that the typecache
branch adds to this block will benefit from the same fix once it lands.

the acute "é" used for the verb "è" throughout, "Impossible" to
"Impossibile", a mismatched guillemet, two garbled fragments, and the
rollback message that mistakenly read "commit".

Three further fidelity fixes correct the meaning of ported strings:
"ending copy" no longer reads as cancellation, the missing-output
diagnostic refers to function outputs rather than an "output function",
and the copy-cancel response message keeps "error". msgfmt -c passes.

fix(deps): update dependency com.gradleup.shadow:com.gradleup.shadow.gradle.plugin to v9.4.3

feat(largeobject): expose server version for 64-bit LO API selection

lo_tell64 and lo_lseek64 require PostgreSQL 9.3+. Expose the cached
server version through Fastpath#getServerVersionNum and add
LargeObject#supports64BitOffsets so callers can pick the 64-bit
fastpath functions by version instead of calling them and recovering
from the failure on older servers. The version is negotiated at
connection startup, so the check costs no extra round-trip.

fix(largeobject): reset BlobInputStream relative to the LargeObject position

BlobInputStream assumed the underlying LargeObject was positioned at the
start, so mark() and reset() computed offsets from the wrong origin when
the stream was created from a LargeObject that had already been seeked.
reset() then repositioned to the wrong byte.

Initialise the stream position from the LargeObject's current position
(lo_tell64, or lo_tell on servers older than 9.3) on first use, and make
the read limit relative to that position. The initialisation is deferred
out of the constructor so the failure surfaces as a checked IOException.

Also invalidate the read buffer before seeking in reset(), so a failed
seek cannot leave stale buffered data behind.

Closes #3149

Co-authored-by: James Howe <jmh205@cam.ac.uk>

feat(largeobject): skip in BlobInputStream by seeking instead of reading

InputStream.skip on a BlobInputStream used the default implementation,
which reads and discards the bytes, so skipping a large distance cost a
full read. Override skip(long) to seek with lo_lseek/lo_lseek64, making
the cost independent of the distance.

Large objects are sparse, so skipping past the current end is allowed:
later reads return -1 and the returned count still reflects the
requested distance, as the InputStream.skip contract permits. Skips that
stay within the current buffer advance the buffer pointer without a
round-trip.

Closes #3144

Co-authored-by: James Howe <jmh205@cam.ac.uk>

docs: clarify search_path correctness for server-prepared statements

The server-prepare page warned that a reused server-side prepared
statement "could fetch data from the old table" after a search_path
change and that "it is hard to tell which behaviour is expected". That
matched PostgreSQL before 9.3, which kept the old cached plan. Since 9.3
PostgreSQL re-plans a cached statement when the search_path changes, so a
reused server-side prepared statement returns rows from the table the
current search_path selects.

Reword the section accordingly, describe pgJDBC's search_path tracking as
a cache optimisation that re-prepares on a detected top-level change, and
give two recommendations (avoid frequent changes; keep set search_path at
the top level so the driver can re-prepare, otherwise a column-layout
change can fail with `cached plan must not change result type`).

Add two SchemaTest cases next to the existing search_path prepared-
statement tests: they reuse a server-side prepared statement across a
search_path change the driver does not see -- one made via set_config(),
one inside a PL/pgSQL routine -- and assert the rows follow the current
search_path. They rely on the backend re-plan, so they are gated to
PostgreSQL 9.3+ (9.1 silently keeps the old plan). The PL/pgSQL case also
checks the server reports search_path only from PostgreSQL 18 on
(GUC_REPORT).

Closes #3399

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: note PKCS-12 client certificate chain requirement

The documented `openssl pkcs12 -export` example exports only the leaf
client certificate. When that certificate is signed by an intermediate
CA, the resulting `.p12` omits the chain and the server rejects the
connection with `connection requires a valid client certificate`.

Document that the archive must hold the full chain and that `-certfile`
adds the intermediates. The test certificates are signed directly by the
root CA, so the example command itself needs no change; a Makefile
comment records where `-certfile` would go.

Closes #3795

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ci: skip Codecov upload on failed branch builds

A failed run on master (or release) reports only partial coverage, since
the report is merged from whatever the aborted test step collected. Codecov
treats that as the new project baseline, so the global coverage drops and PR
diffs compare against a poisoned reference.

Upload coverage on branch builds only when tests pass, so PR diffs compare
against the last successful branch run. Pull requests still upload even after
a test failure, so a PR shows how much of the changed code is already covered.
The post-failure report rebuild now runs on pull requests only, since a failed
branch build no longer uploads.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(jdbc): honor scale in ResultSet.getBigDecimal(int, int)

getBigDecimal(int columnIndex, int scale) used -1 internally as a "do not
rescale" sentinel, so an explicit scale of -1 was silently ignored even
though it is a valid BigDecimal scale. It also called BigDecimal.setScale
without a rounding mode, so requesting a smaller scale than the value
carried (e.g. getBigDecimal(col, 2) on 1.1234) threw "Bad value" instead
of rounding.

Replace the -1 sentinel with a nullable Integer (null means "no
rescale") and round with RoundingMode.HALF_EVEN. The binary numeric path
now applies the requested scale too, matching the text path. The public
static toBigDecimal(String, int) stays public and delegates to a private
nullable overload, so the API is unchanged.

Decode the numeric typmod scale as a signed 11-bit value, so numeric
types with a negative scale (e.g. numeric(2,-2), supported since
PostgreSQL 15) are scaled correctly in both the text and binary paths
instead of being masked to a large positive scale.

Co-authored-by: eperez <eperez@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(jdbc): return null CHAR_OCTET_LENGTH for non-character columns

DatabaseMetaData.getColumns reported CHAR_OCTET_LENGTH as COLUMN_SIZE for
every column, including non-character types such as integer or integer[].
JDBC defines CHAR_OCTET_LENGTH only for character and binary types, so it
is now copied from COLUMN_SIZE for those types and reported as null for the
rest.

Also declare the CHAR_OCTET_LENGTH result column as INTEGER rather than
VARCHAR, matching the JDBC type and the sibling COLUMN_SIZE column.

Reworked from #3589 to apply on top of the current test layout and to fold
in the review feedback.

Closes #3589

Co-authored-by: GAJERA TIRTH <tirthgajera121@gmail.com>

fix: detect native CALL preceded by a comment in CallableStatement

A leading comment before CALL hid the native call from
Parser.modifyJdbcCall, which only skipped whitespace before checking
for the call keyword. As a result registerOutParameter failed for SQL
such as "/* comment */ call proc(?, ?)" with "This statement does not
declare an OUT parameter".

Skip leading whitespace and SQL comments (both -- line comments and
/* */ block comments, the latter nesting per the SQL spec) before
looking for the opening brace of the escape syntax and before the
native CALL detection.

Adds parameterized ParserTest cases covering comments before both the
native CALL and the { ? = call ... } escape forms, plus negatives that
ensure a comment containing the word "call" is not mistaken for a call.

Closes #2538

Closes #4130

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: invalidate prepared statement cache via search_path GUC_REPORT (PG 18+)

pgJDBC invalidates its server-prepared statement cache on a search_path
change so a reused statement re-prepares against the new path. Until now
it recognised only top-level SET/RESET commands by scanning the command
text, so a change hidden inside PL/pgSQL or a function slipped through and
could make a reused statement fail with `cached plan must not change
result type`.

PostgreSQL marks search_path as GUC_REPORT from version 18, so the server
reports every search_path change to the client in a ParameterStatus
message, wherever the change happens. Consume that report in
receiveParameterStatus and invalidate the cache only when the value
actually changes. On those servers the report is authoritative and covers
SET, RESET and RESET ALL, so skip the command-tag scan entirely once
search_path has been reported. Servers older than 18 do not report
search_path, so they keep using the command-tag scan and behave exactly
as before.

Add a SchemaTest case that changes search_path from inside PL/pgSQL
between two differently typed tables: PostgreSQL 17 and older keep the
cached statement and fail with `cached plan must not change result type`,
while 18+ invalidates the cache from the report and re-prepares cleanly.
Verified against PostgreSQL 16 (unchanged) and 18 (the SET/RESET/RESET ALL
tests pass through the report with the command-tag scan disabled).

Refs #3399

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: render bytea text parameters in PreparedStatement#toString

A bytea value supplied as text via PGobject (for example the hex string
"\x01020304") is bound as a String with the BYTEA oid. SimpleParameterList#toString
passed it straight to PGbytea.toPGLiteral, which only handles byte[], so toString()
threw "Unable to convert bytea parameter ... to literal". The crash surfaced through
BatchResultHandler.handleError, turning an expected serialization failure into a
driver exception.

Handle the two text encodings of bytea:
- hex format (\x...): validate the value the way PostgreSQL does, then render
  '\x...'::bytea. The characters after \x must be hex digits or the whitespace
  PostgreSQL ignores (space, tab, newline, carriage return), and the digit count
  must be even. Validation rejects stray quotes and backslashes, so the literal
  cannot be abused for SQL injection.
- escape format: quote and cast like any other text literal via quoteAndCast,
  which escapes quotes and backslashes per standard_conforming_strings.

Also fix the adjacent "Can't convert ..." message: the apostrophe starts a
MessageFormat quote and suppressed the {0}/{1} substitutions.

fixes https://github.com/pgjdbc/pgjdbc/issues/3757

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test: guard authentication-plugin test against trust auth

ObjectFactoryTest.invalidAuthenticationPlugin expects opening a connection
to fail while the driver loads a bad authenticationPluginClassName. The
driver loads that plugin lazily: AuthenticationPluginManager.withPassword
instantiates it only when the server actually requests a password, so under
"trust" authentication the plugin is never loaded, the connection succeeds,
and the test failed with a cryptic "Expected SQLException ... but nothing
was thrown". The Docker harness hides this because certdir/server/pg_hba.conf
requests md5 for the test database; a non-Docker reader following TESTING.md
was never told the test user must not be on a trust line.

Skip the test with a pointed message when it detects trust authentication,
and add a TESTING.md section that documents the HBA requirement, mirroring
the existing SCRAM section.

Re #2442

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(jdbc): classify updatable result set by search_path visibility

isUpdateable() looks up the candidate key columns through
getPrimaryUniqueKeys() with no schema qualifier when the query uses an
unqualified table name. The lookup matched every schema, so two schemas
holding a table with the same name and the same primary or unique index
name but different key columns produced one merged constraint whose
columns were the union of both. A result set over such a table could
then be wrongly rejected as not updatable.

Restrict the unqualified lookup to the relation the query actually
resolves to by adding pg_table_is_visible(ct.oid), which applies the
same search_path visibility rules as the server. pg_table_is_visible()
has existed since PostgreSQL 7.3, so this keeps the 9.3 baseline.

Supersedes PR #3400, which addressed the same bug by falling back to
connection.getSchema(); that only covers current_schema() and misses
tables resolved through later search_path entries.

fix: flush LargeObject output stream before marking closed (#4248)

* fix: flush LargeObject output stream before marking closed

LargeObject.close() set closed=true before calling
BlobOutputStream.flush(), which in turn calls LargeObject.write().
write() calls checkClosed() and throws because closed is already true.

Move closed=true to after the flush so the write can complete.

Fixes #4247

* fix: flush LargeObject output stream before marking closed

LargeObject.close() set closed=true before calling
BlobOutputStream.flush(), which calls LargeObject.write() and fails
its checkClosed() guard.

Wrap the flush in try/finally so the object is always marked closed
and lo_close is always issued, even if the flush throws.

Fixes #4247

* fix: prevent lo_close from masking flush errors in LargeObject.close()

The previous try/finally structure ran lo_close and commit
unconditionally in the finally block. If os.flush() threw and then
lo_close also threw (typical after a transaction abort), the finally
exception replaced the original, so callers saw "current transaction
is aborted" instead of the real flush cause. The commitOnClose path
could also commit a half-written large object after a flush failure.

Replace the try/finally with explicit error capture: flush errors are
stored, lo_close always runs but its failure is attached via
addSuppressed, and commit only fires when both flush and lo_close
succeeded. closed is still set after flush so BlobOutputStream.flush()
can call back into LargeObject.write() without hitting checkClosed().

Addresses review feedback from vlsi on PR #4248.

fix(scram): fail closed on channel-binding downgrade (no scram bump)

Under channelBinding=require, the driver silently downgraded to a non-PLUS
SCRAM mechanism when it could not derive a channel-binding hash from the
server certificate (for example an Ed25519 certificate, whose signature
algorithm has no associated hash under RFC 5929 tls-server-end-point).
TlsServerEndpoint.getChannelBindingData returns an empty array in that case,
which the SCRAM client treats as "no channel binding available" and
negotiates a bare mechanism.

Enforce channel binding on the pgjdbc side, keeping the existing scram-client
3.2 dependency (no ChannelBindingPolicy / getChannelBindingHash, which are
3.3+):

- When the binding hash cannot be derived under require, fail with a message
  that names the certificate signature algorithm and the remediation, instead
  of returning an empty array.
- After negotiation, require that the selected mechanism actually uses channel
  binding (isPlus). This is the authoritative guarantee: regardless of how
  negotiation resolved, require never connects over a non-PLUS mechanism.

The existing advertisedMechanisms check still rejects require early when the
server offers no -PLUS mechanism.

Ref: GHSA-j92g-9f8w-j867

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(jdbc): reject empty timestamp/timestamptz text with a clear error

toTimestamp(Calendar, byte[]) read bytes[0] for the infinity check
before validating the length, so an empty value (an empty string
decodes to new byte[0]) threw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of
a normal SQLException. Both timestamp and timestamptz text decoding
share this method, so both leaked the raw runtime exception; date and
time were already clean.

Reject empty input up front with a PSQLException that reuses the
existing "Bad value for type timestamp/date/time" message (SQLState
22007), so no new translatable string is needed and the failure matches
how other malformed values are already reported.

feat(sessions): add support for remote redis session store (#3345)

Description
====================
zot currently stores session cookies in memory or in a local directory.
For cases where the session cookies should be independent of the
instance where they were created such as multiple instances of zot, or a
fully stateless zot instance, there is a need to support a remote
session storage.
This change adds support for using Redis and Redis-compatible services as a
remote session driver as well as introduces a new configuration option
for it.

What has changed
=======================
- New config added under Auth config to specify configuration for
  the session driver.
- Examples README updated with details of the new Auth config.
- The config supports only 2 drivers in this change - local and redis
- Using the local driver is backwards compatible and behaves the same
  way that zot currently works for local session storage.
- Omitting this config does not result in an error. In this case, zot
  behaves as it normally does for local session storage.
- When configured, zot can use redis for persisting cookie
  information for zot UI.
- The cookie in the store is deleted on logout or after the max
  expiry time for the cookie.
- Configuration for the redis session driver accepts the same configuration
  values as that of the remote meta cache.
- A separate connection is established for the session driver. An
  existing connection for meta cache will not be re-used for the
  session driver.
- A key prefix is configurable for the redis session driver. The value will be
  converted into a string for use. If no value is provided, a default
  prefix of "zotsession" will be used.
- Redis sessions does not support hash key or encryption in this change.
- New BATS test added to verify zot behavior with Redis session store.
- Github workflow updated to install valkey-tools dependency for BATS.

Signed-off-by: Vishwas Rajashekar <dev@vrajashkr.com>

feat: the default retention delay is not the GC delay (#3447)

Most users don't make the difference between retention deleting untagged manifests vs GC deleting other blobs.
This causes confusion since the GC delay and the retention delay (used for untagged manifests and orphan referrers) have different defaults, and are set separately in the zot configuration.
Most users don't configrue retention policies, and they still expect untagged manifests to be deleted at GC time.

With this change, if retention delay is not specified in the config file, the value used is the GC delay.
If GC delay is also unspecified in the config file, the default GC delay is used for both.

fix(api): return 416 for bad upload range on PUT; fix GET upload Range at size zero (#3983)

Align closing blob upload (PUT) with the OCI Distribution Spec: invalid /
out-of-order upload ranges (ErrBadUploadRange) return 416 Requested Range Not
Satisfiable instead of 400, for both the final-chunk PutBlobChunk path and
FinishBlobUpload.

GetBlobUpload (GET upload status): fix the Range response when zero bytes have
been received—send Range: 0-0 instead of Range: 0--1, consistent with a new
session and the spec’s Location + Range upload status shape. Only map
ErrBadBlobDigest to 400 here; do not handle ErrBadUploadRange on GET (that
request carries no range; ImageStore.GetBlobUpload does not return it).

Document PUT upload failures 400 and 416 in swagger; regenerate swagger
artifacts. Update route tests (expect 416 on UpdateBlobUpload for
ErrBadUploadRange), drop the mock-only GetBlobUpload+ErrBadUploadRange case,
and assert Range: 0-0 in TestPullRange after GET on a new upload location.

Fix potential panic when parsing Content-Range (index out of range)
when accessing `tokens[0]`.

Signed-off-by: Andrei Aaron <andreifdaaron@gmail.com>

feat(zb): Support for TTFB measurement + on-demand sync tests (#3929)

feat(zb): support for measuring TTFB + sync tests

Adds supports for measuring time to first byte (TTFB)
for Pull tests for the manifest check, the manifest get,
the config get, and the blob get.

Additionally, this introduces 2 new sync tests which measure
the performance of on-demand sync.

Setup code has been refactored to accomodate a new
blob size of 1GB.

Parts of zb have been refactored to address linter errors.

Signed-off-by: Vishwas Rajashekar <dev@vrajashkr.com>

fix(api): recognize Docker Compose/Buildx User-Agent in v2 challenge workaround (#3992)

Docker Compose and Buildx proxy through the Docker daemon, which sends
a User-Agent starting with "docker/<version>" rather than the
"Docker-Client/<version>" string sent by direct Docker CLI pulls.
This caused compose/buildx pulls to skip the 401 challenge on
registries with mixed anonymous/authenticated access policies,
resulting in 'unauthorized' errors.

Add strings.HasPrefix(ua, "docker/") alongside the existing
Docker-Client check so daemon-proxied requests from any upstream
tool (compose, buildx, etc.) are handled correctly.

Fixes #3991

feat(auth): support OIDC RP-Initiated Logout (#3975)

POST /zot/auth/logout now returns an endSessionUrl in the JSON
response body when the session was established via an OIDC provider
whose discovery document advertises an endSessionEndpoint, so the
UI can navigate the browser to it and terminate the session at the
IdP in addition to clearing the local cookie.

- The OIDC callback records the provider name in the session after
  login; the github OAuth2 path is untouched.
- end_session_endpoint is read from the zitadel/oidc RelyingParty
  and validated as an absolute http(s) URL.
- post_logout_redirect_uri prefers http.externalUrl when set and
  falls back to deriving the origin from the incoming request.
- No id_token_hint is sent; client_id identifies the RP, so the
  ID token does not need to be persisted.
- Non-OIDC sessions (local/basic/LDAP/GitHub) retain the existing
  200 OK, no body behavior.

Operators must register the URI zot sends as a valid post-logout
redirect URI on the IdP client.

Ref: https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-rpinitiated-1_0.html

Signed-off-by: Nikita Vakula <programmistov.programmist@gmail.com>

Multipart download enhancements (#4021)

* fix(api): set blob response Content-Type from OCI descriptor

Blob HEAD responses had no Content-Type and GET responses echoed the
request's Accept header verbatim, which produced missing or malformed
media types and left multipart/byteranges parts without a per-part
Content-Type. This breaks OCI distribution-spec conformance and
consumers like stargz-snapshotter that need a well-formed layer media
type.

Add a blobResponseMediaType helper that resolves the descriptor's
MediaType via GetBlobDescriptorFromRepo and falls back to
application/octet-stream. Use it in CheckBlob (HEAD), GetBlob full
(200), GetBlob single-range (206), and per-part in
writeMultipartRanges (206 multipart). Lookup is deferred until after
the blob is known to exist.

Cover the new behaviour with mock-based unit tests in routes_test.go
and end-to-end assertions in TestPullRange.

Signed-off-by: Andrei Aaron <andreifdaaron@gmail.com>

* perf(api): stream multipart blob ranges lazily with precomputed Content-Length

writeMultipartRanges previously opened every range reader up front
and emitted no Content-Length, so an N-range request held N
concurrent storage readers (and their fds / read buffers) per
response window and forced chunked encoding on HTTP/1.1 — neither
friendly to proxies nor to fan-out scenarios like stargz lazy pulls.

ci: fix golangci-lint install URL (#4052)

1. Cause
SBOM assets were added to the release checksum file, so you get two lines that contain the same substring, e.g. …linux-amd64.tar.gz and …linux-amd64.tar.gz.sbom.json.
The old install.sh logic used something like grep "${BASENAME}", so both lines matched. That breaks want (wrong or ambiguous hash) and shows up as checksum verification errors (including the 8df… vs fd3… style mismatch you debugged).

2. The upstream fix is in https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/pull/6539
The matcher was changed so the checksum line must end with the archive name — i.e. grep "${BASENAME}$" — so the .sbom.json line no longer matches.

3. In the same thread they say master on raw.githubusercontent.com is not the right branch anymore and recommend the canonical installer URL:
https://golangci-lint.run/install.sh
(see the PR description and local install / binaries.)

Signed-off-by: Andrei Aaron <andreifdaaron@gmail.com>

fix(storage): treat dedupe-candidate cache miss as no candidates, not an error (#4122)

GetAllDedupeReposCandidates propagated zerr.ErrCacheMiss from the cache's
GetAllBlobs verbatim. But a cache miss is the normal case for a not-yet-cached
blob — the first push of a new blob, or a cross-repo mount check during a push
— and semantically means "no dedupe/mount candidates", not a failure.

Propagating it caused canMount (used by the CheckBlob and CreateBlobUpload
handlers) to surface the error, which the route handlers log as an
"unexpected error". With remote (e.g. S3) storage a cache is always present
(dedupe:false does not disable it), so this logs an error-level line for every
fresh blob digest on every push — significant log spam during bulk pushes and
cross-repo mounts, with no functional impact (the push still succeeds via a
normal upload).

Handle ErrCacheMiss the same way as the existing nil-cache branch above:
return no candidates and no error.

Signed-off-by: Janko Thyson <janko@kaosmaps.com>

mensagens_commits:
Fixup benchmark scripts (#3753)

* chmod local scripts

* Prefer `#!/usr/bin/env bash` over `#!/bin/bash`

Using `/usr/bin/env bash` will performa lookup for `bash` on the PATH while `/bin/bash` requires the exact absolute path to bash be at `/bin/bash`.

ci: helper.rb - catch error writing to `ENV['GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY']` file (#3752)

remove toplevel constants

Move sleep cluster logic to its own class (#3746)

* Move cluster logic to its own class

Simplify the calculation. This is an alternative to #3723.

Puma 6.6.1 behavior documented here https://gist.github.com/schneems/cef38e9448dfb72943d13050a7da0869

This changes the puma 7 behavior to:

- Starts sleeping the event loop before being overloaded (the prior `pool.busy_threads` included in the ready @todo queue) and would only fire. This is closer to puma 6.6.1 behavior
- Sleeps a consistent proportional amount, closer to puma 7 behavior, versus puma 6 used a static value.
- Sleeping behavior is restricted to 2 or more workers, verus puma 7 was accidentally enabled for clusters with only 1 worker

Fixes #3740. This `wait_for_less_busy_worker` value is now treated as a maximum value for the sleep calculation. It also now respects a value of 0 to mean "don't sleep at all" which was the prior behavior of that value.

* Whitespace

* Remove unused method

The busy_thread call is now accessed directly through the thread pool and only used in one place.

* Add docs about server <-> reactor relationship

The code doesn't make it clear who is calling whom when looking at it in isolation.

* Make maximum 25x thread count and allow for overage

Puma can take in more requests than it has threads. This change preserves the same logic as before, but it doesn't hit maximum sleep until it is at 25x the number of max threads. That means that if a server was using 5 threads,  before it would hit 0.005 sleep if those five threads were busy, now if (only) five threads are busy it will sleep 0.0002 seconds.

* Move order of comparison

If busy threads is zero we don't need to calculate percentage.

* Refactor out clamp

Because we're clamped at the numerator, the division will naturally tend towards 1.0. We don't need a second clamp on the result. This allows us to remove an intermediate variable and multiply directly on the return calculation.

* Lazy max_threads

There are proposals to make thread counts dynamic RE https://github.com/puma/puma/pull/3658. If this happens we need to pull in the current value, and cannot rely on it being set once.

* Avoid re-checking the `max_delay` number every iteration

* Refactor out branching

The equation already holds up the tested properties without needing to special-case when busy threads is zero. Removes a branching conditional.

* Push worker logic into delay class

The logic of whether or not the calculation should be performed based on worker count can be calculated once and not repeated on every iteration.

* Optimize case where no threads are busy

Moves the condition from checking if the delay is zero to checking if the input is zero earlier. This is prevents some calculations and preserves the same number of conditionals.

puma_http11.c: Use interned UTF-8 strings for hash keys (#3754)

* Call `rb_global_variable` before assigning to it

The API doc is quite clear the registration must be first:

```c
/**
 * Inform the garbage  collector that the global or static  variable pointed by
 * `valptr` stores  a live  Ruby object  that should not  be moved.   Note that
 * extensions  should use  this API  on  global constants  instead of  assuming
 * constants defined  in Ruby are  always alive.   Ruby code can  remove global
 * constants.
 *
 * Because this  registration itself has  a possibility  to trigger a  GC, this
 * function  must be  called  before any  GC-able objects  is  assigned to  the
 * address pointed by `valptr`.
 */
void rb_gc_register_address(VALUE *valptr);

/**
 * An alias for `rb_gc_register_address()`.
 */
void rb_global_variable(VALUE *);
```

* puma_http11.c: Use interned UTF-8 strings for hash keys

`rb_str_new2` creates a mutable, ASCII-8BIT (binary) strings.

Hence, when used with `rb_hash_aset`, ruby always has to lookup
the equivalent string in the fstring table, likely fail to find it,
then dup and free the given string, and use that as the hash key.

By keeping interned strings in these global variables, we can save
Ruby quite a bit of work. It's not a whole lot in the grand scheme
of things, but still welcome.

Strip whitespace from the beginnings of request header values. (#3742)

Whitespace is OWS, which is HTAB and SP.

Fix SSL_shutdown error handling (#3703)

* Fix SSL_shutdown error handling

SSL_shutdown() call may result in error and in OpenSSL every error
should be consumed by the caller via SSL_get_error() or a similar func.

MiniSSL implementation was breaking this convention so it resulted
in cryptic bugs like SSL clients (not related to Puma in any way)
return errors with text like "SSL_read: shutdown while in init" that
is initially generated by the Puma reactor but not consumed by it.

Such bugs are really hard to debug...

Remove global side effect from test (#3765)

## Before

This test asserts that when certain configuration options are specified that a custom load error is raised if concurrent-ruby cannot be found. It does this by: 

- finding the real file on disk-
- renaming the file
- running code and asserting an error with a specific message
- ensuring the file rename is reverted

Most developers would be surprised that running the test suite of one project might cause other code running on the same machine to fail, but because these modifications to disk are global, that's what happens.

## After

Instead of making a real system change, this mocks the interface where that file is loaded i.e. the "require" call:

```ruby
    def require_processor_counter
      require 'concurrent/utility/processor_counter'
    rescue LoadError
```

This is done by monkey patching the `require` method on the specific instance of Configuration under test. This means that not only does it have no side effects that are visible by other running processes on the same machine, other instances of the configuration class won't be affected.

To get this strategy to work we have to force the instance to re-parse the environment by explicitly calling the `puma_default_options` method (which in turn eventually calls the code that generates the warning). This is needed because the Puma::Configuration class eagerly evaluates the environment and calls this logic in the constructor

```ruby
module Puma
  # ...
  class Configuration
    # ...
    def initialize(user_options={}, default_options = {}, env = ENV, &block)
      default_options = self.puma_default_options(env).merge(default_options)
```

Reintroduce keepalive "fast inline" behavior: 8x faster performance (#3794)

* Refactor into a one iteration loop

* Reintroduce keepalive "fast inline" optimization

Short: This reintroduces a performance optimization dropped in Puma 7, and adds a guard to prevent "unfair" or "longtail" request distribution when the server is overloaded.

## Context

Puma 6 and before had a "fast inline" loop. A connection can have many requests, as an optimization, this "fast inline" feature would allow a Puma thread to respond to multiple requests on the same connection in a row without requiring that the connection be placed in the queue or the thread needing to go through mutex lock/unlock-ing to get it back. This improved preformance but created a "longtail" situation where one keepalive connection can "monopolize" a thread for up to 10 requests in a row. If all threads are busy, this blocks an incoming request for 10x the average time to serve a request, this was reported in https://github.com/puma/puma/issues/3487. 

Puma 7 changed this behavior to ensure that all responses are "fair" and that a keepalive connections cannot "monopolize" a thread. This eliminated the "longtail" behavior. 

Recently https://github.com/puma/puma/issues/3788 was opened to highlight that while MRI numbers on TechEmpower benchmarks look pretty decent, the JRuby ones fell off a cliff. Previously we worked on tuning/improving the MRI performance on a similar report against 7.0.0.pre1 https://github.com/puma/puma/issues/3715. We fixed that by removing an env var from the TechEmpower setup and increasing the default keepalive connection default. This new report with JRuby seems directly related to the overhead involved in coordinating between many threads. 

One way to think of this is with https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amdahl%27s_law. Where the amount of speedup in a system by adding a new resource is directly limited by the amount of coordination needed between resources. When a request is placed on the Puma queue, other threads all coordinate via mutexes and conditiona variables in-order to do book-keeping and only pull of the next  request in line. MRI also has a GIL/GVL, in addition to these locks, versus JRuby does not have a GIL, each thread can independently  run Ruby code. It seems that decreasing pressure on the locking mechanisms is much more important for JRuby than for Cruby (MRI).

A key fact in the prior "longtail" reproduction is that it only occurs when all Puma threads are busy, that is when Puma is overloaded. That is because if a thread is busy working on several requests in a row and a new request comes in, but can be picked up by another thread ... that request does not have to wait and can be served fairly.

## This change

This PR reintroduces the prior "fast inline" behavior to allow a thread to be monopolized, but with a key difference. This will only be allowed when Puma detects that there are idle threads waiting for a new request. If all threads are busy, it will put the next request on the connection in the queue for proper ordering. This approach preserves the Puma 7 "fair" ordering in addition to reintroducing the Puma 6 "fast inline" optimization.

Puma 6 had a setting `max_fast_inline` that would auto close a connection after a number of requests on it were served (default was 10). That was needed to prevent a DoS as otherwise an attacker could saturate all threads with keepalive connections and then prevent any new requests from being served. This change does NOT reintroduce this concept. Connections will be closed after they've reached the maximum keepalive number of requests (default is 999). As long as the system has excess capacity (spare threads), it is not at risk of DoS via this vector. As soon as all threads are saturated, it will not close the connection (as before) but instead place it in queue.

## Reproduction

Performance comparison using this script https://gist.github.com/schneems/bc7ee417007d467a63abcf793793b989/b51629f86f6e05e2afc52041875033c6bffa5012

```
$ git co <branchname> && ./tmp/profile_puma.sh
```

Results:

```
v6.6.1    Requests/sec: 116,403.14
v7.04     Requests/sec:  20,968.15
My branch Requests/sec: 169,514.68
```

Higher is better. Not only does this meet the performance of Puma 6, but it beats it.

Fix flaky test test_horrible_queries (#3857)

`test_horrible_queries` can be flaky, but it's very hard to detect.
This commit fixes the flakiness.  To understand the flakiness, let me
put the original test code below:

```ruby
 # then that large mangled field values are caught
10.times do |c|
  get = "GET /#{rand_data(10,120)} HTTP/1.1\r\nX-Test: #{rand_data(1024, 1024+(c*1024), false)}\r\n\r\n"
  assert_raises Puma::HttpParserError do
    parser.execute({}, get, 0)
    parser.reset
  end
end
```

The way I understand `rand_data(xxx, false)` is that the function should
_always_ return invalid bytes (IOW cause the parser to raise an
exception).

However, it is possible for that function to _sometimes_ return valid
bytes.  The above test asserts that an error is raised when
`parser.execute` is called, but if an exception gets raised, then
`parser.reset` isn't called.  If `parser.reset` isn't called, then
subsequent calls to `parser.execute` will raise an exception
_regardless_ of whether the input is parse-able or not.  In other words,
if the first iteration caused an exception, subsequent iterations are
guaranteed to raise an exception.

This commit does two things:

1. Pulls `parser.reset` outside of the assert_raises so that the flake
   is more obvious / reproducible
2. Changes `rand_data` to always add an invalid byte so that if the
   random data happens to contain parsable data, we'll at least have one
   byte guaranteed to fail.

<!-- Release notes generated using configuration in .github/release.yml at main -->

> [!WARNING]
> We have migrated all our documentation to the more complete and modern class `multidimensional.MMM`. See the migration guide: https://www.pymc-marketing.io/en/latest/notebooks/mmm/mmm_migration_guide.html
> We will remove the old `mmm.MMM` class in 0.20.0. Please migrate your code! Most changes are internal optimizations. The APIs are very similar!


## What's Changed
### Major Changes 🛠
* Default to unpooled transformation priors in Multidimensional MMM by @ricardoV94 in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2293
* CLV API Deprecation by @ColtAllen in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2347
### New Features 🎉
* Some fixes TimeSlice Cross Validation and Extend Case Study by @juanitorduz in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2393
* Validate YAML with Pydantic by @juanitorduz in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2418
### Bugfixes 🐛
* Raise explicitly when trying to optimize or measure incrementality of discrete channel data by @ricardoV94 in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2337
* bug : mlflow uses the name param on versions 3.0.0 and greater by @daniel-saunders-phil in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2339
* Respect channel ordering when applying budget bounds by @cetagostini in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2350
* Implement MultiDimensionalMMM with pymc.dims by @ricardoV94 in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2204
* Fix: Handle DateIndex in CSA plot_data to resolve crash (fixes #1864) by @shivamlalakiya in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2302
* remove superfluous use of `arbitrary_types_allowed` in  annotations by @nataziel in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2403
* BUG: HSGPKwargs.cov_func does not support custom Cov by @isofer in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2398
* fix nb: GAM NOTEBOOK BROKEN by @juanitorduz in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2416
* fix: work around RuntimeError by @williambdean in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2421
* Add compute_mean_contributions_over_time to MMM multidim by @juanitorduz in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2423
* Fix: Channel coordinates are alphabetically sorted in multidimensional MMM, causing ROAS calculation errors  by @juanitorduz in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2422

* Support cost_per_unit for channels with non-monetary data (impressions, clicks, etc.) - part 1 by @isofer in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2320

Respect channel ordering when applying budget bounds (#2350)

* Respect channel ordering when applying budget bounds

Fix bug where budget_bounds dict was applied in the wrong channel order by iterating over self.mmm_model.channel_columns. Use the optimizer's budget coordinate ordering (self._budget_coords[self._budget_dims[0]]) so per-channel bounds map to the correct channels. Add a regression test (test_dict_bounds_respect_channel_ordering) that uses non-alphabetical channel names and asymmetric bounds to ensure each channel's bound is respected. This addresses ordering-related failures (regression for #2323).

* Fix DataArray bounds ordering and add regression tests for #2323

Fix both dict and DataArray bounds paths in BudgetOptimizer.allocate_budget
to respect channel ordering when model coords differ from channel_columns.

Dict path (original PR): iterate _budget_coords instead of channel_columns.
DataArray path (new): add .reindex() before .transpose().values to align
the user-provided DataArray with internal coordinate ordering.

Add regression tests using real multidimensional MMM with non-alphabetical
channel names (2ch and 5ch), covering both dict and DataArray bounds paths.

Validate YAML structure and warn on unknown keys (#2409)

Add defensive parsing and validation for YAML configs and spec building. Introduces KNOWN_SPEC_KEYS and makes build() warn when a spec contains unknown keys (e.g. accidental top-level keys nested under a class). Adds _validate_config_structure() to detect common mis-indentation (keys like effects, calibration, original_scale_vars, data, idata_path nested under model) and raise a clear ValueError/TypeError. build_mmm_from_yaml() now calls the validator and treats calibration/effects/original_scale_vars/data robustly when they are None, avoiding silent failures. Tests added/updated to cover the new validation, factory warnings, None handling, and ordering of original_scale_vars, plus example YAML fixtures for mis-indented configs.
