Replace potential by likelihood in calibration by target (#2407)

* Replace potential by likelihood in calibration by target

* Ricardo & Teemu: Applying feedback

1. Refactor cost-per-target calibration to accept separate cost and target XTensor inputs instead of a precomputed CPT tensor. add_cost_per_target_observations now takes cost_value and target_value, computes ratio as mean(numerator)/mean(denominator) over the date dimension, clips the denominator to avoid instability, and adds an observed Normal likelihood per calibration row. A target_per_cost flag was added to flip the ratio (target-per-cost). The deprecated add_cost_per_target_potentials forwards to the new function with a warning. MMM now passes spend and original-scale contribution to the calibration helper and sets an internal _has_cpt_calibration flag so posterior predictive sampling excludes the calibration observed RV by default. Tests updated to provide cost/target tensors, exercise in-/out-of-sample posterior predictive behavior, and assert expected shapes and absence of calibration RVs in posterior predictive output. Documentation strings and examples were updated accordingly.

## What's Changed
### New Features 🎉
* Update serialization process (#2379) by @isofer in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2391
* Support fixed/user-defined scaling factors for stable model refreshes by @drbenvincent in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2479
### Bugfixes 🐛
* Fix Serialization LogNormal from YAML by @juanitorduz in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2476
* Fix: Latex rendering in new Adstock guide  by @timbo112711 in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2472
### Documentation 📖
* Porting causal identification notebook to MMM multidimensional [V2] by @juanitorduz in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2475
* Use arviz-darkgrid style globally for all plot directives via plot_pre_code by @williambdean in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2492
### Maintenance 🔧
* Move mmm-modeling skill out of dot-directory for crawler discovery by @lfiaschi in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2489
* Initial PR for MMMPlotSuite by @isofer in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2437
* Add DiagnosticsPlots class with 6 time-series diagnostic methods by @isofer in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2459
* fix: register xr.DataArray deserializer in SpecialPrior to fix save/load round-trip by @PabloRoque in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2496
* Bump version to 0.19.3 by @juanitorduz in https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/pull/2498


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/pymc-labs/pymc-marketing/compare/0.19.2...0.19.3

Support fixed/user-defined scaling factors for stable model refreshes (#2479)

* Support fixed/user-defined scaling factors for stable model refreshes (#2478)

Add method="fixed" to VariableScaling so users can pin scaling constants
that remain stable across production model refreshes, eliminating
scale-induced prior drift when data distributions change.

Made-with: Cursor

* Address review feedback: serialization, dict-valued scaling, key validation

- Fix legacy MMM serialization round-trip: use model_dump() in
  create_idata_attrs and pass value through in _deserialize_scaling so
  fixed scaling survives save/load.
- Support dict-valued fixed channel scaling in legacy MMM (per-channel
  constants keyed by column name); reject dict-valued target with a
  clear error since the 1-D MMM has a single target.
- Validate dict keys against coordinate labels in multidimensional MMM:
  report missing and unexpected keys explicitly instead of late KeyError
  or silent ignore.
- Add regression tests for all three fixes.

Made-with: Cursor

* Improve patch coverage: add tests, remove dead code

- Remove dead `scaling is None` branch in create_idata_attrs (scaling is
  always set in __init__)
- Replace isinstance guard with cast() for mypy narrowing
- Add test for dict-valued scaling with wrong remaining dims count
- Add tests for VariableScaling dims validation (date, duplicates)

Made-with: Cursor

* Restore legacy MMM scaling type check

This preserves the legacy TypeError contract for non-fixed scaling so the shard 5 edge-case test passes after the fixed-scaling refactor.

Made-with: Cursor

* Refactor VariableScaling into a two-class hierarchy

Split the single VariableScaling class into an abstract base with two
concrete subclasses (DataDerivedScaling and FixedScaling) to eliminate
the awkward optional value field and its cross-field validation, per
code review feedback.

- VariableScaling(ABC) keeps dims + _validate_dims
- DataDerivedScaling has method: Literal["max", "mean"]
- FixedScaling has value: float | dict[str, float] (non-optional)
- Scaling.to_dict/from_dict use the __type__ registry for polymorphic
  serialization; legacy format (no __type__) still loads correctly
- Updated legacy MMM and multidimensional MMM to use isinstance checks
  and the new concrete classes
- All 844 tests pass across test_scaling, test_mmm, test_multidimensional

Made-with: Cursor

* Extract _build_fixed_scale to eliminate multiple returns

Address review comment by refactoring _compute_scale_for_variable into
two methods: the main method now has a single return, dispatching to a
dedicated _build_fixed_scale helper for FixedScaling logic.

Made-with: Cursor

* Validate dict-valued FixedScaling keys at init, not build_model

Move the missing/extra key checks for dict-valued channel FixedScaling
from build_model() to MMM.__init__() in both legacy and multidimensional
implementations, so users get immediate feedback on key mismatches.

Made-with: Cursor

fix: register xr.DataArray deserializer in SpecialPrior to fix round-trip (#2496)

SpecialPrior.to_dict() serialises xr.DataArray parameter values via
xr.DataArray.to_dict(), but from_dict() dispatched any dict-valued kwarg
to pymc_extras.deserialize() which had no handler for that format,
causing DeserializableError on every multidimensional MMM with per-channel
priors (e.g. LogNormalPrior(mean=xr.DataArray(...), dims=('country', 'channel'))).

Fix: register _is_xarray_dataarray_dict / xr.DataArray.from_dict via
register_deserialization(), and add an explicit xr.DataArray branch in
to_dict()'s handle_value() before the generic hasattr check.

Four new tests: deserializer registration, full round-trip with coords,
non-centered variant, round-trip via top-level deserialize().

* Fix: Add 'color' to reserved_keys in waterfall plot to prevent TypeError

The waterfall method's _plot_waterfall_panel passes 'color' as an explicit
keyword argument to ax.barh(). If a user passes bar_kwargs with a 'color' key,
it would cause a TypeError for duplicate keyword arguments. This fix adds
'color' to the reserved_keys set to provide a helpful ValueError instead.

Applied via @cursor push command

* Fix waterfall plot to handle baseline without extra dimensions

The waterfall method previously assumed entries[0] (baseline) would always
have all extra dimensions (e.g., 'geo'). When the intercept is shared across
geos while channels are geo-specific, this caused a KeyError when accessing
ref_da.coords['geo'].

Fixed by:
1. Searching for an entry that has all extra dimensions instead of blindly
   using entries[0]
2. Falling back to constant_data coordinates if no entry has all dims
3. Only selecting dimensions that exist in each DataArray during panel
   extraction to avoid errors on scalar baseline DataArrays

Added test case for shared intercept across geos to prevent regression.

* Fix _select_dims to handle contributions with different dimensions

Filter dims dict to only include dimensions present in each DataArray
before validation. This prevents ValueError when calling waterfall() or
contributions_over_time() with dims like {'geo': ['CA']} on models where
baseline lacks the geo dimension but channels have it.

Add Zarr save/load support to ModelIO (zarr>=3 shim) (#2512)

* Add Zarr save/load support to ModelIO via xr.DataTree shim

arviz<1.0 InferenceData.to_zarr() / from_zarr() hard-error on zarr>=3.
Shim the gap using the same pattern arviz>=1.0 adopted:

  idata_to_zarr  -> idata.to_datatree().to_zarr(store)
  idata_from_zarr -> az.from_datatree(xr.open_datatree(store, engine='zarr'))

ModelIO.save() / load() now dispatch on .zarr extension, keeping full
backward compatibility with existing .nc files. Functions live in
pymc_marketing/data/idata/utils.py; pymc_marketing/utils.py re-exports
them for backward compatibility.

* docs: mark zarr shim as temporary

* fix: align zarr and netcdf model I/O

fix: restore original_scale Deterministics on MMM save/load round-trip (#2508)

* fix: validate_api_docs hook uses git ls-files instead of iterdir

The hook was scanning the filesystem with iterdir() which picked up untracked
files in the working tree, causing spurious failures. Switch to git ls-files
so only tracked files are considered.

* fix: restore original_scale Deterministics on MMM save/load round-trip

save() now writes the base names of any *_original_scale Deterministics to
idata.attrs["original_scale_vars"] (mirroring the mu_effects pattern).
build_from_idata() reads this attr after build_model() and re-adds the
Deterministics via add_original_scale_contribution_variable, with a fallback
that infers them from idata.posterior for artifacts saved before this fix.

* test: cover fallback path in build_from_idata for pre-fix idata artifacts

feat(mmm): parametrise GeometricAdstock by half-life (#2839)

* feat(mmm): parametrise GeometricAdstock by half-life

Reasoning about carryover in periods until the effect halves is more
intuitive than reasoning about a retention rate, so allow the geometric
decay to be given a prior on its half-life instead of on alpha.

The parametrisation is selected either by passing a "halflife" prior or
explicitly via parametrization="halflife". Alpha is then derived inline as
0.5 ** (1 / halflife), which keeps it in (0, 1) for any positive half-life.

* fix(mmm): match half-life default prior to the alpha default

Address review feedback on the half-life parametrisation of
GeometricAdstock.

The previous Gamma(mu=2, sigma=1) default implied a median alpha of 0.69
against 0.21 under the Beta(1, 3) alpha default, so switching
parametrization silently changed the model rather than only the
coordinates. Because 1 / h = -log2(alpha) and Beta(1, 3) is the minimum
of three uniforms, 1 / h is the maximum of three Exp(1) draws over ln 2,
which makes the half-life close to inverse-gamma rather than gamma. The
new InverseGamma(2.6, 1) default reproduces the implied median alpha to
0.207 against 0.206, and its density vanishing at the origin keeps
samplers away from the region where d alpha / d h underflows to zero.

Also make the parametrization contradiction check symmetric, since an
explicit parametrization="alpha" combined with a halflife prior was
silently overridden, and restore signature-based checking in
_has_defaults_for_all_arguments so subclasses overriding function keep
the guard.

* docs(mmm): move half-life detail from the docstring into the guide

The GeometricAdstock docstring had accumulated three paragraphs of
half-life prose. Keep the mapping, the note that the trace holds
adstock_halflife instead of adstock_alpha, and a two-sentence pointer to
the guide, which now carries the reasoning: why truncation and
normalization preserve the half-life, why the default is inverse-gamma
rather than gamma, and why a custom prior must avoid zero.

* docs(mmm): trade the inverse-gamma derivation for the implied alpha tails

The reason the half-life default is inverse-gamma rather than gamma is of
little use to a reader choosing a prior; how closely the two defaults agree
is, so quote the 5th and 95th percentiles of alpha alongside the median.

* fix(mmm): reject priors for the inactive adstock parametrisation

The conflict check ran only when parametrization was passed explicitly, so
priors for both alpha and halflife were accepted, one of them silently
ignored, and then serialised together with the inferred parametrization into
something from_dict refuses to load. Moving the check into the function_priors
setter closes both that path and assignment after construction, since
Transformation.__init__ assigns through the same setter.

Also drop a deepcopy the setter already performs, and quote the implied median
half-life, which the docstring reported only as an alpha.

docs(skills): fix az.plot_trace call broken under ArviZ 1.x (#2842)

The mmm-modeling skill still taught `az.plot_trace(data=mmm.fit_result, ...)`,
which raises `TypeError: plot_trace() missing 1 required positional argument:
'dt'` under the ArviZ >= 1.2 pin (the first parameter was renamed and the
legacy signature removed). Replace both call sites with
`az.plot_trace_dist(mmm.fit_result, ...)`, matching the pattern used in the
mmm_quickstart notebook. Verified against arviz 1.2.0: the old call fails, the
new one renders trace + distribution panels as before.

alongside custom ones.

* Fix MemoryError (std::bad_alloc) in mmm_evaluation notebook CI (#2669)

The "Test Notebooks" job for `mmm --start-idx 10` was failing with
`MemoryError: std::bad_alloc` while rendering the RMSE-distribution plot
in mmm_evaluation.ipynb.

Root cause: under CI the sampler is mocked (pm.sample -> mock_sample), so
the posterior-predictive draws are not meaningful and the resulting RMSE
distribution spans a huge range (up to ~6e6). The cell forced
`ax.set_xlim(0, 500)`, which compresses the data->display scale so that
the KDE line (extending to ~6e6) maps to an enormous physical extent. The
inline backend renders with `bbox_inches="tight"`, and `get_tightbbox`
does not respect axes clipping, so it computed a ~21,640-inch-wide figure
=> ~4.3M x 1.3k pixel Agg renderer => std::bad_alloc.

Fix: drop the hard-coded `ax.set_xlim(0, 500)` and let the axis
autoscale, matching the sibling R-squared cell (which has no xlim and was
always safe). For a real fit the RMSE distribution and both reference
lines sit in a narrow range, so the rendered figure is equivalent; under
the mocked CI sampler the figure now renders at a sane size.

Verified with the exact CI runner:
`uv run python scripts/run_notebooks/runner.py --notebooks docs/source/notebooks/mmm/mmm_evaluation.ipynb`
-> "Notebooks run successfully!"

Make incrementality correct beyond the additive case: link-aware reduction, mediated mu_effects, and pm.do interventions (#2813)

* Fix incrementality for non-additive links

* Fix panel mean-scale incrementality and widen log-link coverage

central_tendency="mean" crashed for panel log-link models. The LogNormal
correction keeps the model's custom dims, but _stack_samples was asked to
flatten it to (sample,) alone, so transpose("chain", "draw") dropped
"country" and raised. It now infers and preserves every non-sample
dimension along with its coordinates, so the correction applies per
custom-dim cell. Both call sites get simpler: the reduction already
broadcasts by dimension name, so the baseline no longer spells out its dims.

Test coverage follows the same fault lines: the per-channel oracle now spans
controls, time-varying media, panel monthly/marginal/no-carryover, and spend
factors of 0.5 and exactly 1.0. A new test pins the direction of the
multiplicative overlap, since per-channel increments overstate the joint
knock-out rather than summing to it. The multi-chain subsampling test used a
duplicated posterior, which made it blind to a chain-major/draw-major mix-up;
the chains now differ and the selected draws are checked explicitly.

Also corrects dimension-order claims that still said (channel, *custom_dims),
and documents that a zero spend factor is a spend intervention, not removal
of a channel's effect.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* Include channel-dependent mu_effects in incrementality (#2815)

* Include channel-dependent mu_effects in incrementality

A spend counterfactual was assumed to reach the response only through
channel_contribution. A mu_effect can read channel_data itself -- a funnel
mediator does -- and that part of the incremental response was silently
dropped, reporting the direct path as if it were the total.

Effects now join the increment additively in the linear predictor,
Dmu = Dv + sum_j De_j, which goes to the same IncrementalReducer as before;
the reducer hierarchy and the log-link algebra are untouched.

- MuEffect.incrementality_spec() is an opt-in. A spend-dependent effect that
  has not opted in raises NotImplementedError instead of being dropped.
  Effects independent of spend cancel in the difference and are skipped
  without being consulted, so nothing existing has to change.
- Date-indexed pm.Data an effect reads is discovered from the graph, so an
  effect cannot forget to declare one. Only its additional carryover length
  is declared, and the evaluation window is sized for the longest path.
- One counterfactual per channel when an effect is present: a funnel sums
  over channels inside a nonlinear transform, so no per-channel column
  survives to be read off a single all-channels perturbation. The separable
  case keeps one scenario per period and costs what it did before.
- Evaluation windows are clamped to the fitted dates rather than zero-padded
  past them. Padding is inert for spend but not for an effect whose
  contribution at zero spend is its own intercept, where it injected

* fix(mmm): exclude the last axis date from spend-probe eligibility

SpendProbe._select_probe_indices excluded only the first date. An
ordinary flighted model, dark through the head with spend growing
toward the end, could probe the final date: pick()'s argmax fallback
had nothing to stop it, on both the per-channel and covering paths. An
impulse at the last date has no later date to move, so in _reach_of
last_moved == n_dates - 1 and every node reads full-axis regardless of
its true reach, a silent slowdown today and one that defeats the
planned full-axis carryover fix, whose truncation bound a last-date
probe would report as zero.

Exclude the last date from eligibility symmetrically with the first
(eligible = per_date[1:-1]), add the mirrored only_last guard so a
channel reachable only at an axis edge returns no probe, and tighten
the n_dates guard from < 2 to < 3 to match. In the corner this newly
disables, the fix trades a live completeness check for the warned
full-axis fallback; a net win since the alternative was a silent tail
cut.

* fix(mmm): sum the whole carry-out under full-axis evaluation

Full-axis evaluation is selected when the probe cannot put a number on some
node's reach: it saw the node still moving the last fitted date, or moving
dates before the perturbed one. The window then spanned every date, but the
dates entering each period's *sum* were still bounded by end + effective_l_max,
and TemporalReach.full_axis() hard-coded additional_carryover_lags=0, so for an
effect declaring nothing that bound collapsed to the model's own l_max. The
mediated tail past it was computed correctly and then dropped, and increments
and ROAS came back low with no warning.

Two changes close it. EvaluationWindows.build now runs the evaluation range to
the axis end when full_axis is set and carryover is included; this is exactly
safe, because for a date the perturbation does not reach the counterfactual and
the baseline are the same computation on the same inputs and the extra summands
are exactly zero. And _reach_of now carries the lag lower bound the probe did
establish into the full-axis reach, so _reconcile_declarations can still refuse
a declaration narrower than what was plainly measured.

The oracle in test_a_global_effect_selects_full_axis_evaluation is corrected to
sum to the axis end for the same reason: a perturbation that moves every date
has no tail length to stop at, so the old l_max window left out moves the effect
demonstrably makes. The correction is to the oracle, not to the assertion.

The estimand boundary this leaves is recorded in the EvaluationWindows
docstring: a date-reducing node also moves dates before the period, and those
moves stay out of the sum under every variant, because a period's increment is
read as forward-looking and overlapping periods would not be a decomposition.

* test(mmm): pin the full-axis lag bound, and fix the refusal it enables

Carrying the measured lag lower bound into a full-axis TemporalReach was
untested, and it made the under-declaration refusal reachable where it never
was before: an effect declaring additional_carryover_lags=N whose reach
measures full-axis now raises. The message that refusal emitted was written
for the windowed case and is false there, because under full-axis evaluation
the sum runs to the axis end and no window cuts anything.

_reconcile_declarations now branches the message on the measurement's own
requires_full_axis. The full-axis wording says the tail could not be bounded,
that nothing is cut, and that the declaration is refused for being false rather
than for shortening the increment; it also quantifies the measurement as "at
least N", which is what a lower bound supports. The bounded case is unchanged
and still covered by test_under_declared_carryover_is_refused.

Two tests in TestSpendProbe cover the behaviour. One pins that a full-axis
measurement carries max(last_moved - probe_index - l_max, 0) lags, asserted
both as the expression and as a literal. The other, parametrized over
evaluation_mode auto and full, exercises the refusal against a declaration
narrower than a full-axis measurement and asserts the message no longer claims
a window would cut the tail. Both fail with the lag bound reverted.

* fix(mmm): account for float32 cancellation noise in completeness tolerance

SpendProbe.assert_increment_is_complete compared two full-magnitude
evaluations whose rounding floor is eps(dtype) * |node|, not eps * |move|,
while the tolerance was proportional only to the move's own scale. Under
float32 this spuriously raised the unattributed-spend NotImplementedError
for moves small relative to the node magnitudes. The tolerance now also
floors at COMPLETENESS_ACCUMULATION_SAFETY_FACTOR * eps * node_magnitude,
with eps read from the compared arrays' actual dtype and node_magnitude
taken over every compared node (predictor, channel_contribution, and each
effect contribution var) so float64 models are unaffected.

* fix(mmm): refuse an ambiguous linear predictor and say when the check is skipped

Recovering the linear predictor by the name "mu" took the first match in an
unordered graph traversal, in two places that had drifted apart: one rooted at
the observed variable, the other at the observed plus the deterministics. A
user-added intermediate carrying the same name would bind the completeness
check to the wrong quantity, nondeterministically, and the check would then
either refuse a correct model or pass a broken one without saying a word.

ambiguous name rather than guessing, and both root the search at the observed
plus the deterministics. One collision stays out of reach and is documented: a
user-registered Deterministic named "mu" is found by the named_vars lookup
before any graph search runs.

increment's completeness goes unverified instead of dropping the guarantee in

* fix(mmm): refuse a counterfactual evaluated on a mutated auxiliary input

CounterfactualEvaluator snapshotted date-indexed auxiliary inputs (control
data, seasonality, mediator data) straight off the live model's shared
variables. A same-length in-place mutation after fitting -- via
MMM.sample_posterior_predictive(..., clone_model=False) or a direct

* docs: fix RST inline-literal warnings in the optimization variables module

Sphinx builds with warnings treated as errors, and ``DataArray``s puts a
word character straight after inline markup, which docutils cannot parse
("Inline literal start-string without end-string"). Three warnings, all
introduced by this branch. Rephrased to ``DataArray`` objects; every
docstring in the module now renders clean.

* fix(budget-optimizer): align every coordinate-bearing input, not just the mask

Adversarial review of #2879 found two regressions introduced by the mask
alignment and four pre-existing bugs in the paths it touches. All are
fixed here through one shared abstraction rather than scattered guards.

align_to_model_coords() is now the single place a labelled input is put
into the model's coordinate frame. Reindexing alone is unsafe in both
directions: it drops labels the model does not have and fills missing
ones with NaN, so both are rejected. Four inputs go through it:

- budget_distribution_over_period was never reindexed, so once the mask
  was realigned the two disagreed positionally and each channel received
  another channel's temporal profile (regression).
- budgets_to_optimize silently dropped entries for channels absent from
  the model, where the old code raised on the shape mismatch; a typo'd
  or stale channel vanished and its budget was redistributed
  (regression).
- cost_per_unit was validated before reindexing, so a coordinate the
  model had but the input lacked became NaN and reached the graph.
- budget_bounds had no post-reindex check, handing scipy (nan, nan).

channel_scales is now divided after the spreading branch rather than
inside it. Scaling is elementwise per channel and spreading elementwise
per period, so the two commute: the uniform path is unchanged and the
temporal path, which built its result from the raw flat vector and so
never saw the division, is fixed. Its docstring claimed the old order
and now matches.

Also: optimized_vars carries the non-media part of the solution rather
than discarding it, an empty mask is rejected at construction instead of
dividing by zero later, budget_bounds=None uses the media variable's own
default_bounds instead of re-implementing them, and FLAT_DIM replaces
three independent spellings of the flat dimension's name.

feat(mmm): co-optimize named pm.Data levers alongside the media budgets (#2884)

* feat(mmm): co-optimize named pm.Data levers alongside the media budgets

Adds LeverVariable and the optimizable_vars field, so any pm.Data node
with a single non-date dim can be optimized jointly with the budgets.
Levers are optimized in their own units: the forward map is the identity
up to relabelling the flat dimension, the warm start is the node's
current model value clipped to its bounds, and they stay out of the
default budget-sum constraint, since a discount depth is not money drawn
from a shared pool.

Everything else comes from the existing abstraction. One flat vector, one
do() substitution, so the Jacobian covers media and levers jointly and
cross-partials between them are correct by construction rather than by
alternating two separate solves. Optimal values are returned in
result.optimized_vars, which the abstraction already populated.

The optimizer stays a graph-level tool: levers are declared by variable
name and nothing about effects or marketing conventions is imported,
which an AST guard test enforces.

Two guards, both exact rather than heuristic:

- Construction-time reachability. A lever the response variable cannot
  reach has an identically zero gradient, so the solver would return its
  warm start and report it as optimal. Graph ancestry answers this before
  anything is compiled, and it fires in practice: declaring a lever
  against the media-only objective is rejected.
- Bounds and dim validation at construction, so a wrong-length bounds
  list or a date-varying node fails before compilation.

BudgetOptimizer.optimization_variables is now public, because constraining
anything other than the media budgets requires reaching a variable's
segment of the flat vector. A test binds a lever through a custom
constraint using only public API.

Also closes a coverage gap left by #2879: a lever is the first genuine
second variable, so the container's isel branch, the slice layout and the
concatenation of bounds and x0 across variables now run in CI.

* feat(mmm): let a variable declare what it spends from the budget

The default sum constraint totalled the media tensor alone, so any
second monetary variable would have been optimized for free. It now
totals whatever each variable reports through budget_contribution,
which defaults to None: a lever is optimized in its own units and does
not draw from the pot, while media reports the monetary tensor it
already builds.

This is a seam rather than a feature. Behaviour is unchanged, since
media remains the only contributor, but it is the piece reach-and-
frequency budgets (#1968) and funnel spend both need, and adding it
here means neither has to change the protocol later.

A method rather than a flag, because the constraint cannot reconstruct
a variable's monetary amount generically: media applies channel_scales,
reach-and-frequency would apply cost_per_unit. Each variable is the only
thing that knows what its slice costs. The contract follows the media
convention of per-period rates rather than horizon totals, since the
constraint sums the contributions directly.

Tested with a stand-in spend variable: two monetary variables total
together, and a lever stays out.

* refactor(mmm): build levers from the model in LeverVariable.from_model

The optimizer hand-rolled the model introspection for every optimizable_vars
entry: look the name up in named_vars_to_dims, reject nodes without named dims
or with a date-varying/multi dim, then read coords and the current value back
off the model. All of that is knowledge about what a lever is, not about how
the optimizer is assembled, so it moves onto LeverVariable as a from_model
classmethod and the optimizer keeps a comprehension.

Error messages are unchanged, so the existing optimizer-level validation tests
still cover the same behaviour. The checks are now reachable without building a
BudgetOptimizer, which is where the new unit tests exercise them.

Also from the pre-review: OptimizationVariables.variables becomes a tuple so
the public accessor cannot be appended to, which would silently desynchronise
the slice layout from the flat input; and LeverVariable documents that its warm
start is read once at construction, consistent with the objective graph being
frozen there too.

feat(mmm): an objective that sees mu-effect contributions (total_response_original_scale) (#2895)

* feat(mmm): an objective the optimizer can point at when effects carry response

`total_media_contribution_original_scale` is built from the channel
contribution tensor alone, so any response routed through a mu effect -- a
funnel mediator, a promotional lever -- is invisible to it. A budget optimized
against it therefore undervalues whatever drives that effect, silently. #2890
measured this on a real funnel model: the media-only objective sees 68% of the
media-driven response and flips the sign of one recommendation.

Register `total_response_original_scale` when the model has mu effects. It is
the total predicted response in original units, built through the existing
`original_scale_transform`, so it is correct under both links by construction
rather than by a per-link formula. `LeverVariable` was already documented as
needing this variable; until now it did not exist.

Registered only when there are mu effects, so plain media models keep their
posterior unchanged, and the default response variable is untouched -- the
optimizer's construction-time reachability check already errors when a declared
lever cannot reach the chosen objective, so wrong usage fails loudly. Choosing
the default belongs with the funnel work, where #2890's numbers can validate it.

The docstring is explicit that this is a response total, not a media
attribution: it includes the baseline, which is an additive constant for the
default mean utility but not for a risk-adjusted one, and in an optimization
model the sum spans the adstock carry-over tail.

Note for effect authors: under the identity link `mu` was previously never
computed as a deterministic, so a contribution carrying a `date` dim of the
wrong length went unnoticed. It is now evaluated, which is why the serialization
fixture's length-1 stand-in becomes a full-length one here.

* docs(mmm): point users at the objective that sees mu-effect contributions

The variable was named only where it is defined, so nothing led a user to it
from the places they actually read: the two `response_variable` parameters and
the optimizer's list of what a model must expose. A funnel or lever model would
keep silently optimizing against the media-only default.

Also state it on `LeverVariable`, which is the case where the default is not
merely imprecise but inert: a lever the response variable cannot reach has an
identically zero gradient, and the optimizer refuses it at construction.

* fix(mmm): warn when a mu-effect model optimizes the media-only objective

The optimizer's reachability check only fires for declared levers, so a model
with effects and no levers could pass through `budget_optimizer()` without a
response variable and silently score against an objective that cannot see its
effects. That is the failure this objective exists to prevent, and a docstring
is not a check.

Resolve the objective in the layer that knows the model has effects, and warn
there when the caller expressed no preference. An explicit `response_variable`
is a deliberate choice and stays silent, including when it is the default --
media-only attribution is a legitimate thing to ask for.

Also state the summation contract: the date axis is summed first, then every
remaining dimension, which is right for one shared budget and wrong for
segments holding separate budgets.

* fix(mmm): treat an explicit response_variable=None as an omission

`"response_variable" not in kwargs` is False when the key is present and None,
so an explicit None skipped resolution and reached BudgetOptimizer, where
Pydantic rejected it as a type error rather than reporting the real problem.
Resolving from `kwargs.get` handles the omitted and the explicitly-None cases
identically.

Also pin the warning's stacklevel with a test asserting it blames the caller's
file: at stacklevel=2 it blames mmm.py, which is what the assertion catches.

`_resolve_response_variable` keeps its str-passthrough branch: the deprecated
`BudgetOptimizerWrapper.optimize_budget` forwards the caller's value straight
into it, so that path is live from both entry points, and the docstring now
says so.

* fix(mmm): warn only when an effect actually carries media response

`if self.mu_effects` was the wrong predicate. Events, trends, Fourier terms and
controls are all MuEffect subclasses and none of them are downstream of the
channel data, so the media objective is exactly right for those models. Warning
about them told every existing events or trend user that their already-correct
objective undercounts, and offered to silence it by restating the default.

The property that matters is graph reachability: does the effect's contribution
have the channel data among its ancestors, as a funnel mediator does. That is
the same question `_set_optimization_model` already asks of the response
variable, so it uses the same `ancestors` traversal. An effect that does not
name its contribution cannot be checked and is treated as though it might carry
response -- a spurious warning is recoverable, a silently undercounted
objective is not.

Also from review:

- Drop the redundant `.sum(dim="date")`; the bare `.sum()` already reduces every
  dimension, so the first reduction only asserted that a `date` dim exists while
  hardcoding a name one layer below a configurable `date_dim`. The `sum(dim=)`
  in `create_media_contribution_deterministic` stays: there it is load-bearing
  for the `* target_scale` broadcast that follows.
- Give the default objective one home, `DEFAULT_RESPONSE_VARIABLE` in
  budget_optimizer, referenced by the Field default and by MMM, rather than a
  constant on one side and a literal on the other.
- Note on `response_variable` that the warning is an MMM-layer convenience:
  constructing BudgetOptimizer directly has no view of the model's effects, so
  silence there is not evidence the default is right.
- Note that under the log link this sums the conditional median, pointing at
  `mean_correction` for the factor; the argmax is unaffected because it is
  per-draw and budget-independent.

Tests now run the warning cases through both public entry points, and a
LinearTrendEffect model pins the negative case: with the old predicate it warns.

fix(mmm): a correct optimization window — effect data, observed inputs, carry-in, effective carryover (#2898)

* fix(mmm): carry mu-effect data into the optimization window

`create_zero_dataset` built only `_channel` and `_control`, and
`DataVarMuEffect.set_data` sets only what the dataset carries, so an effect's
`pm.Data` silently kept its fit-time length. In-sample the lengths happen to
agree and nothing looks wrong; every other window fails on shape, which is why
optimizing a funnel model over a future window currently requires
`pm.set_data`-ing the effect's variables by hand purely to fix their shape
before handing the model to BudgetOptimizer.

`create_zero_dataset` now fills the variables the model's effects read, taking
dims and non-date coords from the training variable so the result differs only
in length along `date`. A variable without a date dim is passed through
unchanged: nothing about the window affects it. It reads `data_vars` off each
effect directly, matching how the function already treats its `model` argument.

Zeros, because a future window has no committed activity by default. Planning
against one that does needs no new parameter: set the variable on the model and
pass that model to BudgetOptimizer, which is what its `model` + `idata`
signature is for. That path only works once the variable is present at the
window's length, which is what this fixes.

* test(mmm): cover the three guards in the mu-effect data fill

Codecov flagged 70% patch coverage: the three branches that decide *not*
to fill a variable were never exercised. Each encodes a real guarantee,
so each gets a test rather than a pragma.

- a variable the training data lacks raises, naming the effect, instead
  of surfacing later as a bare KeyError from the dataset
- a variable with no date dim is left alone; filling it would replace a
  constant (a population, a per-channel rate) with zeros
- a variable the dataset already carries is not overwritten, so the
  spend `_channel` holds -- the decision variable itself -- survives

Mutation-checked: disabling each guard fails exactly its own test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(mmm): flatten the mu-effect data fill

Separates which variables need building from how they get built. The
selection is now a dict comprehension over the effects, so the fill loop
runs once per variable rather than once per (effect, variable) pair, and
two effects reading the same variable no longer race through a `continue`.

Three exits at two nesting levels become two at one, and the date test
reads positively -- fill what varies by date -- rather than as a skip.

Also records why this duck-types instead of `isinstance(effect,
DataVarMuEffect)`, which is the first thing a reader will reach for:
`utils` imports nothing from the package, and `additive_effect` reaches
back here through `events`, so naming the class closes an import cycle.

Behaviour unchanged; each guard still fails exactly its own test when
disabled.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(mmm): correct create_zero_dataset's contract, and cover multi-dim effect vars

The docstring described the function as it was before this branch, and one
line was wrong before it: `include_carryover` claimed to give adstock
"enough leading observations", but the code extends `end_date`. The
extension is trailing -- it scores the carry-over that window spend
produces after it -- and nothing is prepended, so the window starts from a
cold adstock state. Says so now, since the same prepend/append confusion
already exists in BudgetOptimizer's own parameter docs.

Also records what zeros mean in-sample: an exogenous series the effect
reads comes back as zero rather than at its fitted value, which is a

* feat(mmm): carry_in, so an in-sample window reproduces history

Zero-filling the effect variables is right for a future window and wrong
for one that overlaps training: re-optimizing history is a counterfactual
on the spend alone, so every other input should still hold the value the
posterior was fitted to. Zeroed, an exogenous series the effect reads --
a category-demand index, a committed budget -- silently leaves the model
scoring a different scenario than the one it was fitted to.

`carry_in=True` takes the observed value on every date the training data
covers and falls back to zero on the rest. That single rule needs no
knowledge of which kind of window it was handed: it reproduces history
in-sample and decays to the existing zeros on genuinely future dates,
where nothing is covered. It is one conditional, because `reindex` was
already doing the work and `zeros_like` was throwing it away.

`_channel` is deliberately untouched -- it is the decision variable.
Controls follow the same rule as the effect variables, since a zeroed
control breaks the same identity.

Defaults to False, so nothing changes unless asked. The in-sample window
is the only place the flag is observable, so that is where the default is
pinned; mutating it in either direction fails exactly one test.

Renames the flag to what it does. It restores observed values for

block of real spend before the window and lives in

It is also not a choice. Optimizing an in-sample window against zeroed

* feat(mmm): open the optimization window on the spend that preceded it

Optimizing from t0+1 started the adstock cold, as if the business went dark
before the plan. Because adstock feeds saturation this is not an additive
constant: it moves the operating point over the first l_max periods and so
changes the marginal return the optimizer equalises. The data was never
missing -- it is the tail of the training set.

The date axis is now three blocks and only the middle one is decided:

    [ spend already made ][ decisions ][ zero-spend carry-over ]

`pm.do` replaces the channel tensor wholesale, so the leading block cannot
just sit in the model's data and be left alone; `MediaVariable` re-emits it
as a constant, read by `BudgetOptimizer` off the model it was handed rather
than from anything that knows what an MMM is. `create_zero_dataset` takes
its leading dates from the training index, so they are real observed dates
and the count clips itself near the start of training.

`num_periods` now subtracts both flanking blocks. Subtracting only the tail
turns history into decisions and spreads budget over the past; that failure
is pinned by two tests.

Measured on the funnel fixture (l_max=3, 8-period window), carry-in moves
the allocation by 0.036%. Small here, and worth stating plainly rather than
implying otherwise: the fixture's window is long relative to its adstock and
it sits on a near-linear stretch of the saturation curve. The correction
grows as the window shortens relative to l_max.

* feat(mmm): co-optimize a second monetary variable with the media budgets

A funnel's lower-funnel spend is a decision, not an input, and it is money,
so it belongs in the same pot as the media budgets. `LeverVariable` cannot
carry it: a lever is optimized in its own units and deliberately sits
outside the budget-sum constraint. It rides the media path over a different
node instead.

`spend_vars` names the additional pm.Data nodes. Each becomes a
MediaVariable over its own non-date dims, so it gets the window's three
blocks, cost-per-unit conversion and mask scatter for free, and reports its
spend through `budget_contribution` -- which is how it joins the default
sum constraint with **constraints.py untouched**. That seam shipped in
#2884 with one implementor; this is the second.

Three things the generalisation needed:

- `scales_dims`, so a scales array over ("geo",) broadcasts correctly. The
  hardcoded ("channel",) only ever applied to array scales, which is why a
  scalar-scaled spend variable worked without it.
- `MediaVariable.from_model`, reading dims, coords and dtype off the model
  the way `LeverVariable.from_model` already does, so budget_optimizer.py
  gains no model introspection of its own.
- A scatter that recognises a 0-dimensional mask. A budget decided over
  date alone -- a single national spend -- has no cells, and pytensor
  cannot index with a scalar boolean.

`x0` now shares one budget across the cells of every spending variable
rather than handing each the whole of it, which would start the solver at
twice the budget, outside an equality constraint. Asserted on the guess
itself: SLSQP recovered from the infeasible start on the funnel fixture, so
no optimum would have revealed it.

An unreachable spend variable is refused like an unreachable lever, and for
a sharper reason: it still draws from the budget, so the solver funds it
from media and gets nothing back.

Measured on the funnel fixture, media and lower-funnel spend reach a joint
interior optimum and the split is exact:

    total=  10.0  media= 10.000  lf_budget=  0.000
    total=  50.0  media= 36.514  lf_budget= 13.486
    total= 200.0  media=123.204  lf_budget= 76.796
    total=1000.0  media=640.279  lf_budget=359.721

At a small budget media wins outright; as it saturates the lower funnel
becomes worth funding.

test(clv): fix flaky GammaGammaModel convergence test (#2913)

TestGammaGammaModel.test_model_convergence intermittently failed on the
posterior mean of p, e.g.

    Mismatch at index [0]: 8.115 (ACTUAL), 6.0 (DESIRED)
    Max relative difference among violations: 0.353

The aggregated Gamma-Gamma likelihood (Eq 1a) constrains q and the
population mean spend p * v / (q - 1), but not p and v separately: the
posterior has a p-v ridge. Under the model's default HalfFlat priors it
is not identified at all, so the only thing bounding p in this test is
the HalfNormal(sigma=10) prior the test happens to set.

Measured over 15 seeds on the aggregated model (2 chains, N=1000):

    p           mean rel. err 0.259, max 0.318  -> fails rtol=0.3 in 1/15
    q           mean rel. err 0.052
    v           mean rel. err 0.156
    p*v/(q-1)   mean rel. err 0.009, max 0.011

So the old assertion sat right on its own tolerance boundary and tipped
over on sampler/seed jitter. The 94% credible interval for p spans about
[3.7, 16.2] against a truth of 6.0.

Assert point recovery on the identified quantities (q at rtol=0.15,
p*v/(q-1) at rtol=0.1, both with roughly 10x margin) and interval
coverage on p and v, which held 15/15 seeds. The rewritten test passed
10/10 consecutive runs.

TestGammaGammaModelIndividual.test_model_convergence is left as is: that
model conditions on individual transactions, which identifies p directly
(rel. err 0.017 over 6 seeds), so it is not marginal.

* fix(clv): address review feedback on the ECDF plot_type

- Evaluate the ECDF on the attainable integer counts instead of a 100-point
  linspace, and guard against a degenerate single-count dataset.
- Rename the band label to "95% simultaneous band"; it is a simultaneous
  confidence band, not an HDI. Document that the band is conservative for
  discrete data, since it assumes a continuous reference CDF.
- Relabel the y axes, which carry proportions rather than percentages.
- Drop the synthetic leading riser so the curve and the band share one grid,
  and the difference panel is drawn consistently with the ECDF panel.
- Validate 'ax' up front instead of failing on tuple unpacking, raise
  ValueError for an unknown 'plot_type', forward **kwargs to the ECDF helper,
  and warn when 'max_purchases' is ignored.
- Pin arviz-stats to a single minor, since arviz_stats.ecdf_utils is not part
  of its public API.
- Fix the axes fixtures in the tests, which aliased one Axes into both panels
  and leaked a figure at collection time, and assert on the plotted output.

* test(clv): trim an inaccurate comment on the band assertion

* fix(clv): build the ECDF reference CDF from many predictive samples

The ECDF confidence band treats the predictive CDF as known. That held for a
sampled posterior, where the predictive draws are (chain * draw * customer),
but not for a point-estimate fit: `distribution_new_customer` only expands the
draw dimension when the posterior holds a single draw, so the hardcoded
`n_samples=1` gave exactly one predictive value per customer. Both curves then
carried sampling error of the same order and the band came out too narrow.
Simulated coverage of the nominal 95% band on negative-binomial counts with
n = 2357 was 0.28, against the 0.93 an exact reference CDF achieves.

Pass `samples` through instead, and warn when the predictive sample is under 20
per observation. A warning rather than an error because a short fit is still
worth looking at once the band is known to be optimistic.

Also drop the claim that the band is conservative on discrete data. With an
exact reference CDF the measured coverage is 0.93 against a nominal 0.95, so it
is marginally liberal, not conservative.

* fix(clv): only draw the extra predictive samples for the ECDF band

Passing `n_samples=samples` unconditionally also applied to the histogram, which
does not need a precise reference CDF. For a point-estimate fit on 100k
customers that turned a 1.6 MB predictive array into a 1.6 GB one on the default
plot. Pass it only on the 'ecdf' branch.

Also finish the `ax` validation: a sequence of length two whose elements are not
Axes, such as `plt.subplots(2, 2)[1]`, got past the check and failed later with
`AttributeError: 'numpy.ndarray' object has no attribute 'step'`.

* build: allow arviz-stats 1.3

Capping a single arviz package is counterproductive: `arviz` requires its
sub-packages to share a minor version, so `arviz-stats<1.3.0` would hold the
whole stack at 1.2 rather than fail loudly. Verified against 1.3.0 that the
three `ecdf_utils` functions keep their signatures, that the band values are
bit-identical to 1.2.0 for a fixed seed, and that tests/clv/test_plotting.py
passes on the full 1.3 stack.

* docs(clv): keep only the new cells in the CLV notebook diffs

Adding the ECDF cells re-executed the whole notebooks, which rewrote every
output and baked the executing machine's metadata into the files. Only two cells
per notebook are actually new, so take every pre-existing cell from the base
commit and keep only the new cells from the executed run, renumbering execution
counts so each notebook still reads as one sequential run.

* fix(clv): bound the ECDF reference draws and tighten the remaining edges

`ParetoNBDModel.fit` defaults to `method="map"`, so the point-estimate path is
the default for that model rather than a corner, and taking the reference draws
from `samples` put an unbounded cost on it: at 20k customers the default 1000
costs 646 MB and 171 s, and 100k would be ~3.2 GB and ~14 minutes. Coverage
saturates long before that (0.89 at a ratio of 20, then indistinguishable from
nominal from 50 up), so the ecdf branch now asks for a fixed 100 draws per
customer and `samples` goes back to meaning what it did before this PR: prior
predictive checks only.

Also:

- Move `plot_type` to the last named parameter. Inserted third, it silently
  reassigned every existing positional argument, so `f(model, "posterior", 20)`
  meant max_purchases=20 before this PR and raises now.
- Check `np.shape(ax)` before indexing into it. `len(ax)` ran first, so `ax=42`
  or a stray Figure raised TypeError while every other bad `ax` raised
  ValueError. This also rejects a set of two Axes, which passed the old check
  and then unpacked in arbitrary order.
- Format the band label with `:.4g`, since `int()` labelled a 99.9% band "99%".
- Scope the narrow-band advice: "increase 'samples'" is a no-op for a posterior
  check, which is the case that most often triggers the warning.

* test(clv): make the ECDF assertions capable of failing

The previous assertions held for any output of `compute_ecdf` and
`get_pointwise_confidence_band`: monotonicity and [0, 1] bounds are properties
of those functions, and the "same grid" check compared two views of one array.
Both bugs found in review would have passed. Assert against an independently
computed ECDF and grid instead, and check the difference panel reconstructs a
valid CDF.

Verified by mutating the source: plotting the predictive CDF instead of the
observed one, shifting the band one step off the grid, reverting the grid to a
100-point linspace, dropping the kwargs forwarding, and reverting the reference
draws each now fail the suite. Under the old assertions the first four passed.

Also covers the new `ax` rejections and pins `confidence_level` reaching the
band through `**kwargs`, whose failure mode is otherwise silent.

* docs(clv): re-execute the pareto_nbd posterior ECDF figure

`ParetoNBDModel.fit` defaults to `method="map"`, so `pnbd_map` in this notebook
is a point-estimate fit and its posterior ECDF cell was on exactly the path the
reference-CDF fix changed. The committed figure was rendered before that fix, so
the docs were showing the too-narrow band, with the observed curve stepping
outside it just above the markdown that says the model simulates customer
behaviour reliably.

Re-executed on HEAD: the corrected band is wider and the observed ECDF stays
inside it, so the figure and the surrounding text now agree.

The other five new figures were re-executed too and are byte-identical, since
bg_nbd and mbg_nbd fit with 4 chains x 2000 draws and the pareto prior check
never used the reference draws. Only the one changed payload is committed.

  injection surface from LLM output derived from PR text).
- Labels reach bash only via env: indirection (never inline
  interpolation), closing a script-injection vector.
- Sticky comment via hidden marker (edit-in-place on re-runs).
- Agent analysis is capped at <=3 sentences; full reasoning stays

feat: add R2-D2-M2 prior for variance decomposition (#2833)

* feat: add R2-D2-M2 prior for variance decomposition

Implements the R2D2M2 prior (Zhang et al., 2022) for automatic shrinkage
and variable selection via Dirichlet variance decomposition.

Usage:
    from pymc_marketing.r2d2 import R2D2Decomposition
    from pymc_extras.prior import Prior

    r2d2 = R2D2Decomposition(
        r2=Prior('Beta', mu=0.8, sigma=0.4),
        total_sigma=Prior('LogNormal', mu=0, sigma=1),
        dims={'control': 'control', 'fourier': 'fourier_mode'},
    )

    # Component coefficients (lazy VariableFactory)
    r2d2.split('control')   # -> R2D2Split
    r2d2.split('fourier')   # -> R2D2Split

    # Error sigma (lazy VariableFactory)
    r2d2.error_sigma         # -> R2D2Sigma

MMM Integration:
    mmm = MMM(
        ...,
        model_config={
            'likelihood': Prior('Normal', sigma=r2d2.error_sigma),
            'gamma_control': r2d2.split('control'),
            'gamma_fourier': r2d2.split('fourier'),
        },
    )

Key features:
- Lazy auto-build: decomposition created on first split access
- Serialization via @serialization.register
- Type validation for r2 and total_sigma
- Informative error messages for unknown splits

References:
- Zhang et al. (2022): https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.07132

* feat: add reference deduplication to serialization

Adds ReferenceTracker class to handle shared object deduplication
during serialization. When the same object appears multiple times,
subsequent occurrences emit $ref references instead of duplicating.

Key changes:
- ReferenceTracker class with reset() for test isolation
- TypeRegistry.serialize() now tracks objects and emits $ref for duplicates
- TypeRegistry.deserialize() resolves $ref references
- Autouse fixture in test_r2d2.py ensures test isolation

This fixes the R2D2 issue where R2D2Split and R2D2Sigma share the

fix(deps): drop the matplotlib<3.11 upper bound (#2924)

The chain that required the bound has cleared. pyproject pins pymc-extras>=0.14.0, which itself requires preliz>=0.27.0, and preliz 0.27.0 is the release that stopped touching the matplotlib.style.core shim removed in matplotlib 3.11. arviz-plots>=1.2.0 covers the other consumer.

The lock needed an explicit upgrade: removing the bound alone leaves matplotlib at the already-locked 3.10.9, since that still satisfies the loosened constraint. Relocked with --upgrade-package matplotlib, which moves it to 3.11.1 and adjusts the markers that resolution changes.

Closes #2923

casos.name: DSCODE 0.5.0 — review, worktrees, and TUI improvements
casos.body:
# DSCODE 0.5.0

这版聚焦编码 agent 的协作边界、代码审查和终端交互。

- Ultra 主 agent 可在 `subagent` 或 `subagent_fork` 中选择 `worktree: true`，让需要独立编辑的子 agent 从干净的 Git `HEAD` 启动独立 checkout。默认仍共享目录；主目录有未提交改动时拒绝隔离启动。子 agent 不会再委派其他子 agent。
- `/review` 与 agent 的 `review` tool 对指定 Git diff 发起独立、只读模型审查。编码改动通过相关检查后，agent 会在结束前审查一次，并先修复具体发现。可选暂存区、基准分支、单次提交和路径范围；相同 diff 的重复审查复用结果。
- TUI 支持向上滚动历史。运行时首次 Ctrl+C 立即中断 agent，再按一次退出；长文本粘贴在输入区折叠为标记，提交后对话里完整展开。图片粘贴显示 `[Image 1]` 等标记，支持多张图片。用户消息另用背景呈现，不同轮次之间有分割线。
- DeepSeek Flash 的普通 agent 请求获得按任务比例工作的简短引导：简单问题直接回答，有限代码改动完成相关检查后结束。低、高、最大推理档不启动子 agent；Ultra 才能启动或唤醒子 agent。

升级前退出使用同一数据目录的 DSCODE 会话：

```sh
npm install -g @toddzheng024/dscode@0.5.0
dscode update 0.5.0
```

也可从 GitHub Releases 下载 `dscode-0.5.0.tar.gz` 安装独立源码包。两种安装方式使用不同数据目录，不自动迁移会话和凭据。

验证覆盖单元、集成、TUI、包构建、真实本机 Harness 启动和 Hub 安装/回退。不调用付费模型；审查质量、图片在不同终端的剪贴板兼容性仍需实际使用检验。
mensagens_commits: Improve DSCODE diagnostics, telemetry, and terminal behavior
Release DSCODE 0.5.0 with review, worktrees, and TUI improvements
Make relay rendering test independent of local runtime setup

casos.name: DSCODE 0.7.9
casos.body:
# DSCODE 0.7.9

这版让 `dscode update` 一步更新整个安装：tar 安装获得原位自升级，npm/Hub 启动器会替换自身 binary；同时接入 ESLint 10，并修复审查白名单与错误处理上的一批问题。

- tar 安装新增 `dscode update [精确版本号]`：从 GitHub Releases 下载 tar 包并按发布方 sha256 摘要校验（无摘要拒绝安装），迁移 `.runtime`、`.env` 与本地 config（release 自带的新版默认文件不被旧副本覆盖），原位换目录——`dscode` 命令路径不变，无需重新链接；旧安装保留为同级备份目录，可手动换回或丢弃。源码检出处会拒绝并提示 git pull；运行中有会话时拒绝更新，换目录前会再次检查。
- npm/Hub 安装的 `dscode update` 先用 npm 把全局 launcher 本体替换到目标版本，成功后才把 profile 升到同一版本，任一步失败都不会留下半更新状态；省略版本号时查询 npm 上的最新 launcher，有新版本就一起更新，registry 不可达时回退到当前 launcher 的推荐版本，不隐式追踪 latest。
- 仓库接入 `npm run lint`（ESLint 10 flat config）并纳入 `npm run check`；`*-panel.mjs` 等序列化进 TUI 的模板文件按其绑定方式豁免。
- 收紧自动审查的提权白名单：`sysctl -w`、赋值形 key、带参数的 `hostname`/`date` 不再被自动授予，状态可变的诊断回到人工确认。
- code review 收集 untracked 文件时，消失或不可读的文件计入 omitted 而不是让整个 review 报错；审查审计文件损坏行被跳过，不再打断之后的每次审批。
- session-bridge 的一次恢复失败只让当步 fail closed，下一步自动重试，不再永久卡死该会话的收件。
- 邮件存储与验证脚本不再在 finally 中抛错（清理失败不会掩盖成功结果或原始错误）；checks 的完整性校验与套件失败同时上报；六处 catch 补上 error cause。

本版不升级 DSH 上游依赖。

验证：`npm run check` 通过（243 项单测、44 项评估测试；完整源码覆盖率 80.29%；集成、真实 Ink UI 与安装包检查通过）。tar 自升级从本版起随包分发，更早版本的 tar 安装仍需手动换目录一次；更新过程中的会话竞态窗口已收窄到秒级但未消除（不与运行中的会话共享内核锁）。
mensagens_commits: Release DSCODE 0.7.9 with dscode self-update and ESLint

casos.name: DSCODE 0.7.13
casos.body:
# DSCODE 0.7.13

这版把终端从「给上游打包产物打文本补丁」换成 **vendor 接管**：`packages/tui` 直接携带 `dsh-code` 1.2.0 的 TypeScript 源码，DSCODE 的 27 项改动全部落成源码而非补丁文本；同时修掉 shell 模式里多出来的感叹号、footer 宽度把变体选择符当一列、启动时打印 SQLite 实验性提示三处问题。

- **vendor 接管**：上游源码放在 `packages/tui`（`src` 61 个文件），仓库根以 `file:packages/tui` 依赖它，`node_modules/dsh-code` 只是软链，因此日常改动**零构建**、改完即生效。27 个补丁脚本、6 个 UI 验证脚本与 `probe:tui` 一并退役，`scripts/patch-*.mjs` 从 32 个降到 6 个（只剩 host 侧 runtime/Ink/stdin/compaction 补丁）。
- **发布形态改为编译**：Node 拒绝对 `node_modules` 下的文件做类型剥离，所以打包时用 `scripts/build-tui.mjs` 把 `src` 逐文件转译成 `lib`（不打包、不压缩），npm bundle 与 `.dshprofile` 都携带编译产物；仓库检出仍直接跑源码。
- **shell 模式隐藏感叹号**：`!cmd` 草稿已有品牌色圆角边框与 `! shell mode · esc exits` 提示，编辑器不再绘制那枚路由前缀，光标随之左移一列；提交路由、粘贴折叠标记、命令补全与行数预算仍读真实草稿。
- **宽度修正**：`displayWidth` 把零宽字符（组合符号、变体选择符）计成一列，导致 `❄️`（U+2744 + U+FE0F）按 3 列计——footer 的 provider 预算因此随 DeepSeek 峰谷时段摆动一列，off-peak 时那条断言会随机失败。现在零宽字符计 0，footer 预算不再随峰谷时段摆动。
- **启动安静**：harness 启动的每个 DSH 子进程都带上 `--disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning`（该 flag 前置到调用方传入的 node 参数之前），启动时不再打印 `node:sqlite` 的实验性提示；`exec` 路径不再重复传同一 flag。
- **测试基础设施**：测试 fixture 改为把 `node_modules/dsh-code` 软链到 `packages/tui`（与仓库、与真实运行的解析路径一致），集成套件此前因类型剥离限制整条挂掉；覆盖率清单排除 `packages/tui/lib` 这份编译产物，首方清单回到 8,094 行。

验证：`npm run check` 全绿——246 项单测（首方行覆盖 82.98%）、7 项集成探针（session bridge、messaging、runtime foundations、session cards、memory、login runtime、exec）、安装包检查与 44 项评估测试。实机 TTY 交互仍未验证（本环境无 pty，`EXEC_PROBE` 亦据此跳过阻塞终端的用例）。
mensagens_commits:
Release DSCODE 0.7.13 with the terminal vendored as source

- The terminal is vendored at packages/tui: the dsh-code 1.2.0 TypeScript sources
  carry every DSCODE change as code, the root manifest depends on the directory
  through file:packages/tui, and the 27 patch scripts, their UI verify scripts and
  the TUI probe are retired (scripts/patch-*.mjs drops from 32 files to 6).
- Publishing compiles the vendored terminal (scripts/build-tui.mjs transpiles
  packages/tui/src into packages/tui/lib), because Node refuses type stripping for
  files under node_modules; a checkout still runs the sources directly.
- The composer hides the shell-mode bang in the editor view and moves the caret with
  it, while routing, paste markers and the row budget keep the real draft.
- displayWidth no longer counts zero-width marks as columns: the U+FE0F in the
  off-peak marker measured three cells, which flipped the footer provider budget with
  DeepSeek's pricing window.
- Every DSH child boots with --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning, prepended to any
  caller-supplied node arguments; the exec path no longer repeats the flag.
- Test fixtures link node_modules/dsh-code to packages/tui the way the repository and
  a real run resolve it, and the coverage inventory excludes the compiled terminal.

Map the vendored session-query export into the published bundle

The bundle patch rewrote 'dsh-code/startup' and 'dsh-code' but left
'dsh-code/session-query' pointing at a package that an install does not have, so
the installed profile failed at boot with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND; the bundle now
rewrites that specifier too and exports session-query (and invariant) from the
compiled vendored terminal. The Hub probe also reports which fixture tool failed
instead of only that one did.

casos.name: DSCODE 0.7.25
casos.body:
# DSCODE 0.7.25

This release lets a repeated install keep a tar installation current instead of refusing, and adds a Homebrew formula for the launcher.

- **The installer upgrades instead of refusing (change)**: re-running `curl | sh` reads the version already installed and acts on it — equal or newer is reported and left alone with exit 0, older is handed to that installation's own `dscode update`, which downloads the release, verifies the publisher's sha256 digest, migrates `.runtime`, `.env` and the local config, and keeps the previous tree as `.dscode-backup-<version>`. Anything the installer did not create is still refused with the path it found — a directory that is not a DSCODE installation, or a `dscode` command belonging to another installation such as a source checkout — and that check now runs before the download instead of after it. Where the behaviour stops: the swap is the installed updater's work, so a tar installation older than `dscode update` is refused rather than replaced, an upgrade of the installation a session runs from still needs that session to exit, and a pre-release installation is superseded by its release.
- **A Homebrew formula (feature)**: `brew tap qiz029/tap && brew trust qiz029/tap && brew install dscode` installs the published launcher tarball into the formula's `libexec` — so the pinned dependency graph stays npm's rather than the formula's — links `dscode`, and writes `.dscode-brew` beside `cli.mjs`. `brewManaged()` reads that marker, so on a formula installation `dscode update` moves only the Hub profile and leaves the launcher to `brew upgrade dscode`; an explicit version that would put the profile ahead of the launcher is refused. The tap carries its own workflow that follows `npm view @toddzheng024/dscode version` daily, recomputes the tarball's sha256 and commits the formula update. Where the behaviour stops: Homebrew 7 refuses to load a third-party tap's formula until the tap is trusted, so that step is part of the install; the formula claims `dscode` in the Homebrew prefix, so an `npm install -g` launcher already linked there has to be removed first; and the formula's own install has not run on a machine whose Command Line Tools Homebrew accepts.

Verification: the release build runs `npm run check` on both Node 24 and 22.19.0, and `Linux e2e` is green. New cases cover the installer's version decision — an older installation handed to its own updater without any download, an equal or newer one left untouched, a pre-release not mistaken for the release it leads to, and a foreign command still refused with its symlink left in place — and the Homebrew marker the launcher reads. The installer's upgrade path was also run end to end against real releases: 0.7.23 installed into a scratch directory, the installer re-run to move it to 0.7.24 through its own updater with `.dscode-backup-0.7.23` left behind, and a third run reporting that nothing was changed. The formula was checked as far as this machine allows — `ruby -c` on it, `brew info` loading it, its pinned sha256 equal to the published tarball, and the npm global-prefix install with the marker read back by the new launcher code — but **no `brew install` completed here**: `brew doctor` reports this machine's Command Line Tools do not support macOS 26, which Homebrew refuses to install past, so the formula's install and test blocks have no automated or manual confirmation yet. `tests/code-review.test.mjs` does not complete inside a DSCODE session, the documented in-session limitation (it spawns real `git` subprocesses and the run ends with `Promise resolution is still pending but the event loop has already resolved`).

Support Homebrew and make the installer version-aware

The curl installer no longer refuses an existing installation: it reads the installed version, leaves an equal or newer one alone, and hands an older one to that installation's own dscode update, which migrates the state and keeps a backup beside it. Anything the installer did not create - a foreign directory, or a dscode command belonging to another installation such as a source checkout - is still refused with the path it found, and that check now runs before the download rather than after it.

A Homebrew formula in the new qiz029/tap tap installs the published launcher into libexec and writes .dscode-brew there. brewManaged() reads that marker, so on a formula installation dscode update moves only the Hub profile and an explicit version is refused instead of leaving the profile ahead of the launcher; the tap's own workflow follows npm's latest and recomputes the digest daily.

Documented in both READMEs and docs/distribution.md, with the tap step added to the release checklist; no version bump in this commit.

Cut 0.7.25: Homebrew support and a version-aware installer

A repeated curl install now keeps a tar installation current instead of refusing, and the launcher ships in the qiz029/tap tap, whose formula marks its own libexec so dscode update moves only the Hub profile. The version bump, docs/releases/0.7.25.md, the changelog entry and both READMEs ship in this commit; the tag v0.7.25 matches package.json.

casos.name: DSCODE 0.7.31
casos.body:
# DSCODE 0.7.31

This release adds OpenCode Go as a fourth provider: `/provider opencode-go` runs a session on an OpenCode Go subscription, serving its chat-completions models with the reasoning efforts each one accepts, and searching the web through Exa as OpenCode itself does.

- **`opencode-go` route (new)**: a new plugin, `plugins/opencode-go`, registers the route. `/provider opencode-go` (also `/provider opencode`) asks for the key from the OpenCode console and stores it in `~/.dscode/credentials.yaml` like the other provider keys. `OPENCODE_API_KEY` in the environment takes precedence. The key is sent as a bearer token to `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions`. The provider picker, `/login opencode-go` and `/model` pick it up from the provider catalog without terminal changes. Switching from DeepSeek or OpenRouter lands on the same model when Go serves it; otherwise the switch lands on `kimi-k3`.
- **A catalog probed against the live gateway (design)**: Go's `/models` listing returns ids only. It gives no context size, image support or reasoning controls. Go also passes request fields through to each model's upstream, so what a request may contain differs by model. The catalog therefore records, per model, what the gateway accepted in September 2026. It covers the `reasoning_effort` values (GLM, Kimi K2.7 Code, LongCat and Space Bunny cannot switch thinking off, and MiMo V2.6 refuses `max`) and whether the model takes images (a text-only model answers an image with HTTP 404). Context windows follow each lab's published figure. The catalog has 19 models: DeepSeek V4 (4), GLM (4), Kimi (3), MiMo (4), LongCat, Hy (2) and Space Bunny Free. The DeepSeek rows follow DeepSeek's own API rather than a probe, because the test workspace was not set to Go's Global region.
- **Request shape**: the body keeps to OpenAI fields: `reasoning_effort` (Off sends `none`, Ultra sends `max` plus the collaboration policy) and `stream_options.include_usage`. It omits OpenRouter's extensions (`reasoning: {effort}`, `provider`, `session_id`), which Go's upstreams reject with "Extra inputs are not permitted". Each request carries the session id in `x-opencode-session` and a `dscode/<version>` user agent, as Go asks of third-party clients. Reasoning goes back to the model that produced it as `reasoning_content`. DeepSeek gets an empty one after another model's turn, because it rejects a thinking-mode tool-call turn without one.
- **Shared request loop (changed)**: the Go adapter extends the OpenRouter adapter instead of copying it. The request loop, image preparation, SSE parsing and stream translation are now parameterised by route. The route supplies its model lookup, body, headers, replay kind and the name used in error messages. OpenRouter's defaults are unchanged, and its tests pass unmodified.
- **Web search through Exa (new)**: Go has no search endpoint. A Go session's `web_search` therefore calls `web_search_exa` on Exa's hosted MCP server (`https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp`), which is what OpenCode's own client does, and that server answers without a key. An `EXA_API_KEY` in the environment or the credential store moves the calls onto that account, and a key store that cannot be read falls back to the keyless endpoint. Exa's text answer is parsed into de-duplicated sources with title and snippet. A search times out after 25 seconds, and cancellation is honoured. Routing sends only `opencode-go` sessions to Exa, because the keyless tier is Exa's free offer with no published limit. DeepSeek, OpenRouter and Grok sessions search as before.
- **Where it stops**: Go serves Qwen and MiniMax over the Anthropic messages protocol, and Grok 4.x, GPT Luna and Muse Spark over the OpenAI responses protocol. This release implements neither. Naming one of those models fails before any request with a message that names the endpoint. The footer shows no cost and no balance on this route, because Go publishes no allowance API. When the workspace is not in the Global region, Go refuses its DeepSeek models; the error now adds where to change that in the OpenCode console.

Verification: `npm run check` passed on macOS. That covers lint, both typechecks, 581 unit tests at 84.54% measured `.mjs` line coverage (nine tests are new for this route), the nine native Harness integration probes, both package tarballs and 51 evaluations. The extended `scripts/verify-login-runtime.mjs` probe boots a real Harness Host twice and checks that the `opencode-go` row saves its key, keeps it across a restart, lists the catalog with the right efforts and sends the expected request shape. With a real Go key, the adapter completed a tool call followed by a replayed answer on all 15 non-DeepSeek chat models. The DeepSeek and Qwen rows failed with their intended explanations. A live keyless Exa search returned titled, de-duplicated sources, and a cancelled search reported `WEB_ABORTED`.

What has no automated case: the DeepSeek rows were not exercised against Go, because the test workspace was not in the Global region. Image input was checked with direct gateway requests, not through the adapter's attachment path. The provider picker and `/login opencode-go` were not driven by hand in a live terminal. No model ran `web_search` inside a real Go session; routing to Exa is covered by unit cases only.
mensagens_commits:
Release 0.7.31: OpenCode Go provider with Exa web search

Add OpenCode Go as a fourth /provider route, serving the subscription's
chat-completions models, and search the web for Go sessions through
Exa as OpenCode's own client does.

- plugins/opencode-go registers the opencode-go route. /provider
  opencode-go and /login opencode-go store OPENCODE_API_KEY in the
  shared credential store; the picker and /model pick it up from the
  provider catalog without terminal changes.
- The catalog lists 19 models (DeepSeek V4, GLM, Kimi, MiMo, LongCat,
  Hy, Space Bunny) with the reasoning efforts and image support each
  one accepted on the live gateway. Go's /models listing carries ids
  only.
- Requests keep to OpenAI fields (reasoning_effort, stream_options),
  because Go's upstreams reject OpenRouter's extensions. Each request
  sends x-opencode-session and a dscode/<version> user agent, and
  replays reasoning as reasoning_content to the model that produced it.
- The Go adapter extends the OpenRouter adapter; the request loop,
  wire serializer and stream translation take route parameters, with
  OpenRouter's defaults unchanged.
- Qwen, MiniMax, Grok, GPT Luna and Muse Spark use Go's messages or
  responses endpoints and are refused before any request. A workspace
  outside Go's Global region gets a hint for DeepSeek refusals.
- A Go session's web_search calls Exa's hosted MCP search keylessly;
  EXA_API_KEY is optional. Other routes search as before.

Verified: npm run check on macOS (581 unit tests, nine integration
probes including a real-Host opencode-go login and request check,
package tarballs, 51 evaluations). With a real key, all 15 non-DeepSeek
models completed a tool call and replay. DeepSeek was not exercised
(workspace not in the Global region), and no model ran web_search in a
live Go session.

casos.name: playwriter@0.0.52
casos.body:
## Features

- **First extension keeps connection**: When multiple Playwriter extensions are installed (e.g., dev and prod), the first one with active tabs now keeps the connection instead of being replaced by newer connections. Idle extensions (no tabs) can still be replaced.
- **Smarter extension slot detection**: `/extension/status` endpoint now returns `activeTargets` count, allowing extensions to know when the slot becomes available (no active tabs).
- **Accessibility snapshot format options**: `accessibilitySnapshot` now supports `format` option (`'yaml'` or `'markdown'`) with deduplication of interactive refs
- **Session management CLI commands**: New CLI commands for managing relay sessions (`playwriter sessions list`, `playwriter sessions kill`)
- **Eval CLI flag**: New `-e/--eval` CLI flag for quick code execution from command line
- **Auto-enable environment variable**: CLI now passes `PLAYWRITER_AUTO_ENABLE` when starting relay server

## Bug Fixes

- **Relay server auto-recovery**: Restored auto-recovery on every execute call
- **Preserve tabs during relay reconnects**: Tabs now persist correctly when relay reconnects
- **Show log file path on connection refused error**: Better debugging experience with log file location in errors
- **Improved error messages for extension connection states**: Clearer error messages when extension isn't connected

## Security

- **Block browser access to CLI endpoints**: Prevents browsers from accessing CLI-specific endpoints

## Internal

- **SKILL.md as source of truth**: Refactored to generate `prompt.md` from `SKILL.md`
- **Aria snapshot module**: New `aria-snapshot.ts` with dedicated accessibility snapshot functions
