<!-- notionvc: 3c954cd3-850c-412c-92b3-fa4cfa914be8 -->

* Memory requirement for 512 samples on Llama 8B is ~70Gb, which is
equivalent to batch size 128
* With this option enabled and batch size 32, calibration runtime is
less than 1s per layer (down from ~11s)
* This implies that the theoretical maximum speedup from reducing
calibration time alone is ~15% for this model + dataset

### Misc ###
* Fix examples
* Fixed examples where there's issues between model dtypes and processor
dtypes (Mixtral, Pixtral, Whisper)
* For multimodal models which use multimodal datasets, remove their data
collators, as the batch unwrapping is now done by
the`TextGenerationDataset`
* Remove `_mask_padding` from `IntermediatesCache`, as I do not believe
that this method is effective in masking padding tokens from hessian
calculations
* Fix AWQ
  * AWQ was hard coded to handle only batches of size 1

_compute_layer_means was making in-place changes to the weights which
made the first iteration (until the weights are refreshed from the
cached versions) useless

flow was

1) cache weight
2) compute mean (modify weight)
3) scale weight 
4) calculate loss
4) restore weight, goto 3

so the first run of 3&4 were gibberish

note this bug has been around for a while and we hadn't detected it
because throwing away a single iteration was fine as long as the rest
worked

[Example] Attention and R3 Examples (#2132)

# Attention Quantization in LLM Compressor #
LLM Compressor supports applying static attention quantization to
models. Please note that attention quantization support in vLLM is still
ongoing and is not fully supported as of this writing.

## FP8 Attention Example ##
For an example applying attention quantization, see
[llama3_attention.py](/experimental/attention/llama3_attention.py).

```python
recipe = QuantizationModifier(
    config_groups={
        "attention": QuantizationScheme(
            targets=["LlamaAttention"],
            input_activations=QuantizationArgs(
                num_bits=8, type="float", strategy="attn_head"
            ),
        )
    }
)
```

Note that attention quantization also implicitly applies kv cache
quantization with the same quantization arguments.

## NVFP4 Attention + R3 Example ##
Attention quantization can be improved using the R3 transform, as
described by [SpinQuant](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.16406). This
transform reduces the presence of outliers in the attention activation
distribution, thereby improving accurcy recovery.

```python
recipe = [
    SpinQuantModifier(rotations=["R3"]),
    QuantizationModifier(
        config_groups={
            "attention": QuantizationScheme(
                targets=["LlamaAttention"],
                input_activations=NVFP4["input_activations"],
            )
        }
    ),
]
```

### Evaluations ###
Utilizing the R3 transform has been shown to improve accuracy recovery
for the `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct` model when using NVFP4
attention quantization.

Without R3 Transform

Add support for passing a custom DataLoader to oneshot() (#2390)

SUMMARY:
Adds a `dataloader` argument to the `oneshot` entrypoint.

Allow users to pass a pre-built PyTorch DataLoader directly via the
`dataloader` parameter, bypassing the internal dataset-to-dataloader
conversion. This is useful for custom data pipelines where users already
have a prepared DataLoader and don't need get_calibration_dataloader().

Rather than using `self.dataloader = kwargs.pop("dataloader", None)`, we
could also add a `dataloader` argument/attribute to `DatasetArguments`
if you prefer.

TEST PLAN:
This change is fairly trivial, I made sure
[https://github.com/vllm-project/llm-compressor/blob/main/examples/quantization_w4a16/README.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/llm-compressor/blob/main/examples/quantization_w4a16/README.md)
could still run and that passing the DataLoader too:

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM

MODEL_ID = "meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct"
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID, dtype="auto")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID)

from datasets import load_dataset

NUM_CALIBRATION_SAMPLES=512
MAX_SEQUENCE_LENGTH=2048

# Load dataset.
ds = load_dataset("HuggingFaceH4/ultrachat_200k", split=f"train_sft[:{NUM_CALIBRATION_SAMPLES}]")
ds = ds.shuffle(seed=42)

# Preprocess the data into the format the model is trained with.
def preprocess(example):
    return {"text": tokenizer.apply_chat_template(example["messages"], tokenize=False,)}
ds = ds.map(preprocess)

# Tokenize the data (be careful with bos tokens - we need add_special_tokens=False since the chat_template already added it).
def tokenize(sample):
    return tokenizer(sample["text"], padding=False, max_length=MAX_SEQUENCE_LENGTH, truncation=True, add_special_tokens=False)
ds = ds.map(tokenize, remove_columns=ds.column_names)

from llmcompressor.datasets import get_calibration_dataloader
from llmcompressor.args import DatasetArguments

dataset_args = DatasetArguments(
    dataset=ds,
    max_seq_length=MAX_SEQUENCE_LENGTH,
    num_calibration_samples=NUM_CALIBRATION_SAMPLES,
)

dataloader = get_calibration_dataloader(dataset_args, tokenizer)

from llmcompressor import oneshot
from llmcompressor.modifiers.quantization import GPTQModifier

# Configure the quantization algorithm to run.
recipe = GPTQModifier(targets="Linear", scheme="W4A16", ignore=["lm_head"])

# Apply quantization.
oneshot(
    model=model, 
    recipe=recipe,
    dataloader=dataloader,
)

# Save to disk compressed.
SAVE_DIR = MODEL_ID.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1] + "-W4A16-G128"
model.save_pretrained(SAVE_DIR, save_compressed=True)
tokenizer.save_pretrained(SAVE_DIR)
```

This is the exact same code from the documentation, with the DataLoader
built outside of the `oneshot` call (`dataloader =
get_calibration_dataloader(dataset_args, tokenizer)`) and passed
directly to `oneshot`.

Enable merge queue support in GitHub workflows (#2433)

## Summary
- Configures Mergify merge queue with automatic DCO sign-off to resolve
DCO check failures on merge commits
- Removes GitHub native merge queue triggers from all workflows
- Adds auto-merge rule for PRs with `ready` label and required approvals

## Problem
The DCO (Developer Certificate of Origin) GitHub App was failing on
merge commits created by GitHub's native merge queue, as those commits
lacked the required `Signed-off-by:` trailer.

## Solution
Switch to Mergify's merge queue which automatically adds DCO sign-off to
all merge commits it creates.

## Changes
### Mergify Configuration (`.github/mergify.yml`)
- Added `queue_rules` with automatic DCO sign-off in commit messages
- Added auto-merge rule that queues PRs when:
  - Label `ready` is applied
  - 2+ approvals received
  - All required checks pass (DCO, tests, quality, etc.)

### Workflow Updates (removed `merge_group` triggers)
- `.github/workflows/ready-label-check.yaml`: Removed merge_group
trigger
- `.github/workflows/test-check-transformers.yaml`: Removed merge_group
trigger and condition
- `.github/workflows/test-check.yaml`: Removed merge_group trigger
- `.github/workflows/quality-check.yaml`: Removed merge_group trigger
- `.github/workflows/linkcheck.yml`: Removed merge_group trigger

## Testing
After merging, GitHub's native merge queue should be disabled in
repository settings and Mergify will handle all merge queue operations.

fix: use topological ordering in FX graph cleanup to fix erase_node crash (Granite4 GPTQ) (#2426)

## SUMMARY:
Fix the FX tracing crash reported as the second error in #2338. The BFS
cleanup of concrete args did not maintain topological ordering — if a
node was visited multiple times, its position in the deletion dict was
not updated, causing dependents to be deleted before their dependencies
(`RuntimeError: Tried to erase Node getitem_169`).

The fix uses `move_to_end` in the BFS traversal so that revisited nodes
are moved to the end of the deletion dict, ensuring topological order.

Companion to #2425 (shape fix) and compressed-tensors #609 (3D
pack/unpack). Together they resolve #2338.

(#2425, #2426, compressed-tensors #609).

ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-small --output /workspace/test-output
--calibration-samples 16`

- 3D→2D conversion OK
- Cache preparation OK (16/16 samples)

Add GSM8K evaluation script and AWQ+FP8 results (#2330)

This PR adds GSM8K evaluation results for AWQ+FP8 quantization as
requested in #2305.

## What's included

**RESULTS.md** - Evaluation results comparing FP8_DYNAMIC vs FP8_BLOCK
quantization schemes on Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct

## Results

| Scheme | Strict Match | Flexible Extract |
|--------|-------------|------------------|
| **FP8_DYNAMIC** | **76.42%** | **76.19%** |
| **FP8_BLOCK** | 75.21% | 74.98% |

- **Model:** Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct
- **Hardware:** 8x NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB
- FP8_DYNAMIC outperforms FP8_BLOCK by ~1.2% on strict match

## DIscussion
This behavior where FP8_BLOCK underperforms FP8_DYNAMIC contradicts our
expectation since for RTN FP8_BLOCK outperforms FP8_DYNAMIC, however
there are 2 important things to notice.
1) FP8_BLOCK quantization creates quantization `groups` whose size is
equivalent to the number of elements in a block, whereas FP8_DYNAMIC
quantization creates quantization `groups`
whose size is equal to the in_features. Thus as long as in_features is
less than the block size (128x128=16384) the number of weight scales
will actually be higher for per channel quantization.
For Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct the per-channel weight quantization of the
FP8_DYNAMIC scheme has more scales than FP8_BLOCK for every weight.
2) Its also noteworthy that for AWQ, the scale factors being searched
for during AWQ align directly with the quantization scales of the per
channel weight quantization, this is likely why AWQ yields
   such a large improvement for FP8_DYNAMIC

## Evaluation command

```bash
lm_eval \
  --model hf \
  --model_args pretrained=<model_path>,dtype=auto \
  --tasks gsm8k \
  --batch_size 16 \
  --output_path <output_dir>
```

**Note:** `batch_size=16` is important — the default `auto` picks 1,
significantly increasing evaluation time.

instead of the cache iterator so CPU→device onload overlaps with the
forward pass over cached parent args during smoothing.

iter(), and one that prefetch on an empty cache yields nothing. No new
public API; prefetch is used automatically when AWQ offloads.

[Distributed][SmoothQuant] Add distributed activation scale reduction (#2180) (#2471)

## Summary
Implements distributed support for `SmoothQuantModifier` as part of the
weight-parallel optimization tracked in #2180, assigned to @dzhengAP.

## What this PR does
In a distributed calibration run, each rank observes a disjoint
partition
of the calibration dataset. Activation statistics (per-channel min/max)
are collected locally via forward hooks. Before smoothing scales are
computed, `_reduce_activation_scales()` all-reduces those statistics
across all ranks so every rank has the global activation profile, then
each rank independently computes identical smoothing scales (cheap op,
no weight broadcast needed).

This follows the AWQ strategy described in #2180. Single-GPU behavior
is completely unchanged — all new code is guarded by `is_distributed()`.

## Changes
- `_reduce_activation_scales()`: all-reduces `min/max_channel_vals`
across ranks using async MIN/MAX collectives batched with
`wait_for_comms`
- `_apply_smoothing()`: calls `_reduce_activation_scales()` as first
step
- Unit tests: 5 mock-based tests verifying call contract (no GPU needed)
- DDP example:
`examples/quantization_w8a8_int8/smoothquant_ddp_example.py`
- Multi-GPU integration tests verifying weight equivalence vs single-GPU

- DDP example: ran successfully on 2x V100 32GB, both ranks completed

fix: add norm calibration context for unit-offset RMSNorm (Gemma/Qwen3Next) (#2500)

## SUMMARY

Some architectures (Gemma, Gemma2, Gemma3, Qwen3Next) use an offset
normalization where the forward computes `output * (1 + weight)` instead
of `output * weight`. This breaks any modifier that smooths norm weights
(AWQ, SmoothQuant, SpinQuant, QuIP) because dividing a `(1+weight)`
parameter by scales produces `1 + weight/scales` instead of `(1 +
weight)/scales`.

Following @brian-dellabetta's suggestion, this adds a
`norm_calibration_context` that temporarily replaces offset-norm modules
with standard-norm equivalents during calibration, following the same
pattern as `moe_calibration_context`. On entry, offset norms are
replaced with `CalibrationOffsetNorm` modules (`weight = 1 + original`).
On exit, modules are restored with updated weights (`weight = smoothed -
1`).

Only norms operating on `hidden_size` are converted. Norms operating on
`head_dim` (e.g. `q_norm`/`k_norm` in Gemma3 attention) are skipped
since no modifier smooths them.

## TEST PLAN

Unit tests (8/8 passing):
- Weight conversion and dtype preservation
- Forward equivalence with original norm
- Restore roundtrip (with and without smoothing)
- Registry detection (positive and negative)
- `hidden_size` filter: `q_norm`/`k_norm` correctly skipped

E2E validation:

| Model | Modifier | Norms converted | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| `google/gemma-2-2b-it` | AWQ W4A16 | 105 | Coherent |
| `google/medgemma-27b-text-it` | AWQ W4A16 | 249 (373 total, 124 q/k
skipped) | Coherent |
| upstream (no fix) on medgemma | AWQ W4A16 | 0 | Garbage |

Qwen3-Next architecture verified structurally: `hidden_size=2048`,
`head_dim=256`, `Qwen3NextRMSNorm` uses same `(1+weight)` pattern. No
smaller Qwen3-Next model exists for e2e testing (80B MoE only).

feat: add iMatrix weighted MSE observer and IMatrixGatherer (#2473)

## SUMMARY

Adds `imatrix_mse`, a new weight observer that uses per-channel
activation importance (E[x²]) to weight the quantization error during
range selection. Channels that carry more signal get more careful range
optimization.

Two components:

- **IMatrixGatherer** (`modifiers/transform/imatrix/base.py`):
lightweight lifecycle trigger that orchestrates a calibration pass so
the observer can collect E[x²]. Does not quantize, delegates to the
subsequent `QuantizationModifier` / `GPTQModifier`.

- **imatrix_mse observer** (`observers/imatrix.py`): extends the MSE
grid search with importance weighting: `err = sum(importance * |Q(w) -
w|^p)`. Owns the E[x²] collection lifecycle via
`Observer.attach(module)` / `Observer.detach(module)`. Supports CHANNEL,
GROUP, TENSOR_GROUP, and BLOCK strategies via `flatten_for_calibration`.
Falls back to uniform MSE when importance is unavailable (`strict=False`
default).

### Usage
```yaml
recipe:
  - IMatrixGatherer:
      ignore: ["lm_head"]
  - QuantizationModifier:
      config_groups:
        group_0:
          targets: ["Linear"]
          weights:
            num_bits: 4
            observer: imatrix_mse
```

Composes with GPTQ:
```yaml
recipe:
  - IMatrixGatherer:
      ignore: ["lm_head"]
  - GPTQModifier:
      config_groups:
        group_0:
          targets: ["Linear"]
          weights:
            observer: imatrix_mse
```

### Results

W4A16, WikiText-2 token-level PPL, 141 chunks × 2048, open_platypus
calibration 512 samples.

Llama-3.1-8B, group_size=128:

| Config | PPL |
|---|---|
| FP16 baseline | 6.24 |
| RTN `memoryless_minmax` | 6.96 |
| GPTQ | 6.92 |
| AWQ | 6.89 |
| RTN `imatrix_mse` | 6.85 |
| GPTQ + `imatrix_mse` | 6.83 |

Eval method: GPTQ paper (concatenate WikiText-2 test, non-overlapping
segments of 2048 tokens, exp(mean(NLLs))).

RFC #2456

45 tests added (all CPU, no GPU required):

- `test_imatrix.py` (26 tests): grid search with non-uniform importance,
CHANNEL/GROUP/TENSOR_GROUP/BLOCK strategies, actorder g_idx reordering,
strict vs non-strict fallback, validation (shape, dtype, finite,
non-negative)
- `test_imatrix_gatherer.py` (15 tests): E[x²] collection, ignore list,
accumulation correctness, hook cleanup, weight immutability, on_event
lifecycle
- `test_e2e_integration.py` (4 tests): full pipeline via `oneshot()` on

Fix KV cache calibration for attention modules not named self_attn (#2477)

SUMMARY:
`_apply_kv_cache_scheme` (in compressed-tensors) discovers attention
modules via `is_attention_module()`, which is name-agnostic. However,
`start_calibration` only iterates modules matching `resolved_targets`,
which includes `"re:.*self_attn$"` for KV cache. This regex misses
attention modules with different names (e.g. `"attention"`,
`"self_attention"`), leaving their observers uninitialized and KV cache
scales as garbage values.

Add a fallback pass in `start_calibration` and `end_calibration` that
uses `is_attention_module()` to catch any attention modules missed by
the regex. Gated by `kv_cache_scheme is not None` so there is zero cost
when KV cache quantization is not used. This addresses the existing
TODO: "decouple reliance on this regex for matching attention".

TEST PLAN:
- Added unit test with a stub model whose attention modules are named
`attention` (not `self_attn`). Verifies observers are initialized, hooks
are registered, and modules are frozen correctly.
- All 51 existing quantization modifier tests pass.

[Distributed] [model_free_ptq] Eliminate reindexing step via fine-grained parallelized partial reads (#2498)

## Purpose
Eliminates the `reindex_fused_weights` preprocessing step for microscale
schemes (NVFP4, MXFP4) by enabling each shard to be processed
independently
with full parallelism, even when fused weight sets (q/k/v, gate/up) span
multiple shards.

## Approach
Instead of grouping shards together (which reduces parallelism), each
shard
process fetches only the specific fused partner tensors it needs from
other
shards via targeted partial safetensors reads, computes the fused global
scale locally, and writes only its own output shard. No cross-process
coordination or file locking required.

## Changes

### `helpers.py`
Added `build_tensor_file_index()` — reads `index.json` once at startup
and
builds a flat mapping of `tensor_name → resolved_file_path`. This gives
each
worker process an O(1) lookup to find which file contains any fused
partner
tensor, without re-scanning headers at runtime.

### `process.py`
Updated `process_file_microscale_scheme()` with an optional
`tensor_file_index` parameter. When provided:
- `_fetch_fused_partners()` is called to identify any fused set members
missing from the current shard, then fetches only those specific tensors
via partial safetensors reads (headers + target tensors only, not full
files)
- Fused global scale is computed locally using all members of the fused
set
- `_belongs_to_shard()` ensures only native tensors are written to the
output
shard — fetched partner tensors are used for scale computation only and
  never written to the wrong shard

### `__init__.py`
Simplified back to one job per shard — full parallelism restored. For
microscale schemes, builds the `tensor_file_index` once from
`index.json`
and passes it to each job. No union-find, no grouping logic needed.

### `validate.py`
Removed `NotImplementedError` for cross-shard fused weights — the case
is
now handled natively. Replaced with `logger.debug` noting that partner
tensors will be resolved via partial reads.

## Latest Updates: Eliminate reindexing step via inverse_weights_map
with unified job signatures

## Approach
Each shard job receives a precomputed `inverse_weights_map` specifying
exactly
which tensors to load from which files. For cross-shard fused weights,
only the
shard owning the **primary** tensor (q_proj, gate_proj) fetches its
partners —
preventing double reads. All jobs share a unified signature for both
standard
and microscale schemes.

## Changes

### `microscale.py`
- Refactor `DEFAULT_FUSED_MAPPINGS` from a list of lists to
`{primary_pattern: [partner_templates]}` — only the primary-owning shard
fetches its partners, preventing double reads for cross-shard fused
weights
- Move `build_inverse_weights_map()` here — uses regex match on primary
  patterns to construct partner names and locate them in other shards

### `process.py`
- **Unified signature** for `validate_file`, `process_file`, and
  `process_file_microscale_scheme`:
  `(inverse_weights_map, save_path, scheme, ignore, device, converter)`
- All functions use `safe_open` + `f.get_tensor()` for true partial
reads
- Partner tensors re-saved into requesting shard's output; caller
updates
  safetensors index to reflect new locations

### `__init__.py`
- Single `_get_weights_map()` helper handles both single-file and
multi-file
models (reads `safetensors.index.json` or scans file headers via
`safe_open`)
- Single `_build_quantization_jobs()` replaces separate
standard/microscale
  builders — one job per shard with identical tuple structure for both
- Validate jobs use `*job[1:]` for full future-proofing

### `helpers.py`
- Removed `build_weights_map` and `build_inverse_weights_map` (moved to
  `microscale.py`)

### `validate.py`
- Removed `NotImplementedError` for cross-shard fused weights — handled
natively
- Updated to reflect `inverse_weights_map`-based approach

## Testing
- `pytest tests/llmcompressor/entrypoints/model_free/` — all passing
locally
- `make style && make quality` — all checks pass

Re-enable Mergify merge queue with squash and minimal pull_request_rules (#2543)

## Summary

Fixes the infinite dequeue loop that was caused by:
1. Mergify rebasing the PR branch → `synchronize` event → all CI
re-triggers → checks go `pending`
2. `pull_request_rules` re-evaluated with CI checks → conditions fail →
PR dequeued
3. PR never re-entered the queue automatically

## Changes

- **`merge_method: squash`** — squash doesn't push to the PR branch
during queue processing, so no `synchronize` event and no CI re-trigger
in the normal flow
- **`pull_request_rules` has NO CI checks** — only `label=ready`, 2
approvals, not conflict, not draft. If the branch does need updating,
all checks go `pending` but the PR stays in the queue.
`queue_conditions` handles waiting for CI.
- **`queue_conditions` = `merge_conditions`** — in-place mode,
compatible with "Require branches to be up to date" branch protection
- **`commit_message_template`** without `Signed-off-by: Mergify` —
avoids DCO failures since DCO checks PR branch commits, not the squash
commit
- **`max_parallel_checks: 1` + `batch_size: 1`** — one PR at a time

## Test plan
- [ ] Add `ready` label + 2 approvals to a PR and verify Mergify
auto-queues it
- [ ] Verify PR is merged by `mergify[bot]` without manual intervention
- [ ] Verify a PR where `transformers-tests` is skipped still merges
correctly

```yaml

# After
SmoothQuantModifier:
  algorithm: log_equalization
  mappings: [...]

# Python Function to Sort Numbers in Ascending Order

Here are several approaches to sort a list of numbers in ascending
order:

## Method 1: Using Python's Built-in `sorted()` Function

```python
def sort_ascending(numbers):
    """
    Sort a list of numbers in ascending order.
    
    Args:
        numbers: A list of numbers (int or float)
    
    Returns:
        A new sorted list in ascending order
    """
    return sorted(numbers)
```

## Method 2: Using the `list.sort()` Method (In-Place Sorting)

```python
def sort_ascending_inplace(numbers):
    """
    Sort a list in-place in ascending order.
    """
    numbers.sort()
    return numbers
```

## Method 3: Manual Implementation - Bubble Sort

```python
def sort_ascending_manual(numbers):
    """
    Implement bubble sort algorithm manually.
    """
    numbers = numbers.copy()  # Create a copy to avoid modifying original
    n = len(numbers)
    
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(0, n - i - 1):
            if numbers[j] > numbers[j + 1]:
                # Swap elements
                numbers[j], numbers[j + 1] = numbers[j + 1], numbers[j]
    
    return numbers
```

## Method 4: Custom Comparator with Reverse Parameter

```python
def sort_ascending(numbers, reverse=False):
    """
    Sort a list of numbers with optional direction.
    """
    return sorted(numbers, reverse=reverse)
```

---

## Example Usage

```python
# Test the functions
if __name__ == "__main__":
    my_list = [64, 34, 25, 12, 22, 11, 90]
    
    # Using sorted()
    result1 = sort_ascending(my_list)
    print(f"Original list: {my_list}")
    print(f"Sorted list:   {result1}")
    # Output: [11, 12, 22, 25, 34, 64, 90]
    
    # Using in-place sort
    my_list2 = [64, 34, 25, 12, 22, 11, 90]
    sort_ascending_inplace(my_list2)
    print(f"After in-place sort: {my_list2}")
    # Output: [11, 12, 22, 25, 34, 64, 90]
    
    # Handles different data types
    mixed_list = [3.14, 1, 4.5, 2, 0.5]
    print(f"Mixed int/float: {sort_ascending(mixed_list)}")
    # Output: [0.5, 1, 2, 3.14, 4.5]
```

---

## Summary

| Method | Time Complexity | Space Complexity | Modifies Original? |
|--------|-----------------|------------------|-------------------|
| `sorted()` | O(n log n) | O(n) | No |
| `.sort()` | O(n log n) | O(1) | Yes |
| Bubble Sort | O(n²) | O(1) | No |

**Recommendation:** For production code, use the built-in `sorted()` or
`.sort()` method as they're optimized and well-tested. Use the manual
implementation for learning purposes.

Fix CI regression on AWQ eval (#2606)

This PR updates recovery thresholds to address test failure:
https://github.com/neuralmagic/llm-compressor-testing/actions/runs/23393076845/job/68051194021


SUMMARY:
This regression occured after the [AWQ DDP
PR](https://github.com/vllm-project/llm-compressor/pull/2457), in it we
changed the mean accumulation method as well as the loss accumulation
dype to be more mathematically accurate.

However this seems to have caused a regression on GSM8K evaluation based
on the way the lm_eval tests are set up. I reran using the e2e tests and
then made a new eval framework and ran those. I got generally opposite
trends depending on the setup.

Thus i think we're within the margin of error and can safely just relax
this test threshhold.

-------------

A) leave as is
- worse gsm8k
- better PPL
- accumulation with/without DDP are the same

- better gsm8k
- worse PPL
- accumulation would be different for DDP runs

as you can see the gsm8k evaluations are worse by 1-2% on llama though
they vary wildly for Qwen25. Similarly the PPL numbers are slightly
better. This is a very surprising result as we'd assume either

i) on average one technique to outperform another on multiple metrics
ii) they are at approximate parity  

I also ran gsm8k platinum evals on a more limited set of model/quant
settings which showed the same trend as normal gsm8k

I did additional tests to identify what was causing the error. After
relaxing the accumulation method to use the old accumulation method and
after changing the loss calculation to accumulate in the old Dtype. The
numbers are basicaly the same as the pre-DDP numbers.

Given that the new changes are mathematically more sound and they allow
alignment between DDP/nonDDP runs I think it makes the most sense to
just adjust this test.

Add MoE calibration wrapper for GLM-4.7-Flash (Glm4MoeLiteMoE) (#2547)

## Summary

GLM-4.7-Flash uses a separate MoE class (`Glm4MoeLiteMoE`) that is not
covered by the existing `Glm4MoeMoE` wrapper. Without this fix, MoE
calibration is **silently skipped** for GLM-4.7-Flash models, resulting
in quantization that doesn't properly calibrate expert weights.

## Problem

The model `zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash` (31B MoE) uses `Glm4MoeLiteMoE` with a
different architecture than `Glm4MoeMoE`:

- Has `shared_experts` attribute (not `shared_expert`)
- Uses `Glm4MoeLiteNaiveMoe` experts interface: `(hidden_states,
topk_indices, topk_weights)`
- Has group-based routing with `n_group`, `topk_group` parameters
- 64 routed experts + shared experts

When quantizing with NVFP4, the MoE calibration context manager checks
for registered wrappers but `Glm4MoeLiteMoE` doesn't match `Glm4MoeMoE`,
so calibration silently falls back to standard forward passes without
collecting expert activation statistics.

## Solution

Add `CalibrationGlm4MoeLiteMoE` wrapper class that:
- Registers for `Glm4MoeLiteMoE` class specifically
- Implements `route_tokens_to_experts()` for proper group-based routing
- Collects activation statistics for all 64 experts during calibration
- Provides proper `forward()` that routes through all experts

## Changes

- `src/llmcompressor/modeling/glm4_moe_lite.py` - New 119-line wrapper
- `src/llmcompressor/modeling/__init__.py` - Import the new wrapper

## Testing

Verified that quantization now shows:
```
Found 46 MoE modules to replace
Replaced 46 MoE modules for calibration
```

Instead of the previous behavior where no MoE modules were detected for
`Glm4MoeLiteMoE`.

## Hardware Tested

Add SmoothQuant layer mappings for Cohere, DeepSeek V3, and Phi3 (#2639)

Part of #1442

Follows the pattern from approved PR #2609 (which covers
`Qwen2MoeForCausalLM` / `Qwen3MoeForCausalLM`) and extends coverage to
other architectures that were either missing from `MAPPINGS_REGISTRY` or
incorrectly falling through to `DEFAULT_SMOOTHQUANT_MAPPINGS`.

## What

| Architecture | Mapping used | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `CohereForCausalLM` | `COHERE_SMOOTHQUANT_MAPPINGS` (new) | Parallel
transformer block: attention + MLP both read from `input_layernorm`, no
`post_attention_layernorm` exists |
| `Cohere2ForCausalLM` | `COHERE_SMOOTHQUANT_MAPPINGS` (new) | Same
parallel block structure |
| `Cohere2VisionForConditionalGeneration` |
`COHERE_SMOOTHQUANT_MAPPINGS` (new) | Language decoder follows the same
Cohere parallel block pattern |
| `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM` | `DEEPSEEK_V2_SMOOTHQUANT_MAPPINGS` |
Identical MLA attention (`q_a_proj`/`kv_a_proj_with_mqa`) to V2 —
currently falls through to DEFAULT which does not match MLA layer names
|
| `Phi3ForCausalLM` | `PHI3_VISION_SMOOTHQUANT_MAPPINGS` | Same fused
`qkv_proj` / `gate_up_proj` structure as Phi3V — currently falls through
to DEFAULT which does not match fused names |

## Design notes

**Cohere parallel transformer**: unlike standard transformer blocks,
Cohere models feed `input_layernorm` output simultaneously into
attention and MLP. Both sets of projections (`self_attn.q/k/v_proj` and
`mlp.gate_proj/up_proj`) are therefore included in a single `LayerMap`
balanced against `input_layernorm`. Verified against
[`modeling_cohere.py`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/cohere/modeling_cohere.py)
and
[`modeling_cohere2.py`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/cohere2/modeling_cohere2.py).

**DeepseekV3 / Phi3 reuse**: the architectures are structurally
identical to V2 and Phi3V respectively at the projection level, so the
existing constants apply without change.

`tests/llmcompressor/modifiers/transform/smoothquant/test_utils.py`
covering all new entries

[Tracing] Support Cohere Vision, Decouple vision tower from first layer (#1710)

## Purpose ##

[CommandA](https://huggingface.co/CohereLabs/command-a-vision-07-2025)
have very large vision towers. Until tensor parallelism is implemented
or tracing expands to support vision towers, we must onload the entire

[GPTQ] Support modifier-level ActivationOrdering for all weight strategies (#2670)

Fixes #2524

## Summary
This PR closes the remaining modifier-level gap for
`GPTQModifier(actorder=...)`. Before this PR,
`resolve_quantization_config` only propagated modifier-level actorder to
`strategy=GROUP` schemes, so the same setting was silently ignored for
any other strategy. This PR extends the whitelist to **GROUP,
TENSOR_GROUP, CHANNEL, TENSOR, and BLOCK**, with a `None` fallback (and
warning) for combinations CT rejects on reload.

## Background
- vllm-project/compressed-tensors#682 relaxed the `QuantizationArgs`
validator from `actorder is not None` to `actorder == GROUP` for
non-group strategies, so yaml-level configs like `weights: {strategy:
channel, actorder: weight}` already validate.
- #2616 generalized `quantize_weight`: `if actorder:` permutes for any
strategy, `g_idx` is built for `{GROUP, TENSOR_GROUP, BLOCK}`, and is
saved when `actorder == GROUP`.
- The remaining gap (this PR) is
`GPTQModifier.resolve_quantization_config`: it still only resolved
modifier-level actorder for `GROUP`, so the modifier-level path was
inconsistent with the kernel-level path.

## `actorder=GROUP` fallback
`actorder=GROUP` is only accepted by compressed-tensors on GROUP /
TENSOR_GROUP schemes (per CT #682). For CHANNEL / TENSOR / BLOCK,
`resolve_quantization_config` warns and resets to `None` so the artifact
stays loadable; `quantize_weight` mirrors the same guard for direct
callers.

## Scope summary
| strategy | modifier-level `actorder` (before) | (after this PR) |

|----------------|------------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| GROUP | propagated | propagated |
| TENSOR_GROUP | silently ignored | propagated |
| CHANNEL | silently ignored | propagated; `GROUP` → fallback |
| TENSOR | silently ignored | propagated; `GROUP` → fallback |
| BLOCK | silently ignored | propagated; `GROUP` → fallback |

[AWQ] Seed grid search with identity baseline + fail fast on non-finite loss (#2635)

## Summary

Fix two correctness bugs in the AWQ grid search that allowed
`_compute_best_scale` to either pick a worse-than-no-smoothing candidate
or to silently label a numerically broken layer as a clean identity
fallback.

### Bugs fixed

1. **Identity baseline mis-measured.** `initial_error` was the loss of
"the first surviving grid candidate", which under `duo_scaling=True` is
**not** identity. The recorded reduction therefore compared two smoothed
candidates against each other, and the grid loop was allowed to pick a
worse-than-no-smoothing scale set whenever the first candidate happened
to be worse than later ones.

2. **Non-finite loss silently labelled as identity fallback.** If the
identity baseline forward produced NaN/Inf, every grid candidate's `loss
< non_finite` was `False`, no candidate ever won, and the layer was
silently labelled `fell_back_to_identity=True`. The artifact then
shipped with poison metrics. The same outcome occurred if every executed
grid candidate produced a non-finite loss (e.g. fp16 overflow on heavy
outliers) while identity was finite.

### Implementation

- Extract per-candidate `apply scales → quantize → forward → MSE` into
`_eval_scales(scales, ..., update_fused)`. Call it once with `scales =
ones` to seed both `initial_error` and `best_error` from the real
identity baseline. The grid loop only keeps a candidate if it strictly
beats baseline; otherwise the layer stays at identity by construction.
- Track whether any candidate improved with an explicit
`grid_improved_over_identity` boolean instead of a float sentinel. Each
layer is recorded with a `fell_back_to_identity` flag in
`_error_metrics` so post-hoc inspection can flag layers that didn't
benefit from AWQ.
- Raise `RuntimeError` in two narrow correctness cases: identity
baseline non-finite, or identity finite but every grid candidate
non-finite. Layers genuinely stuck at identity (all candidate losses
finite, none beat baseline) are recorded for inspection, not raised on.
- Hoist the `update_fused` (TENSOR_GROUP strategy) check and the
host→device transfer of `orig_layer_weights` out of the per-candidate
hot path. Relevant when the model is offloaded.

### What this PR does NOT include

The Qwen3.5 `attn_output_gate` per-output-slice mapping fix is in
**#2636** (stacked on this PR).

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/llmcompressor/modifiers/awq/` — full AWQ suite
passes (38 tests)
- [x] New end-to-end regression tests in
`test_compute_best_scale_baseline.py` drive `_compute_best_scale`
through the real code path on a tiny W4A16 module:
  - `test_initial_error_equals_identity_loss`
  - `test_best_error_never_exceeds_initial_error`
- `test_compute_best_scale_raises_when_identity_baseline_is_non_finite`
-
`test_compute_best_scale_raises_when_all_grid_candidates_are_non_finite`
- [ ] Re-run Qwen3.5 27B AWQ calibration end-to-end (to be done on real
hardware)

Observers refactor (#2585)

# Background

problems this PR attempts to solve:

## Large Problems

1) observers always calculate qparams when they are run, even if you
need to do synchronization across ranks on an intermediate value
2) all the qparam calculation functionality was duplicated because we
had qparam calculation happen on run and again after synchronize
3) global scale was treated partially like a qparam and partially, not.
Each modifier handled global scale differently
4) there was a modifier dependent lifecycle for enabling/disabling
quantization. Quantization enabled during calibration for quantization
modifier but not for AWQ,GPTQ...etc


## Smaller Problems 

5) observers were complicated, they needed information from the module
(that wasn't passed in) to do their job so they needed to directly
access module attributes
6) MSE calculations used global scale even though numerically the global
scale could be ignored until later.
7) sync_activation_observers did both syncing and updating of qparams
8) imatrix observer wasn't set up to be synchronized in DDP. 
9) g_idx was treated as kind of like a qparam in several places but then
never actually used, i.e. there was functionality within observers to
handle this, but then in reality g_idx was set as identity when observer
was using it.
10) sequential pipeline was doing duplicated work in sequential epoch
end and calibration epoch end

# Summary

1,2) observers now have update_statistics_from_observed which runs on
forward and get_qparams, other functionality removed.
3) observers have references to observers of fused weights for
global_scale calculation so when they calculate qparams, global_scale
will be set correctly. global_scale logic is now entirely contained in
observers
4) quantization disabled across the board during calibration,
quantization now always happens at the end of the lifecycle
5) removed references to module from observers
6) removed references to global_scale from MSE calculations
7) removed observer functionality for g_idx (was never used)
8) cleaned up a lot of observer utils
9) consolidated synchronization logic, there is a notion of
activation_statistics that all activation observers and one weight
observer has that allows for synchronization
10) removed g_idx from observers, handled externally in GPTQ
11) all work done on sequential epoch end, added sequential epoch end to
basic and datafree pipelines eplicating a separation of concerns where
sequential epoch end does compression while calibration epoch end does
cleanup

clearing/restoring quantization metadata correctly in post-processing.
2. Update the Qwen3 MXFP8 example for
`Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507`.

**bug fix**

Although mlp.gate is listed in AutoRound predefined ignore layers and
reported as ignored in logs, it could still appear quantized after LLMC
post-processing.
Root cause was that LLMC restored legacy qparams/metadata even for
layers that AutoRound had already finalized as FP.
This fix skips qparam restoration for FP-finalized layers and clears
stale quantization metadata, so ignored MoE gate layers remain truly
unquantized end-to-end.

[Tracing] Support tracing cache (#2686)

## Purpose ##
* Support tracing `Cache` instances in fx graphs
* This is needed for models like
[DeepSeekV4](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/main/src/transformers/models/deepseek_v4/modeling_deepseek_v4.py#L1204-L1205)
which use kv cache instances, regardless of whether the user sets the
`use_cache` flag or not
* Prerequisite for #2647

## Background ##
```python3
class HFProxyableCacheMeta(type):
    """
    Metaclass that creates a class with its main methods wrapped to be proxyable.
    In the same way that objects can be replaced with `Proxy`s during trace-time,
    classes can also be replaced with `ProxyableClass`es during trace-time.
    This meta class acts as factory for creating `ProxyableClass`es of `Cache` classes.
    At trace-time, all references to `Cache` classes are monkeypatched with references
    to `ProxyableCache` classes. Whenever this class is used to construct a new instance
    of a `Cache`, an instance of `HFCacheProxy` is generated instead.
    """
```

## Changes ##
* Update how ProxyableClasses are monkeypatched at trace-time
* Previously, `HFTracer` would look at the defining module of the model
(usually `modeling_xxx.py` and monkeypatch the `Cache` imports there.
However, this doesn't work for autowrapped forwards
* Instead of monkeypatching the module dict, instead monkeypatch the
`forward.__globals__` dict. This patch is more direct and relevant, and
works for autowrapped forwards
* Rename `HFProxyableClassMeta` to `HFProxyableCacheMeta`, cause the
class to emit instances of `HFCacheProxy` when constructed during
tracing
* `HFCacheProxy` is a proxy for an instance of a `Cache` and can be
traced
* Fix minor typo in `HFProxyableClassMeta` implementation where fx graph
nodes for `method` and `function` were swapped

## Testing ##
* Added `test_dynamic_cache_produces_hf_cache_proxy_node` which tests
that cache construction and usage can be traced in the fx graph

[Bugfix] Fix coverage SQLite race in torchrun DDP tests (#2757)

## Summary
https://github.com/vllm-project/llm-compressor/pull/2726 was working as
intended to avoid the write time race condition but we now got a
coverage.combine race condition because the subprocesses would try to
call coverage.combine() during the pytest-cov teardown for both the DDP
processes. This happens due to the PYTEST_ADDOPTS --cov flag which gets
added to all subprocesses.

I believe this is intended to make sure each test subprocess
automatically has code coverage enabled and is then infecting the DDP
subprocesses which we don't want.

by using --no-cov in this torchrun subprocess invocation we avoid this
since this dominates the --cov flag.
note: coverage data is still collected for workers due to patch =
subprocess in .coveragerc which works with coverage.py to collect
coverage data, whereas --no-cov disables pytest-cov which normally calls
coverage.combine.

[Autowrapper] [Tracing] Unpin Gemma4, support tracing `UserDict` and `IfExp` (#2781)

## Purpose ##
* Support Gemma4 with the latest version of transformers
* Expand support for autowrapping model definitions which utilize
  * `UserDict`s
  * if expressions (`... if cond else ...`)

## Changes ##
* Support tracing objects which are instances of `UserDict`s
* This is achieved by converting them to normal `dict` instances at
capture time
* Support autowrapping models which use if expressions
* If expressions have the same implementation as if statements; both can
be wrapped
* Update Gemma4 examples to unpin to support latest transformers

<details><summary>Gemma 4 Debug Process</summary>

## Root Cause

Got it. So basically, AST sees an `if` statement that depends on a
dynamic variable `per_layer_inputs` , and therefore tries to wrap it

```python
if per_layer_inputs is None and self.config.get_text_config().hidden_size_per_layer_input:
		pad_embedding = self.language_model.embed_tokens.weight[self.config.text_config.pad_token_id, :]
		multimodal_mask = multimodal_mask.to(inputs_embeds.device)
		llm_inputs_embeds = torch.where(multimodal_mask[..., None], pad_embedding.view(1, 1, -1), inputs_embeds)
		per_layer_inputs = self.language_model.get_per_layer_inputs(llm_input_ids, llm_inputs_embeds)
```

```python
llm_inputs_embeds, multimodal_mask, pad_embedding, per_layer_inputs = wrapped_3(inputs_embeds, llm_input_ids, multimodal_mask, per_layer_inputs)
```

However, we’ve now replaced the concrete tracer input `per_layer_inputs`
, which would normally be concrete `None` with `Proxy(getitem_5)` .

The `fx.Tracer` then erroneously `per_layer_inputs` treats as real
populated variable. While it should have crashed for conditioning on
dynamic variables, it instead is bad and statically evaluates `is not
None` , and therefore puts `per_layer_inputs[:, :, i, :]` in the graph.

```python
per_layer_input = per_layer_inputs[:, :, i, :] if per_layer_inputs is not None else None
```

This is the “autowrapper hides things from torch.fx” situation I once
worried about. The autowrapper hides because it doesn’t (and cannot
reliably) know which inputs are static and which inputs are not, in the
same way that torch.fx can. Name matching is not robust.

## Solution

According to the autowrapper design philosophy, the autowrapper should
steal as much control as it can from torch.fx. If you continue with this
philosophy, it leads you to the natural question: Why didn’t the
autowrapper wrap the conditional slice operation?

```python
per_layer_input = per_layer_inputs[:, :, i, :] if per_layer_inputs is not None else None
```

The reason is because this expression is represented with `ast.IfExp`,
not `ast.If` ! If we add support for `visit_IfExp`, then the slice is
executed eagerly (ie not at all) and everything is groovy once more.

```
IfExp(
    test=Compare(
        left=Name(id='per_layer_inputs', ctx=Load()),
        ops=[
            IsNot()],
        comparators=[
            Constant(value=None)]),
    body=Subscript(
        value=Name(id='per_layer_inputs', ctx=Load()),
        slice=Tuple(
            elts=[
                Slice(),
                Slice(),
                Name(id='i', ctx=Load()), 
                Slice()],
            ctx=Load()),
        ctx=Load()),
    orelse=Constant(value=None))
```

```python
def visit_IfExp(self, node: ast.IfExp) -> ast.IfExp | ast.Call:
    """
    `if else` expressions are treated the same as `if` statements.

    :param node: `if else` expression which may be wrapped
    :return: if the `if else` expression cannot be statically evaluated, return the
        `if else` expression with the condition replaced by `True` or `False`.
        Otherwise, return a wrapper function call
    """
    return self.visit_If(node)
```

[Autowrapper] [Tracing] Unpin Gemma4, support tracing `UserDict` and `IfExp` (#2781)

## Purpose ##
* Support Gemma4 with the latest version of transformers
* Expand support for autowrapping model definitions which utilize
  * `UserDict`s
  * if expressions (`... if cond else ...`)

## Changes ##
* Support tracing objects which are instances of `UserDict`s
* This is achieved by converting them to normal `dict` instances at
capture time
* Support autowrapping models which use if expressions
* If expressions have the same implementation as if statements; both can
be wrapped
* Update Gemma4 examples to unpin to support latest transformers

<details><summary>Gemma 4 Debug Process</summary>

## Root Cause

Got it. So basically, AST sees an `if` statement that depends on a
dynamic variable `per_layer_inputs` , and therefore tries to wrap it

```python
if per_layer_inputs is None and self.config.get_text_config().hidden_size_per_layer_input:
		pad_embedding = self.language_model.embed_tokens.weight[self.config.text_config.pad_token_id, :]
		multimodal_mask = multimodal_mask.to(inputs_embeds.device)
		llm_inputs_embeds = torch.where(multimodal_mask[..., None], pad_embedding.view(1, 1, -1), inputs_embeds)
		per_layer_inputs = self.language_model.get_per_layer_inputs(llm_input_ids, llm_inputs_embeds)
```

```python
llm_inputs_embeds, multimodal_mask, pad_embedding, per_layer_inputs = wrapped_3(inputs_embeds, llm_input_ids, multimodal_mask, per_layer_inputs)
```

However, we’ve now replaced the concrete tracer input `per_layer_inputs`
, which would normally be concrete `None` with `Proxy(getitem_5)` .

The `fx.Tracer` then erroneously `per_layer_inputs` treats as real
populated variable. While it should have crashed for conditioning on
dynamic variables, it instead is bad and statically evaluates `is not
None` , and therefore puts `per_layer_inputs[:, :, i, :]` in the graph.

```python
per_layer_input = per_layer_inputs[:, :, i, :] if per_layer_inputs is not None else None
```

This is the “autowrapper hides things from torch.fx” situation I once
worried about. The autowrapper hides because it doesn’t (and cannot
reliably) know which inputs are static and which inputs are not, in the
same way that torch.fx can. Name matching is not robust.

## Solution

According to the autowrapper design philosophy, the autowrapper should
steal as much control as it can from torch.fx. If you continue with this
philosophy, it leads you to the natural question: Why didn’t the
autowrapper wrap the conditional slice operation?

```python
per_layer_input = per_layer_inputs[:, :, i, :] if per_layer_inputs is not None else None
```

The reason is because this expression is represented with `ast.IfExp`,
not `ast.If` ! If we add support for `visit_IfExp`, then the slice is
executed eagerly (ie not at all) and everything is groovy once more.

```
IfExp(
    test=Compare(
        left=Name(id='per_layer_inputs', ctx=Load()),
        ops=[
            IsNot()],
        comparators=[
            Constant(value=None)]),
    body=Subscript(
        value=Name(id='per_layer_inputs', ctx=Load()),
        slice=Tuple(
            elts=[
                Slice(),
                Slice(),
                Name(id='i', ctx=Load()), 
                Slice()],
            ctx=Load()),
        ctx=Load()),
    orelse=Constant(value=None))
```

```python
def visit_IfExp(self, node: ast.IfExp) -> ast.IfExp | ast.Call:
    """
    `if else` expressions are treated the same as `if` statements.

    :param node: `if else` expression which may be wrapped
    :return: if the `if else` expression cannot be statically evaluated, return the
        `if else` expression with the condition replaced by `True` or `False`.
        Otherwise, return a wrapper function call
    """
    return self.visit_If(node)
```

</details>

Transformers v5 (#2647) # Transformers v5 # * Resolves #2159 ## Examples and Model Loading ## * `dtype` now defaults to `"auto"`, so we can remove this explicit argument to reduce confusion * `from_pretrained` no longer supports `use_auth_token` * Model structures differ between v4 and v5. This means that our example regexes need to be updated. This was done manually and with assistance from [AI-generated tests](https://github.com/vllm-project/llm-compressor/pull/new/kylesayrs/example_regex_tests) ## Tied Embeddings ## * Transformers now has a slightly different policy for handling checkpoints with tied embeddings, but where the values differ in the checkpoint. Previously, transformers would throw away the lm_head. Now, this conflict is detected, and the embeddings are untied. In practice, these models are essentially malformed, but `nm-testing/tinysmokellama-3.2` is one such malformed model and we need to update our tests to use different models/ account for this change in behavior. ## MoE ## There are two default pathways to adding MoE support for quantization, both of which are specified in `linearize.py`. I've pulled out the MoE linearization logic from `moe_calibration_context` into dedicated methods `load_quantizable_moe`, and `linearize_moe`. This allow us to do the super-fast load pathway, and also means that we can toggle the calibrate_experts flag without necessarily having to unfold the model for saving. ### `load_quantizable_moe` ### This context allows users to load moe models with efficient linearization and integration with the `calibrate_all_experts` flag. 1. In the best case, the model architecture has a pre-baked conversion mapping, which allows the model to be converted into 2d linearization as it's loaded. This case is the best for load runtime. ```python3 experts_cls, forward_mapping, backward_mapping = _get_2d_mappings(model_type) linear_experts_2d_cls = LinearExperts2D.create_linear_experts_cls(experts_cls) register_patch_mapping({experts_cls.__name__: linear_experts_2d_cls}) register_checkpoint_conversion_mapping( model_type, forward_mapping, overwrite=True ) ``` 2. In the fallback case, the model is loaded into the standard transformers v5 `Experts` form, then converted to a linearization. This is often inefficient, as models are sometimes undergo 2d -> 3d -> 2d, but is guaranteed to work for all transformers-v5-compliant model definitions. ```python3 linear_experts_cls = LinearExperts2D.create_linear_experts_cls(original_experts_cls) for name, module in non_linearized_moes.items(): linear_moe = linear_experts_cls.from_experts_module(module, model.config) model.set_submodule(name, linear_moe) ``` 3. In the final case, if a model does not have the standard transformers v5 `Experts` form, then we must write a custom replacement. This involves registering a new subclass of `LinearExperts2D`. ```python3 class GraniteMoeLinearExperts(LinearExperts2D): def from_experts_module(...): ... def __init__(...): ... def forward(...): ... ``` ## Adjust LM Eval Thresholds ## This PR makes two adjustments to lm_eval test thresholds 1. `w4a16_awq_sym: flexible-extract` (`0.91 -> 0.90`): The base model's score increased, while the compressed model's score stayed the same 2. `w4a16_actorder_group`: strict-match` (`0.95 -> 0.94`): All scores for this config decreased by ~0.025 points, the strict match happened to just go under the threshold. From the charts below, you can see that there are minimal changes in lm-eval scores before and after v5 upgrade, any there is no evidence of a correlated trend downwards.
Δ scores
Δ recovery
## Follow Ups ## * Implement a load context like `load_compat` to simplify UX for loading models * Add documentation and tutorials for supporting MoE linearization for new models ## Thoughts on Future Model Support ## * A high priority for LLM Compressor moving forward should be to improve zero day support by supporting model definitions which are not Transformers compliant. This means * Supporting hooks/templates for MoE linearization * Reducing reliance on the `PreTrainedModel` definition, potentially allowing users to pass a config template * Adding guides for all of the above ## Testing ## * Integration, E2E, lm_eval: [passing](https://github.com/neuralmagic/llm-compressor-testing/actions/runs/26935762392); Examples: [passing](https://github.com/neuralmagic/llm-compressor-testing/actions/runs/26959652272) * Added tests which replace the previously individual MoE replacement tests * Added tests for MoE replacement's compatibility with offloading and distributed offloading * Ran AI-generated tests for testing that regexes still match after v5 upgrade https://github.com/vllm-project/llm-compressor/pull/new/kylesayrs/example_regex_tests --------- Signed-off-by: Kyle Sayers

Add `load_context` unified context manager (#2811)

## Summary
This PR introduces a new unified context manager `load_context` that
combines both `load_offloaded_model` and `load_quantizable_moe`
contexts, simplifying model loading code across the codebase.

## Changes

### Core Implementation
- **Add `load_context()` in `src/llmcompressor/utils/dev.py`**
- Uses `ExitStack` to combine `load_offloaded_model` and
`load_quantizable_moe`
  - Passes `model_cls` parameter to both underlying contexts
  - Added to `__all__` exports for public API

### Bug Fix
- **Remove unnecessary warning in `linearize_moe()`**
  - No longer warns when model is not an MoE model
  - Silently returns if no experts found to linearize

### Examples Migration
- **Update 29 example files to use `load_context`**
  - Replace standalone `load_quantizable_moe()` usage (20 files)
  - Replace standalone `load_offloaded_model()` usage (9 files)
- Replace combined `load_offloaded_model(), load_quantizable_moe()`
usage
  - Remove redundant imports
  - **All examples now use the unified context manager**

## Benefits
- **Simplified API**: Single context manager for both offloading and MoE
linearization
- **Reduced boilerplate**: Less code needed in examples and user scripts
- **Consistent pattern**: Unified approach across all examples
- **Better defaults**: Both contexts are always applied, reducing
potential for errors

## Example Usage

**Before:**
```python
from compressed_tensors.offload import load_offloaded_model
from llmcompressor.modeling.moe.linearize import load_quantizable_moe

with load_offloaded_model(), load_quantizable_moe():
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID)
```

**After:**
```python
from llmcompressor.utils.dev import load_context

with load_context():
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(MODEL_ID)
```

Add AWQ Mappings for Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLM (#2768)

Fixes #2696

## Summary:
Adds AWQ smoothing mappings for `Glm4MoeLiteForCausalLM` (GLM-4.7-Flash
model).

## Architecture Notes
GLM-4.7-Flash:
- **MLA attention** (`q_a_proj`, `kv_a_proj_with_mqa`, `q_b_proj`,
`kv_b_proj`) instead of standard `q/k/v_proj`
- **Mixed dense/MoE FFN**: `first_k_dense_replace=1` means layer 0 is a
standard dense FFN; layers 1–46 are MoE with 64 routed experts + 1
shared expert

## Key Design Decision
`mlp.gate` (the MoE router) is intentionally excluded from balance
layers. Including it causes `match_modules_set` to never complete a
group for the dense layer 0 (which has no router), accumulating all
`post_attention_layernorm` entries across all 47 layers into a single
group.

## Testing
Quantized `zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash` with AWQ + W4A16 successfully.
Verified inference via vLLM produces coherent outputs.

## v0.1.109 — traversal-state convergence

### Direct 收敛后不再有遍历扫描
- Direct 成为唯一收敛状态：所有 punch/probe/peer-reflexive/fresh-mapping prediction/reverse check/validation enqueue 在源头与发送中途双重检查 Direct，promotion 后一个 probe 内停止。
- 删除 Direct 期间的 speculative-alternates 探测策略：Direct peer 的 synchronized punch targets 无条件为空，消除了 Mini-Air 观测到的 264-probe post-Direct 扫描。
- 同步 punch task 在 spawn、fresh-mapping 测量后、candidate sweep 前、每次 advertisement HTTP 前重查 Direct；probe-loop 重试在 Direct 确认后中止。
- peer-reflexive signal loop/worker 在 relayed HTTP signal 与 fast punch 前重查 Direct；ingress、validation enqueue、triggered reverse check 在源头对 Direct peer 抑制。
- Active-pool / remote-scatter / stable-unique-scatter punch 共享 per-probe Direct gate（is_direct_sync 镜像，接收路径无新锁序）；fresh-mapping punch generation 中途中止。
- candidate publication 对健康确认 Direct peer 推迟 relay-assisted punch，health failure 或 generation change 后重新打开。

### 恢复能力保持不变（已测试）
- relay fallback（Direct health failure）、generation advance/reclaim window、single-flight validation registry、newest-wins endpoint 更新、owner-bound expectation 清理。

### 测试与验证
- 10 个新测试（post-Direct punch/ACK/peer-reflexive 流量、Direct peer 的 scheduled hole punch skip、Direct probe-target 为空、LAN candidate 延迟至 health failure）。
- cargo test --workspace、clippy -D warnings、Go test/vet/fmt、nat-sim 5/5、Mini-Air 5/5 双端 Direct ≤10s（最终 SHA 3a8b5b7e，4.7-9.5s/round）。
- Mini-Air harness：远程 control/relay 模式（测试拓扑对齐产品公网路径）、link health gate、Air 二进制原子上传、B-liveness 等待、10s PASS 预算。

Release v0.1.109: traversal-state convergence gates and post-Direct scan elimination

- Direct is the single converged state: every punch, probe, peer-reflexive
  signal, fresh-mapping prediction, reverse check and validation enqueue is
  gated at the source and re-checked mid-send, so a session scheduled before
  promotion stops within one probe once the peer turns Direct.
- Removed the speculative-alternates probe strategy while Direct
  (should_probe_private_alternates_while_direct and its only consumers):
  synchronized punch targets are now unconditionally empty for a Direct peer,
  which eliminates the 264-probe post-Direct sweep observed in Mini-Air.
- Synchronized hole-punch tasks re-check Direct at spawn, after fresh-mapping
  measurement, before the candidate sweep and before each advertisement
  HTTP request; probe-loop retries abort once Direct is confirmed.
- Peer-reflexive signal loop and worker re-check Direct before the relayed
  HTTP signal and the fast punch; ingress, validation enqueue and triggered
  reverse checks are suppressed at the source for Direct peers.
- Active-pool, remote-scatter and stable-unique-scatter punch sessions share a
  per-probe Direct gate (is_direct_sync mirror, no new lock ordering on
  receive paths); fresh-mapping punch generations abort mid-sweep.
- Candidate publication defers relay-assisted punch for healthy confirmed
  Direct peers and re-opens on health failure or generation change.
- Recovery is unchanged and tested: relay fallback on Direct health failure,
  generation advance/reclaim window, single-flight validation registry,
  newest-wins endpoint updates and owner-bound expectation cleanup.
- Tests: 10 new tests covering post-Direct punch/ACK/peer-reflexive traffic,
  scheduled-hole-punch skip with live candidates, Direct probe-target
  emptiness with public candidates, and LAN-candidate deferral until health
  failure; all daemon suites plus the pre-existing control/flaky windows pass.
- Mini-Air harness: remote control/relay mode (test topology now matches the
  production public-path topology instead of Tailscale DERP), link health
  gate scripts, atomic Air binary upload, B-liveness wait and a 10s PASS
  budget; 5/5 rounds both Direct at 4.7-9.5s with the final release SHA.
- Version bumped to 0.1.109 across Cargo workspace, Cargo.lock, pubspec,
  Tauri config, package.json and tray metadata.

客户端直连 api.github.com 拉取组件版本列表会撞匿名 60/h 限流（403）
且大陆网络不稳定。新增 /api/components/{ffmpeg,ytdlp} 转发 GitHub
Release API，服务端可选持 token 提升配额，缓存按 token 分档（有则
12h、无则 24h）禁止过频回源，边缘 s-maxage 与内存 TTL 同步。

顺带引入 @astrojs/check + typescript 5.x（7.0 preview 不提供 astro
check 依赖的编程 API，需锁定），并把 build 前置类型检查；修复由此暴露
的 sitemap changefreq 字面量类型错误。

docs(plugins): 补充 variants/helperScript manifest 字段文档

同步 openapi.json 的 helperLabel schema，及中英文 API 参考/manifest
文档的 variants（多画质/格式选择）、defaultVariantIndex、helperScript/
helperLabel（复制辅助脚本按钮）字段说明。

feat(plugin): 新增 resolve 变体选择与设置项辅助脚本

插件 resolver 可返回多个变体（画质/格式），宿主经新增的
HostSelection::select_resolve_variant 让用户选择，超时/免打扰/headless
回退到插件指定的 default_index；变体在 resolve worker 内收敛后回流 actor，
空变体保持单一直链旧语义、零破坏。桌面/web/移动端各接入变体选择对话框。

设置项新增可选 helperScript：非空时字段旁渲染复制按钮，把脚本文本
复制到剪贴板供用户在浏览器 Console 执行（典型用途：提取 cookie）。
宿主绝不执行脚本，仅复制；仅 string 字段有效，长度上限 4KB。

fix(ui): 补齐 Windows 自定义标题栏顶部系统边线

自定义 titlebar 去掉 WS_CAPTION 后 DWM 不再绘制顶部 1px 边线，仅 Windows 补齐；macOS/Linux 保持原生边框行为不变。

fix(synology): 修复导航窗格无图标与目录读取失败

群晖套件版两处问题（issue #80）：

- 打包补充 ui/config 应用入口（.url 类型）与 grid_* 图标，
  并在 INFO 声明 dsm_ui_dir="ui"，使主菜单/导航窗格显示图标、
  可拖到桌面。
- fs_list 浏览到授权目录外时 EACCES 不再整体失败（避免选择器卡
  在「目录读取失败」无法后退），改为返回空子目录 + 可用 parent，
  让用户仍能沿上级继续导航。

Closes #80

chore(website): 调整落地页组件、文案与 i18n

- Features/Extension 区块组件重构
- 赞助墙允许匿名（名称/留言可空，服务端用兜底文案）
- 文档术语「牢笼」统一为「沙箱」
- 移除页脚 logo 投票入口，更新 en/ja/zh-CN 文案

docs(website): 新增 FFmpeg 组件安装说明文档

补充浏览器扩展使用文档,说明 DASH/HLS 流分离音视频轨道时需安装 FFmpeg 才能合并输出,中英双语同步。

feat(engine): 支持修改已存在任务的线程数

活跃任务自动暂停→改配置→恢复以立即生效，已下进度完整保留（复用现有分段布局续传，恢复期间零全量 GET）。已完成任务拒绝修改。新增详情面板/右键菜单编辑入口与 TaskSegmentsUpdated 信号。

feat(plugins): yt-dlp 示例插件泛化为多平台通用解析

从 YouTube 专用（fluxdown@youtube）改为 fluxdown@ytdlp，白名单收口至 YouTube/Bilibili/Niconico/Twitch/Vimeo/Dailymotion/SoundCloud/AcFun。新增按平台隔离的 Cookie 设置项与自续期存储、播放列表条目选择、附加 yt-dlp 参数、cookie 域按 URL 自动推导；移除固定画质设置改为下载时弹框选择。

fix(windows): 修复 Win11 顶部标题栏边线消失

还原顶部非客户区时保留 1px（不再按 Win11/Win10 区分），让 DWM 在无标题栏窗口下画出全宽顶边线；Dart 侧移除逐 widget 模拟（仅覆盖 HeaderBar 中段的临时方案）。

feat(website): 赞助者名单新增精选榜并改按时间排序

按金额取前 3 名单列「特别感谢」卡片区；其余最新赞助改回单纯按时间降序展示，不再按金额排序。

refactor(controller): 移除修改线程数需先暂停的限制

引擎已支持对活跃任务自动暂停→改→恢复，清理过时提示文案与文档注释。

## 📦 下载预编译二进制

| 平台 | 资产 |
|---|---|
| Windows x64 / ARM64 | `FluxDown-CLI-0.2.1-windows-{x64,arm64}.zip` |
| macOS Intel / Apple Silicon | `FluxDown-CLI-0.2.1-macos-{x64,arm64}.tar.gz` |
| Linux x64 / ARM64（musl 静态链接，任意发行版可用） | `FluxDown-CLI-0.2.1-linux-{x64,arm64}.tar.gz` |

解压后得到 `fluxdown`（Windows 为 `fluxdown.exe`），放入 PATH 即可使用。文件校验见 `SHA256SUMS.txt`。

## 🛠️ 从源码安装

```bash
cargo install --git https://github.com/zerx-lab/FluxDown fluxdown_cli
```

## 🚀 快速开始

```bash
fluxdown ping                         # 探活（需 FluxDown App / server 运行中）
fluxdown add https://example.com/f.zip
fluxdown ls
```

服务地址经 `--url` 或 `FLUXDOWN_URL`（默认 `http://127.0.0.1:17800`），
管理 token 经 `--token` 或 `FLUXDOWN_TOKEN`。

fix(engine): 消除 Windows 拉起控制台子进程时的黑窗闪现

ffmpeg/ffprobe/yt-dlp/tar 及版本探测子进程未设 CREATE_NO_WINDOW，每次拉起都会闪现黑色控制台窗口，设置「组件」页做版本探测时尤为高频。新增 proc::no_console_window 统一处理，所有控制台子进程调用点必经此函数。

feat(updater): 新增更新渠道与预发布版本支持

新增「稳定/前沿」更新渠道设置：前沿渠道纳入 vX.Y.Z-rc.N 预发布版。updater 语义版本比较升级为完整 SemVer 2.0 优先级（含 prerelease 标识符排序），/api/release 按 channel 参数返回对应版本线。release 工作流对含 - 的 tag 标记 prerelease、不抢占 latest、不打包扩展，build-name 取剥离 prerelease 后缀的 CLEAN_VERSION。

update .omp

feat(update): 内置更新失败时支持改用下载任务下载

更新器自身的下载/获取失败后，暴露「改用下载任务下载」按钮，将安装包 URL 交给下载列表处理，避免用户无法获取更新。

casos.name: FluxDown Mobile v0.3.0
casos.body:
<!-- fluxdown:lang:zh -->
## [0.3.0] - 2026-07-31

### 🚀 新功能
- 新增「文件已存在时」设置：重名时可选择保留旧文件并给新文件改名（默认），或直接覆盖旧文件
- BT 任务暂停后恢复明显更快：不再重建下载会话，跳过重复校验和节点冷启动等待
- BT 种子初次校验阶段的任务列表现在会显示实际校验百分比，不再只显示「准备中」
- 自动代理更聪明：多次验证稳定的代理线路会被记住并跨重启保留，下次直接使用，无需重新试探

### 🐛 问题修复
- 修复下载在自动降级为单线程续传时会清空已下载进度、导致从头重新下载的问题
- 修复部分服务器返回非标准 Content-Encoding: none 时下载被永久判定失败、无法自动重试的问题
- 修复新建任务偶发因队列归属信息未及时同步而在任务列表中短暂不可见的问题

<!-- fluxdown:lang:en -->
## [0.3.0] - 2026-07-31

### 🚀 Features
- Added a "When file exists" setting: on a name collision, keep the old file and rename the new one (default), or overwrite the old file directly
- BT torrents resume noticeably faster after being paused — resuming no longer rebuilds the download session, skipping the repeated hash check and cold peer startup
- The task list now shows the actual verification percentage during a torrent's initial check, instead of just "Preparing"
- Smarter auto-proxy: routes proven reliable over repeated checks are now remembered across app restarts and reused immediately, instead of being re-tested from scratch

### 🐛 Bug Fixes
- Fixed downloads that fell back to a single connection on resume wiping out already-downloaded progress and restarting from byte 0
- Fixed downloads being permanently rejected with no automatic retry when a server sent the non-standard "Content-Encoding: none" header
- Fixed newly created tasks occasionally not appearing in the task list due to a delay in syncing queue assignment

casos.name: FluxDown Mobile v0.3.1
casos.body:
<!-- fluxdown:lang:zh -->
## [0.3.1] - 2026-08-01

### 🐛 问题修复
- 修复 SOCKS5 代理下 DNS 可能在本地解析导致代理形同虚设的问题：现在域名解析统一交给代理侧完成，网络环境存在 DNS 污染/劫持时也能正常连通
- 自定义代理地址新增对 `socks4a://` 的显式支持；填写不支持的协议前缀时会明确报错，不再被静默当作 HTTP 代理处理
- 修复多进程同时写入日志文件时可能互相覆盖内容的问题，日志导出与排查问题时不再丢失记录

<!-- fluxdown:lang:en -->
## [0.3.1] - 2026-08-01

### 🐛 Bug Fixes
- Fixed SOCKS5 proxy connections that could still leak DNS lookups to local resolution, making the proxy ineffective — hostname resolution now always happens on the proxy side, so connections work correctly even when local DNS is censored or hijacked
- Added explicit support for `socks4a://` in custom proxy addresses; unsupported proxy scheme prefixes now surface a clear error instead of silently falling back to HTTP
- Fixed a log file corruption issue where concurrent writes could overwrite each other's content, so exported logs no longer lose entries
